"You're really lucky."
Luina was quietly listening to their conversation when she was brought back from her calm by Bella's question.
"Luina, how was it for you?"
"...What?"
"Your three days with Gerhard. Honestly, since I didn't see you fight directly, I'm so curious about how it was."
Next to her, Aina exclaimed, "Me too!"
"There wasn't anything special."
"Nothing special, yet you got first place?"
"Right, and you defeated Carlo and Allia's pair?"
"Hmm."
What was Gerhard like? Luina pondered for a moment.
It wouldn't be an exaggeration to say they won thanks to his contribution.
The problem was that it was thanks to artifacts, which she thought was a bit cowardly, and Gerhard didn't want that fact to be revealed.
"We just worked well together."
"That's it?"
"I don't really have anything else to..."
There was a moment of silence after the ambiguous answer.
"But Luina."
Then Bella broke the silence.
"It really wasn't because of money, right?"
"I already said it wasn't. Why are you asking again?"
"No, that's not what I meant..."
Her gaze moved to Luina's body.
"Your armor seems to have changed..."
"Come to think of it, your weapon too..."
Gulp, Luina suppressed the tea that was about to spurt out, using even her aura. Her throat and nose stung, but she managed her expression as best she could.
"...I changed them with scholarship money. My father insisted that I shouldn't send money this time since he had some to spare. And my weapon and armor were a bit worn out."
"Really?"
"Good job, Luina. Your equipment was a bit, no, very worn out. I even wanted to replace it for you!"
Fortunately, they seemed to have accepted it.
'I'm glad I thought about this in advance.'
Luina secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
It was a secret that she had been thinking of excuses every day, not wanting to reveal that she was receiving sponsorship from Gerhard.
***
"Good work, sir."
As he left the classroom, a servant was waiting for Gerhard. He threw himself onto the bed inside the carriage with familiarity.
"...I feel like I'm going to die."
"I heard you got first place."
"Yes. I bought first place with money."
Puhehe, Gerhard chuckled dryly.
"This is why I like money."
"Did you use everything you took?"
"Fortunately, not to that extent."
Of course, it was just not everything; the amount consumed was by no means small.
"But at least I earned something back too, so that's a relief."
Gerhard took out five glass bottles filled with troll blood and handed them over.
"Troll blood."
"I didn't have the situation to collect everything, so I only took the most efficient things."
"You did well. By the way, how was Luina Berchef?"
"More cooperative than I expected."
Not bad for something forcibly bought with money.
She did resist his words occasionally, but she didn't particularly refuse if it was a reasonable choice.
Her skill was naturally beyond question. She wasn't second-ranked for nothing. Whether she would truly become a Royal Knight, he still didn't know.
"I'm tired."
There had truly been many events.
From the first place in the exercise to the suddenly emerged futures. He was exhausted both physically and mentally.
"Take a nap. I'll wake you when we arrive at Lavidus Hall."
"Please do. Oh, by the way, were there any unusual occurrences while I was gone?"
"Nothing within the Academy."
That implied there was something outside the Academy.
"What?"
"A letter arrived."
"A letter?"
The servant handed over the letter. The elegantly embossed golden turtle seal was distinct enough to immediately know who it was from.
"Father?"
"Yes. A letter from the Duke."
Gerhard tore the envelope and unfolded the letter.
On the snow-white paper.
As if emphasizing the beauty of whitespace, there was only a single sentence written:
[I accept your audacious deal.]
But it was intensely what Gerhard had been hoping for.
"...Good."
"Did your intimidation succeed?"
"It's the pufferfish strategy."
The corners of Gerhard's mouth turned upward.
Though an ominous future had newly emerged, everything was going smoothly.
For now.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Behind the Glory [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 18: Behind the Glory [1]
[An unexpected upset in the collaborative class between second-year Knight Department and Magic Department. Breaking everyone's expectations, first place was claimed by Luina Berchef, the second-ranked student of the Knight Department, and Gerhard Goldenheim, ranked 10th in the Magic Department.]
[Gerhard Goldenheim, who defeated the Carlo Deneb and Allia Torta pair and imprisoned ten students for about 5 minutes. Was he hiding his power?]
[How did Luina Berchef and Gerhard Goldenheim become a pair?]
The joint class between the Knight Department and Magic Department became a major issue for not just the second-year students but the entire Academy.
Aint checked the daily newspaper and exclaimed in admiration.
"As expected of the Goldenheims. And the Berchefs, though they've lost their rights to the Golden Decree, are still Berchefs."
"Hmm, that upstart has achieved quite a good result."
"No, is it because of the Berchef bloodline?"
"The status of those upstarts rising while House Berchef falls close to ruin. The world is truly in decline."
The Ego residing in the sword, Gardner Alpenfassen, clicked his tongue as if displeased.
"You seem to dislike the Goldenheims but like the Berchefs?"
"Don't compare those two families. The head of the Berchef family was the only knight who could stand alongside the former emperor and me on the battlefield."
"I miss those days when we scoured the battlefield together and took the heads of those demon bastards."
Gardner's voice, which had been immersed in nostalgia, hardened again.
"In contrast, those Goldenheim bastards...!"
"Never compare them again. It's disrespectful to the Berchefs."
"But now the Goldenheims are more respected. The Berchefs have also incurred a massive debt to the Goldenheims."
"That's why the world is in decline."
"A hero's family is trampled to the ground while the status of those wretched upstarts soars to the sky."
"If I didn't need the military funds, I would have struck them down with my own hands... Wait a minute."
The sword where Gardner resided trembled.
"That's it."
"Huh? What do you mean by 'that's it' all of a sudden?"
"Didn't that Gerhard or Berhard fellow say that? To come find him anytime if you need something."
"...Senior Gerhard never said such a thing."
He did deliberately seek him out, but he only engaged in meaningless chitchat.
"Didn't I tell you? It might not have been direct, but showing goodwill and deliberately seeking conversation is their method."
"Your equipment isn't very good anyway, so go ask him for some money."
"...What?"
"Why are you surprised?"
"You also agreed that you should make those fellows your patrons."
"But isn't it too sudden to do that now?"
"Sudden? On the contrary, that's probably what he's hoping for."
"I guarantee you. He'll probably give you the money as if he's been waiting for this."
Gardner grinned confidently.
"Of course, they'll try to collect it back with interest later, but who cares? When the demons become active, they'll have no choice but to cling to your pant leg."
"...Demons."
At that point, Aint's face hardened.
"...Honestly, it's still hard to believe. Are the demons really becoming active again?"
"Yes."
Gardner affirmed.
"The reason the former emperor made me an Ego of the sword was to prepare for the demons' activity, which he foresaw."
"The fact that I've awakened means that the future is flowing as predicted."
"...Hmm."
"Don't worry. You will definitely defeat the demons and save the world."
"I will make it so."
"...Yes."
"So for now, go to that upstart and extract some equipment."
"As a hero who will save the world, he should naturally provide at least that much."
His voice, which had been solemn until just now, turned frivolous again.
Aint was a bit confused about which was Gardner's true nature.
"...But won't he be wary of Schwaben?"
"That's all the more reason to do it."
"Aren't you curious why he deliberately approached you despite Schwaben?"
"If my prediction is correct, he will definitely help you. Of course, if you go openly, he won't because of those watching around him."
Gardner spoke with conviction.
And that conviction...
"...I'm sorry, but Young Master Gerhard said he has no reason to meet you."
"...What?"
...was shattered as he was turned away at the door by the clerk of the store where they had held their secret meeting.
***
The perception had changed.
From the beginning, Gerhard Goldenheim had attracted people's attention since his admission.
But that was quite different from the attention he was receiving now.
The prestige of the Goldenheim family and the expectations that came with it.
There were no direct expectations or cheers for Gerhard himself.
Even if he ranked 10th, it was considered natural because he was a Goldenheim. Rather, he was evaluated as not particularly talented because he only ranked 10th.
That was completely flipped in an instant.
Although it was thanks to forming a pair with Luina, and he had only placed first once, it was completely different from before.
"You must be pleased."
"It's just a flame that will soon be extinguished."
They might treat him like an amazing talent now, but they would quickly cool down as if it never happened. If his grades turned bad even once, it would happen even faster.
Therefore, Gerhard didn't particularly respond to the cheers of others.
That wasn't what was important.
"Didn't you say this was your first time getting first place and that you were happy?"
"I thought so, but now I don't particularly feel that way."
Luina shook her head.
"Even though you've finally beaten Almon?"
"It's just a simple exercise, not a midterm or final exam, isn't it?"
"It's the exercise that gives the most bonus points after those two. Grad might not, but Professor Rosalia doesn't lie."
This time, she nodded slightly. But her determined gaze didn't change.
"It's only been once so far. They were just caught off guard by your unexpected blow, and we don't know what will happen from now on. We need to work harder and continue our victories."
"You always speak so stiffly and formulaically."
"I'm just talking about the fundamentals."
She took a sip of tea and changed the subject.
"So why did you call me this time?"
"The Academy gives scholarships as rewards for good grades."
"...You mean you're going to give me something because we got first place?"
You? Luina's face distorted slightly.
"Well, I am your sponsor after all."
"I don't need it."
"But you do. And giving is my choice."
"I almost raised suspicion from my friends after receiving the equipment. A second time..."
"Take it."
Gerhard didn't properly listen to Luina's objection and took out a small box.
"What is this...?"
"You still haven't eaten the mandrake."
"I haven't finished my preparations yet."

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Behind the Glory [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 19: Behind the Glory [2]
Mandrake root, with its vast mana content, wasn't the kind of elixir one could consume hastily.
"Yes, my mistake. I naturally thought that level of preparation would be easy, but I was thinking too much from my own standard."
The Goldenheims were prepared for whatever they wanted to do. But the Berchefs, who had declined and were barely rebuilding, couldn't do the same.
"..."
Having her embarrassing weakness exposed, Luina shut her mouth and glared at Gerhard.
"I didn't mean to insult you. If you feel offended, I apologize."
"Your expression doesn't suggest that at all."
"What's important is that I said it verbally."
Click, Gerhard opened the box. Inside were five reagents.
"What are those?"
"Reagents for the mana control magic circle, reagents to strengthen the mana roads, reagents to strengthen mental power, reagents to increase the efficiency of mandrake, and reagents to neutralize the poison of mandrake."
It was a set of supplements for smoothly consuming mandrake.
"Naturally, they're all top-grade items with prices to match. So, don't you need them?"
"...I do need them."
Gerhard grinned. Luina murmured in a voice as small as a mosquito's.
"...I will definitely repay this debt."
"There's no need for that. Doesn't a sponsor provide support without expecting anything in return?"
"I understand that usually, they do expect something."
That was true. After all, sponsoring a talent is ultimately because you want that talent to work for you.
"And do you think I would believe that you're spending a huge amount of money without expecting anything in return?"
"So you won't accept it?"
"...Thank you. Someday, I will definitely..."
After sending Luina off, Gerhard returned to Lavidus Hall.
It wasn't bad that the relationship seemed to be improving better than expected.
"I've properly fastened the first button. Now I need to move on to the next."
"You've already fastened all the buttons on your clothes, though?"
The servant who had just entered asked.
"I wasn't talking to you."
"We're alone, and I could hear everything you said, but if you say so, then that must be it."
At the servant's nonchalant words, Gerhard contemplated for a moment.
'Should I tell him?'
About the end of the world, about Aint Armian being the protagonist of the prophecy book, and even about the terrible future where he falls.
Hyde, his servant, had been serving him since childhood and was his closest aide. Except for family, he was the most trustworthy person.
He was also Gerhard's hands and feet, so he was the most suitable assistant for more effectively responding to the end of the world.
"Hyde."
"Yes, Young Master."
"...No, it's nothing."
Nevertheless, he still couldn't bring himself to talk about it.
When considering the situation in reverse, Gerhard couldn't find it in himself to believe it.
'I'll talk about it after securing definitive evidence.'
He decided to go with the method most characteristic of himself.
Appealing to emotions wasn't his way, nor was he confident in it.
"By the way, what's the matter?"
"Ah. A guest has come to see you."
"A guest?"
"Yes. He said his name is Aint Armian."
"...Where is he?"
"At the company store where you had your previous meeting. What would you like to do?"
"Wait a moment."
'I didn't expect him to make contact first.'
It was unexpected.
He thought the bait wasn't enough yet, but was he wrong?
"Why do you think Aint Armian wants to see me?"
"It must be because you gave him an opening, Young Master."
"The reason?"
"People who knock on the Goldenheims' door are diverse, but their objectives are all the same."
Money. Whether it's wrapped in various words like sponsorship, support, or loans, the fundamental aim was ultimately the same.
"Yes. I think the same."
Gerhard nodded.
If you know the opponent's intentions, it becomes easier to respond.
"You must be careful."
"Careful?"
"We don't know how the imperial family will react. The current imperial family is embarrassingly different from the old one, but even so, you would be an eyesore to them."
"I know."
Nevertheless, he had to create and maintain a connection. Because he had seen what kind of hero Aint Armian would grow into.
"For now, refuse the meeting."
"Should I send someone discreetly?"
"Yes."
"I'll use the person prepared for this situation. Will you write a letter?"
Gerhard shook his head. Their relationship wasn't sentimental enough to exchange letters.
"Give him an elixir."
"Money instead of equipment?"
"The Academy is a place full of eyes, though he would have been careful. If his equipment changed after he was rejected from meeting me?"
It would be a suspicious situation to anyone.
"I'll prepare an appropriate elixir."
"No."
He recalled the future he had seen before.
'Andromalius.'
That terrifying appearance was enough to give him goosebumps just thinking about it.
Gerhard did not want to confront it at all, and stopping it was Aint's role from the beginning.
'Since I don't know how the future might change due to the butterfly effect caused by me, giving help when I can is the surest way to reduce variables.'
It was somewhat regrettable, but better than the extinction of humanity.
"Go to the family vault yourself and bring it."
Gerhard said with determination.
***
That day, when Aint returned to his dormitory grumbling to Gardner, he was shocked to see a small box placed on the bed.
"See!"
"What did I tell you!"
"There's no definitive proof that Senior Gerhard gave this..."
Aint, who was opening the box, involuntarily dropped it when he confirmed the identity of the elixir inside.
"A Saint Bird's heart? Crazy, how did he get this?"
It was the heart of a sacred bird that handled light. It had perfect compatibility with the Armian swordsmanship, which also utilized the power of light.
"As expected of those upstarts."
"Now, look. Who else would put this expensive elixir in elegant packaging and leave it on your bed but those upstarts?"
"Do you think that makes sense normally?"
"...I can't deny it. But it's not the equipment we requested."
"Yes. It's evidence that the upstarts are being wary of the usurpers."
Gardner's triumphant smile was just a bonus.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Pawn
chapters.content:
Chapter 20: Pawn
"Magic Survival Techniques," "Combat, War and Magic," "Exploration of Magical Beasts and Monsters."
These three classes built foundations in the first year, and from the second year onward, joint lectures with the Knight Department were frequent—or rather, held every time.
They were also subjects that valued practical experience more than theory.
And the Knight Department's "War and Practical Dueling" was a subject that aligned with the three subjects of the Magic Department.
"The time has come."
It had already been a month since he and Luina took first place in the first joint class.
During that time, there hadn't been any major incidents, but to Gerhard, this peace felt like the calm before a storm.
"Today, another upset will occur in the duel."
A part explicitly stated in the prophecy book.
His purpose today was to verify the scene and observe Veriana Kalproten, who would turn into a demon's pawn because of this incident.
Having organized his plan, Gerhard called his servant.
"Hyde, you've dropped the money, right?"
"Of course."
"Let's go."
"Yes."
Gerhard put on his coat.
***
"The winner, Aint Armian!"
It was quite interesting.
Watching the future from the prophecy book unfold exactly as foretold.
"My goodness, Aint won!"
"Aint defeated Veriana?"
"Impossible! How?"
"His admission rank was 38th, right? Is this possible in just a month or two?"
And also observing people's intense reactions as the future flowed in a direction generally unexpected.
He could feel a subtle sense of superiority, knowing it alone while watching those reactions.
'This could become addictive.'
It seemed like it would be quite good to take up as a hobby.
Gerhard rested his chin on his hand and calmly reviewed the battle between Veriana and Aint.
'It was a bit different from the content of the prophecy book.'
It couldn't be said that he completely dominated. But it wasn't the paper-thin, precarious battle mentioned in the prophecy book either.
'Is it thanks to the elixir?'
His energy had clearly increased noticeably. Overall, Veriana's swordsmanship was superior, but Aint overwhelmed her with his aura.
It would be impossible to say that Gerhard had no part in that.
He smiled with satisfaction.
'The future changes, albeit slightly, according to my actions.'
It was a fact he had already confirmed once with Carlo. As it repeated again, he couldn't help but smile.
It was because he was gradually gaining confidence that he could change the gloomy future with his power.
"Is it thanks to the elixir?"
"Well, it certainly had some influence."
"That sounds like you're saying Aint would have won even without the elixir."
"That's something no one knows."
Gerhard shrugged and tapped the armrest with his finger.
His gaze was now directed not at the winner but at the loser.
'Veriana Kalproten.'
The heir of the rising Kalproten Viscount family.
Honestly, at first, he thought it was strange that she would take a demon's hand after just one defeat, no matter how shocking it was.
But after understanding Kalproten's inner thoughts, it wasn't that strange after all.
"Hyde."
"Yes, Young Master."
"Is Kalproten still frequently meeting with nobles?"
"Yes. Her already active political movements have increased significantly since Fridien obtained the right to the Golden Decree."
The Imperial Electors. Only seven in the empire, gloriously holding the authority to elect the emperor of the empire.
They were originally the founding contributors of the empire.
The Armian royal family, which became the foundation of the empire, and the descendants of the five kingdoms and religions that the first emperor had unified.
To the empire, the electors were insurmountable, massive pillars and strongholds.
But that had collapsed for the first time, and a new pillar had been erected.
'From the perspective of those who think there's not much difference between the new pillar and themselves, it would only be regrettable.'
They would think and continue to think that position should have been theirs. And they would derive new possibilities.
The conclusion that if it was possible once, there's no reason it couldn't happen twice.
In that process, the interests of Schwaben and Kalproten aligned.
For Schwaben, the old imperial family was an eyesore, and for Kalproten, among the seven pillars, the old imperial family was currently the most vulnerable.
The collusion between the two was all too natural.
Therefore, while on the surface it appeared to be a simple practical duel between students, looking deeper, it was a war between Kalproten and Schwaben to defeat the Armians.
And Kalproten had lost.
"...This can't be happening."
While everyone was cheering and shocked at the upset, Veriana Kalproten was bowing her head, feeling the loneliness in the crowd.
Surprisingly, no one paid attention to her.
'If I also get defeated by Aint and things flow according to the prophecy book, will I end up like that too?'
Forgotten by the protagonist recognized by the world?
Gerhard swallowed a groan at the terrible thought that naturally arose.
"...But it's interesting."
"What is?"
"Every time you attend to observe, Aint Armian causes an upset."
The servant's eyes turned suspicious.
"Just a coincidence."
Gerhard dismissed it as such, but it was actually intentional. The reason he even brought his servant to observe. It was bait to make it more believable when he eventually talked about the prophecy book.
"I'll believe that for now."
"Hyde."
"Yes."
"Keep an eye on Veriana for a while."
"You mean Veriana Kalproten?"
There were time skips in the prophecy book. Between Veriana's defeat, her mistreatment by Rudger, and the midterm exam where she would face Aint again, there was a gap of about two weeks.
During that time, there was not even a mention of exactly how or by what method Veriana made contact with a demon and gained power.
It just happens suddenly after two weeks.
For Gerhard, who valued process over results, and the evidence gained through that process, this was a very regrettable part.
As for the result, well, it was predetermined that Aint Armian would stop it, so there was no need to make a fuss.
"Yes. Where she goes."
Where she makes contact with a demon.
"Who she meets."
How she meets a demon.
"And what conversations she has."
How the demon tempts her.
"Every little detail."
"You mean the heir of Kalproten?"
"Just don't get caught. Can you do it?"
"I didn't say I couldn't. Yes, I understand. Until when should I continue?"
"Until I say it's enough."
"Yes."
Afterwards, Gerhard confirmed Aint's companions mentioned in the prophecy book.
Balrosi Viston and Barosu Drage.
'The heir of Viston, who's the top student in the Knight Department, and the disciple of the Mercenary King, who's ranked 3rd. One companion is outstanding.'
They were individuals who could provide solid backing even outside the Academy.
It made him think that this was indeed the protagonist of the prophecy book, but on the other hand, it also seemed to suggest that without at least this level of support, it would be difficult to stop the demons' resurgence.
Balrosi and Barosu won as befitting their reputation, and they celebrated each other's victories with Aint.
"Viston and Armian are friends? Is that okay?"
"They'll handle it themselves."
Gerhard shrugged, and his gaze happened to catch Veriana again.
She was gritting her teeth while looking alternately at Balrosi and Aint.
'Ah, come to think of it...'
Veriana had been desperate to build a relationship with Balrosi. But the person in question was drawn to Aint, not her.
That aspect probably also had some influence on her decision to make a contract with a demon.
'It's like the world is pushing her to make a contract with a demon.'
Having confirmed everything he needed to, Gerhard rose from his seat.
***
"..."
Upsets tended to spread faster than ordinary rumors.
The news that Aint Armian had defeated Veriana Kalproten quickly spread throughout the Academy.
"What is there to be sorry about? It's just that my expectations were a bit high. For now, take some time to recover your body and mind. If there's an opportunity in the future, we'll talk again."
'...This can't be happening.'
Veriana, who had just faced Rudger, swallowed a sigh.
She knew. That her defeat was truly an absurd thing.
Apart from the fact that he was an Armian, for the second-ranked to be defeated by someone ranked merely 38th? Even though the 10th-ranked Anto had fallen first, there was a clear difference in level between second and tenth.
'...Damn it.'
This incident wouldn't be a major problem.
Schwaben and Kalproten had many means to defeat the Armians. Veriana was just their first blade.
Yes, on a grand scale, there was no significant problem.
'But what about me?'
What about her, who had not only betrayed her family's expectations but had lost to none other than an Armian?
The Kalproten family and Veriana Kalproten were distinctly different entities.
The biggest problem was that her family had talent that could replace her at any time.
She wasn't the only heir of Kalproten. She had a younger brother, and his talent wasn't much inferior to Veriana's.
'That damned brat dares to take my place...!'
And his ambition was no less than Veriana's.
What if this incident became the trigger?
The prince was disappointed, and her father would be furious. It wasn't a baseless, far-fetched assumption.
'I must win. There's no second chance for me.'
The root of all causes was Aint Armian. It was because of her defeat to him that she was in this situation. The best solution was to defeat him and regain her prestige and honor.
'In swordsmanship, I was actually ahead.'
She was only slightly advantageous against an Armian whose swordsmanship was half-forgotten, but nevertheless, she had the advantage.
The problem was energy.
'His aura was greater than mine...'
It was purer and denser. She was pushed back in the battle of auras.
'How?'
She had grown up as an elite with her family's support since childhood. She had consumed countless elixirs, not to mention swordsmanship, etiquette, and education.
No matter how she thought about it, she couldn't understand how the heir of the declining Armians had more aura than her.
Nevertheless, the result was out, and she had to turn this situation around.
'I must...'
Her hand gripping the sword tightened.
***
[Veriana Kalproten is just swinging her sword, traveling between lectures, dormitory, downtown, and the training grounds.]
[She does encounter students and professors while going to lectures, but she doesn't engage in any notable conversations.]
[In town, she visits bookstores, grocery stores, general stores, blacksmiths, etc., but doesn't do anything special other than buying or repairing items.]
[Since that day, there has been no meeting with Prince Rudger so far.]
[There are no special matters yet. I will continue to report consistently.]
Gerhard, who had returned after having a meal, checked the report placed on his desk.
'So there's no contact point yet. How exactly does the contact occur?'
Demons were certainly not common beings.
A thousand years ago, they were completely exterminated by the first emperor who founded the empire, and all traces were thoroughly erased.
Matters concerning demons were almost taboo, and couldn't be found just because one wanted to find them.
'Veriana wouldn't think of demons first.'
Over a thousand years, humanity had erased the word "demon" from their minds. It was nearly impossible for Veriana to come up with the idea of a contract with a demon on her own.
'Then, as expected...'
It means demons hiding among humans would approach Veriana first.
That's why monitoring Veriana's every move was more important than anything. It meant they could catch traces of demons.
And two weeks passed.
Frighteningly, nothing happened.
'...This isn't right?'
Clearly, something should have happened, and it should have happened significantly.
It should have...
'Could it be false? Was the most important demon part among the contents of the prophecy book actually false?'
It was two days before the first-year Knight Department's midterm exam, where Aint Armian would battle with Veriana Kalproten, who had given in to a demon.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Demons Rising [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 21: Demons Rising [1]
"Finally, today is the day."
["Again, again it's you! Aint Armian!"
Veriana rushed at him. Aint calmly withstood her attack.
After her defeat, Veriana's sword tip had become sharper, having ground her teeth in bitter resentment.
A fierce exchange of blows ensued.
But the winner was predetermined. Aint was not careless enough to lose to an opponent he had already defeated once.
Especially with Gardner Alpenfassen, the greatest master, by his side.]
["I don't have any particular ill feelings toward you."
Aint's sword cut Veriana. Veriana's map burned.
"It's over..."
"Don't make me laugh!"
Despite this, no instructor appeared, and Veriana refused to accept defeat.
"You're a filthy one who's forgotten chivalry. Kill him. If he lives, he's a worm that will bring down the honor of knights."
"That's not allowed."
"Then knock him unconscious. If you leave him, the instructors will take care of him."]
[Aint, who left after Veriana collapsed, didn't know. The demonic energy that was beginning to creep out had started to corrupt his body and mind.]
In the early dawn as light began to break, Gerhard Goldenheim greeted the morning with a headache.
After having a light tea time, he visited the Golden Turtle Company's academy branch.
"Young master, you've arrived?"
"Young master."
He roughly acknowledged the greetings from the staff and headed to the warehouse.
Opening the doors of one of dozens of massive warehouses, he went inside and began to sweep items into his personal subspace.
"What are you doing?"
"Preparing for contingencies."
"...Are you going to war?"
Gerhard ignored the other person's words and stuffed his subspace to capacity. Empty spaces appeared here and there in the company's spacious warehouses.
"Hyde, when did you get here?"
"I arrived when you entered the warehouse."
Hyde answered.
"What about Veriana?"
"Didn't you tell her to come early this morning?"
"So, where is Veriana?"
"There's still nothing unusual."
"Even now?"
"Yes."
"That's a bit troublesome."
Hyde had no reason to lie to him. Although something felt off, Gerhard had no choice but to accept it.
'Then there are two possibilities.'
Either the demon doesn't exist, contrary to the prophecy book.
"...Or your abilities were insufficient."
"That's the first time I've heard such words in my life."
Hyde became serious.
"Whatever it is, I carefully offer my opinion on whether your suspicion is just a suspicion or not."
"In short, you're saying I'm delusional."
"That's not what I meant. To begin with, I don't even know why you ordered me to monitor Veriana Kalproten."
That was natural since he hadn't explained the clear reason.
Even if Hyde tried to think about it, without knowing the future where the guy would fall to a demon, it would be impossible to come up with a reasonable inference.
'Right, that's how the world usually works.'
Things rarely proceeded smoothly. Especially regarding matters related to demons that hadn't appeared even once in the past thousand years.
"Anyway, there's something more urgent now."
Gerhard replied as he closed his filled subspace.
"I'm going to observe the midterm exam now."
"First-year students again?"
"Yes."
"Do you really need to go that far for Aint Armian? I don't understand."
"I'll explain everything after this is over."
He would be able to do that. If Veriana really became a demon's dog, he could convince Hyde with evidence, or if the prophecy was false, he could make Hyde understand based on that.
"I trust you, but do you really have to go this time?"
"Why do you ask?"
"Because I can't accompany you."
"...What do you mean?"
Gerhard's eyes widened at the unexpected development.
"A letter came from the family."
Hyde handed him a letter with the seal broken. After checking it, Gerhard clicked his tongue.
"A summons from my father."
"Yes."
"Hah... of all times?"
"Yes."
This was troublesome.
He was on his way to personally verify a demon with his own eyes. Since he couldn't be certain what variables and dangers might be lurking, he wanted to prepare as much as possible.
In that sense, having an escort wasn't an option but a necessity.
After contemplating briefly, Gerhard nodded.
"It can't be helped. Go. I'll go with someone else."
"Who might that be?"
Gerhard tore a piece of paper from the side of the warehouse and scribbled on it.
"Deliver this to Luina Berchef. As quickly as possible."
Fortunately, he had another card left.
***
"What brings you here so suddenly in the morning?"
After leaving the company, Gerhard found a café. It was operated by the company. When he opened the door to a private room, Luina, who had received his message, greeted him.
"Since we don't have much time, I'll get straight to the point. I've discovered a very precious spirit medicine growing in the northwestern mountain region."
"Spirit medicine?"
"It's comparable to the mandrake root you ate. I want to harvest it."
At the mention of mandrake, Luina's eyes widened.
"What does that have to do with me?"
"I'd like to ask you to escort me. When gathering spirit medicine, I can't really pay attention to my surroundings."
Hearing Gerhard's words, she tilted her head.
"...But the western part of the mountain region is where the first-year knight department's midterm exam is taking place now, isn't it? Access should be restricted?"
"In this world, nothing is impossible with money."
"...You speak so boldly about bribing someone."
A contemptuous gaze shot at Gerhard.
"Who was it? No, I don't even need to ask. Professor Grad, to think he would accept a bribe and allow someone to intrude on the exam..."
"That's not particularly important."
"How is that not important?"
Gerhard brought up the nonexistent spirit medicine story because he knew her personality well.
It was better to demonstrate a clear intention that would not harm others, rather than intruding on the exam site without any reason.
"I'll just quietly gather the spirit medicine and leave. If you escort me, we can avoid causing any disturbance."
"Does it have to be today?"
"It's a precious spirit medicine. What if someone else discovers it today?"
"Even if you're late by a day..."
"Even being one minute late can change ownership when it comes to plants."
And all he needed to do was bring her along and make it seem like a coincidence when they encountered the demon.

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Demons Rising [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 22: Demons Rising [2]
Luina Berchef was a person with orthodox chivalry who believed in upholding justice and protecting the weak.
What would she do if a real demon appeared before her?
If she realized that she had to fight against a being like a demon?
How would she act? Would she stand by and watch, or would she try to do what she could?
Furthermore, would she become more cooperative with Gerhard in his efforts to stop the demons, or not?
'Although the reliability of the prophecy book has declined a bit, it predicted that the entire continent would be engulfed in war by demons.'
It wasn't something that could be handled by one individual or a single family.
He needed allies.
The prophecy said that if left alone, Aint Armian would stop it, but he was now aware that his own actions could change the future.
He couldn't even guess what kind of butterfly effect the changed future might cause, so it was right to prepare as much as possible for the aspects that could be prepared.
"In that sense, you're quite suitable."
Second in rank at the academy, and the daughter of a former Arch Duke family slowly recovering its fortunes.
And a future Royal Knight certified by the prophecy book, which had slightly lost credibility but was still mostly accurate.
She couldn't be more suitable as an ally.
Originally, he had planned to just show her the evidence, but now that Hyde had something come up, he had no choice but to make her his escort and let her see with her own eyes.
"...What do you mean all of a sudden?"
"I mean, please be my escort."
"I haven't agreed to it yet."
Luina's brow furrowed.
"Why should I do that? I'm busy with the midterm exams too."
"You ate the mandrake root."
Her demeanor was quite different from before. It seemed she hadn't fully assimilated the spirit medicine's energy yet, as she appeared rough and unrestrained.
"...How long do you think you can use that?"
"This is only the second time. And it will be the last."
"Even so, intruding on the exam site is a bit..."
As she hesitated, Gerhard spoke again. He didn't intend to ask without offering something in return.
"I'll be visiting my family during the upcoming vacation. I'm thinking of mentioning the Berchef family to my father."
"...Are you threatening me now?"
"No. It's a proposal. If you help me, the interest on your debt might not accrue for a while even after you graduate."
"Even so, I..."
"I think we've built up a reasonable amount of trust."
"Even so..."
"The rebuilding of the Berchef family might be advanced by who knows how many years."
Luina grabbed his hand.
***
The first-year midterm exam wasn't particularly special.
They showed off to each other in exactly the same way as the second-year students had done in the northern mountain region until recently.
The differences were that it wasn't in pairs but solely for the knight department, the duration was two days, and it was a real exam rather than a practice.
Dense mountains. A man and a woman were moving between them.
"Keep your presence hidden as much as possible. Don't let the professors or instructors notice us."
The man, Gerhard, spoke while wearing a stealth cloak that concealed his presence and aura.
"Didn't you say you bribed Professor Grad?"
"Just because I bribed him doesn't mean it's okay to walk around openly, don't you think?"
"I'm glad you at least have the awareness that this is problematic."
Luina, also wearing a stealth cloak, sighed softly.
"So where are we supposed to go?"
"Wait and see."
Gerhard took out a map from his pocket. It was a map with red and blue dots moving around.
"According to the map..."
"...Isn't this a professor's map?"
"That's right. I received it along with instructions to avoid bumping into instructors or other students."
"...Hah. Professor Grad. I'm not even surprised anymore."
No, at this point, it might even be a good method since he let them in. She muttered lowly.
Gerhard thought he had handled it well and looked for a number. A dot marked with 38. That was Gerhard.
"Ho-oh."
He noticed a dot marked with 2 not far from them, and his eyes lit up.
"This way. Let's go."
"Yes. We really must just gather the spirit medicine and leave immediately."
"Of course."
"When you say it, somehow it doesn't seem obvious."
The two quickly entered deeper into the mountains. Monsters appeared emitting foul odors, but thanks to keeping their presence hidden as much as possible and with the help of artifacts, they somehow managed to avoid them.
Thanks to checking the map and avoiding others, they didn't even encounter other students or instructors.
The anomaly occurred then. When Gerhard and Luina reached about the center of the mountain region.
───!
──!
Monster roars and cries began to be heard from all directions.
An ominous energy spread from everywhere.
The dots on the map became busy with movement, and student screams echoed through the mountains.
"...What is this?"
Luina drew her sword in confusion.
Before them stood a troll with bloodshot eyes and flaring nostrils.
Its prominent veins and muscles, along with the drool it was dripping, indicated that it wasn't in a normal state.
─!
Sword and club collided. The club was split in an instant by the blue aura sword.
But even after losing its weapon, the troll didn't lose its fighting spirit, extending its fist with rolling eyes.
Bang!
A small hole formed in the ground. Broken fragments flew in all directions.
At the same time, stone spears from all around struck the troll, but the creature seemed to lack the defense mechanism that all living beings possess.
Ignoring the spears embedded in its back, it just kept rushing at Luina to kill her.
It smashed trees with its body, and even when its arm was cut off by Luina's sword, it didn't care.
It was madness itself.
"What on earth is this?!"
"It's berserk. Be careful! The troll doesn't know pain now, so you must completely cut off its head to finish it."
A berserk monster is in a completely different state from a normal monster. Because it burns everything while consuming its life force, each one is never easy to deal with.
An anomaly serious enough to halt the exam immediately.
Though he hadn't expected it to instinctively see through the stealth artifact, Gerhard remained calm.
'It has begun.'
Because he knew this was what was meant to happen, as mentioned in the prophecy book.
'The monster wave occurs even though there was no contact with demons from Veriana.'
What a joke, is it playing hard to get?
Gerhard snorted and cast a spell.
For now, it was time to deal with that persistent creature.

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Demons Rising [3]
chapters.content:
Chapter 23: Demons Rising [3]
There's a common story that often appears in plays.
When the protagonist is in danger, problems simultaneously occur all around them.
At the same time, helpers who could assist the protagonist disappear, so the protagonist must solve the problem alone with their own strength.
It's absurd that such clichéd situations happen in reality too, but anyway, the situation was racing toward chaos as written in the prophecy book.
"We should leave this place quickly and leave it to the professors and instructors."
Luina was right.
The professors and instructors were originally stationed throughout the area in preparation for such unexpected incidents.
They would somehow resolve the situation, even if it took some time. Of course, there would be some casualties in the process, but that wasn't something the two of them needed to worry about.
"No, we won't do that."
But that wasn't what Gerhard wanted.
"We're going in there."
"Are you crazy?"
"Hardly."
This is what he came to see. This is why he specifically brought Luina along, to prepare for this situation.
"The monsters in the northwestern region are only limited to certain types. Their level isn't even that high."
This was because the western part of the northern mountain region was a field for lower-grade students.
"Even if they're berserk, would they really be a match for us? With you and me here?"
"...Did you perhaps anticipate this and bring me along?"
Unnecessarily sharp.
"Don't say such nonsense. How could anyone predict this?"
"That's true."
"The spirit medicine is not far from here. Are you asking me to give it up? Even after I promised you compensation?"
"...Given how things have turned out, you can cancel it."
"No, I can't miss the spirit medicine."
He shook his head firmly.
"Is spirit medicine more important than life?"
"You're making me repeat myself like a parrot. How would our lives be in danger when I'm not weak and you're here?"
Right after Aint defeated Veriana who challenged him and knocked her unconscious, a large-scale berserk outbreak of monsters caused by demons occurred.
While professors and instructors were running around trying to resolve the berserk situation, Veriana, who received power from a demon, pursued him.
And Aint Armian struggled against an opponent he couldn't handle, continued to struggle, and eventually awakened.
He absolutely had to see with his own eyes the moment Aint Armian first confronted the demon, which could be considered the most important scene in the prophecy book.
To get the final confirmation about the prophecy book.
"If you won't go, I'll go alone. Go back. Let's forget about our agreement."
Gerhard walked away without even listening to Luina's answer.
Luina stared blankly at his back.
"...What's so special about this spirit medicine?"
Of course, it wasn't that it wasn't valuable. But no matter how precious the spirit medicine was, could it be worth one's life?
Luina simply couldn't understand Gerhard.
"If you tell me to go, do you think I can't go?"
Gerhard wasn't that weak. And since he knew how to fill his gaps using artifacts, even with monsters going berserk, there shouldn't be a major disaster.
...Probably.
"..."
Luina took a deep breath.
If she left him now and he died, she felt she might never sleep soundly again.
"Wait!"
She bit her lip tightly and followed after Gerhard.
***
"Didn't you tell me to go alone?"
"I never said such a thing."
Luina strode ahead, cutting a path. Since there wasn't a proper path in the dense forest, it was more efficient for her to take the lead.
"We really must just gather the spirit medicine and leave immediately."
"Are you helping me?"
"Do I need to say it again with my own mouth?"
"Right. I'll make sure to do that. As soon as we gather the spirit medicine, we'll leave."
"Which direction should we go?"
Hmm. After briefly checking the map to confirm their location, Gerhard pointed west.
At that moment, Luina stopped walking. Her hand gripping the sword tightened.
Not far away, there was a student fleeing from a group of monsters.
"Help me! Instructor! Instructor!"
His figure, being chased by dozens of monsters, looked quite precarious.
"Do you want to help him?"
"If we leave him like that, he'll die."
"We mustn't be discovered."
"But..."
Gerhard checked the map again.
"There's no instructor nearby, but there's a decent reinforcement. He'll be saved soon."
"Reinforcement?"
At that moment.
─!
A dark blue sword light sliced through the sky.
The group of monsters chasing their prey was split in half, and scraps of flesh flew up.
"Get behind me!"
With a short shout, the sword light flashed again. Each time the sword pierced through space, a monster inevitably fell.
"Balrosi...!"
The student who received help hid behind the man's back. The battle ended as quickly as it had made the chase scene look insignificant.
That's how extreme the level difference felt.
"Thanks, Balrosi."
"It's only natural."
"...Ah, but..."
The student hesitated, belatedly realizing the purpose of the midterm exam. But Balrosi shook his head.
"I have no intention of pursuing grades in this situation. I'm thinking of finding the instructors. Let's go together."
"Is that okay?"
"Yes."

chapters.title: Chapter 24: Demons Rising [4]
chapters.content:
Chapter 24: Demons Rising [4]
The two students disappeared beyond the bushes.
Luina, who had been watching silently while suppressing her presence, murmured quietly.
"...Balrosi Viston."
He was a monster who had become the top student in the knight department after overwhelming Veriana, who had been in second place.
"What do you think? Am I not right?"
"Indeed you are."
"What's your impression after seeing him directly? Could you win if you fought him?"
"Since he wasn't using his full power, I can't properly gauge his level, but..."
Luina nodded as if it were natural.
"I don't think I would lose."
"Right, that's how it should be."
Gerhard didn't know whether Balrosi Viston would become a Royal Knight or not. But Luina was a Royal Knight candidate certified by Sir Gardner Alpenfassen.
There was absolutely no reason for Luina to be inferior to Balrosi, regardless of what kind of talent he had, both in terms of ability and as Aint's comrade.
'Balrosi Viston. That one also needs to be observed carefully.'
Gerhard memorized Balrosi's appearance.
"What do you mean by that?"
"Nothing. Let's hurry. We'll be late at this rate. I'll use magic from now on."
Rumbling, Gerhard moved the ground and advanced quickly.
"Yes."
Luina nodded slightly and followed him. Then she tilted her head.
'Late for what?'
Weren't they going to gather spirit medicine?
***
They were late.
That's what Gerhard judged.
The broken giant trees, the gouged earth, the shattered piles of rocks, and the monster corpses scattered everywhere.
The scene, reminiscent of a battlefield, showed that there had been an extremely fierce battle here.
And in the center of that ruins, there was one collapsed figure.
"...What is this?"
"There was a battle."
"...Veriana Kalproten?"
Luina recognized the fallen figure.
"Wait...!"
Before Gerhard could stop her, she hurriedly ran over. After examining the fallen Veriana's wounds and breathing, she heaved a sigh of relief.
"There are some injuries, but fortunately, she's alive."
"Don't approach carelessly!"
"What are you saying about someone who's collapsed?"
Luina made a face that showed she couldn't understand. Gerhard, who couldn't yet convince her about the prophecy book, swallowed.
"We might be discovered. She seems to have been eliminated, so the instructors will take care of her."
That wouldn't happen.
The sudden berserk outbreak of monsters had ruined the midterm exam itself, and the instructors didn't have the luxury to pay attention to all students.
At least not until the moment when Veriana, corrupted by demonic energy, would rise and attack Aint.
"But we can't just leave someone who's collapsed like this. Aren't the monsters in an abnormal state too?"
"So..."
How should I explain this?
Gerhard glanced at Veriana. Fortunately, there was no sign of her waking up at the moment.
Just as he thought that.
Kreeeeek-
There was a bizarre sound that couldn't be described.
Gerhard's gaze instinctively turned to Veriana.
Her eyes, which had been quietly closed, were now open.
That wasn't all.
Not only were they bloodshot to the point where she could hardly be called human, but her entire body's skin was also grotesquely swelling and contracting repeatedly.
"What is this...?"
"Luina! Put her down and back away immediately!"
Luina flinched in surprise and created distance.
Veriana seemed about to fall headfirst to the ground, but then sprang up like a coiled spring.
Haa, a dark breath was exhaled along with heated breathing. The two red eyeballs alternated between looking at Gerhard and Luina.
And then.
──!
Killing intent exploded.
Seeing this, Gerhard realized.
"...This is insane."
That something had gone wrong.
***
Her appearance was grotesque.
Parts of her skin had turned black, and her eyes were beyond bloodshot, having changed to a bright red color.
It was enough to take one's breath away with the overflowing murderous intent and fighting spirit, as if she had no intention of hiding it.
Above all, the black energy creeping out from her entire body evoked ominousness and instinctive revulsion.
"...What on earth."
Luina didn't know what it was, but Gerhard clearly recognized it.
That is demonic energy.
And that person has been tainted by a demon.
The prophecy was right.
After reaching these three consecutive conclusions, Gerhard quickly assessed the next situation.
The red pupils were not directed toward where Aint, who had made her like this, had disappeared, but toward Luina and Gerhard.
It was the worst situation.
'This is why I told you not to approach carelessly.'
They should have moved away before she woke up.
No, it's fine. There was no need to blame Luina.
A student who had fainted and collapsed in a situation where monsters had gone berserk.
If one didn't know about demons, it was natural to go help.
'But...'
I won't blame you, but since you woke her up, you'll have to handle it.
"What on earth is that...?"
"Luina. First, calm down and listen to me."
Gerhard slowly walked to the side. Her gaze followed him. It didn't seem like she would leave them alone and go to Aint.
"That's demonization."
"...Demonization?"
"She's been tainted after receiving power from a demon. Judging by her eyes, she seems to have almost no reason left."
"Are you saying that demons have reappeared in this world? And inside Veriana Kalproten's body?"
Luina was shocked.
"How do you know that...?"
"Can you win?"
"...I don't know."
Luina bit her lip.
The momentum that was continuously amplified along with the demonic energy had long surpassed the limits of Veriana.
It was not easy to gauge the opponent's level.
"Right, I suppose so."
Gerhard wasn't disappointed.
A demon appearing after a thousand years, a monster that even Aint, who received help from Sir Gardner Alpenfassen, could barely defeat after awakening.
There was certainly a gap between the current Luina and Aint, but even considering that, it would not be an easy opponent.
That was somewhat fortunate.
"Luina."
Since he always acted assuming the worst.
"Hold on for ten minutes. I'll give you a signal when I'm ready."
He had some countermeasures prepared.
"I wish you luck."
"...What?"
Gerhard ran away without even listening to Luina's answer.
Her blank gaze pierced his back, and at the same time, the tightrope-like confrontation broke.
───!
Veriana moved.
A blade riddled with demonic energy struck Luina.
"Ugh...!"
She let out a groan at the impact that was beyond imagination.
"This...!"
─!
──!
In a brief moment, after exchanging dozens of attacks and defenses, she had no choice but to leave Gerhard, who was quickly moving away.
She trembled with a sense of betrayal.

chapters.title: Chapter 25: Merchant’s Battle [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 25: Merchant's Battle [1]
'How much time has passed?'
I don't know.
Sweat poured down like rain, breath was caught in her throat, armor was half-broken, and the sword blade was nicked here and there.
'She's strong.'
Definitely not at the level of a first-year student.
The sword was sharp, and the aura was immensely heavy.
Above all, the intense ominousness felt from the aura was even eerie.
'Demonic energy?'
That's what Gerhard had said. That she was corrupted by a demon. If so, the black energy must be the power used by demons. That is, demonic energy.
Is that really why? The demonic energy continuously tried to erode her aura. Because of this, her aura consumption was greater.
Bang!
Luina rolled on the ground. The earth where she had just been standing was shattered.
The black demonic energy pursued her closely. She hurriedly straightened her posture and raised her blade.
Clang! Dark and blue flashes collided. Fragments of broken aura scattered in all directions.
"Come to your senses, Veriana Kalproten!"
Her shout wasn't heard by her opponent.
'What should I do?'
After several clashes, Luina had clearly gauged her opponent's level.
If she wanted to win, there was nothing stopping her from winning.
But even though Veriana was corrupted by a demon, she was still a student from the same school, and the problem was that it wasn't possible with a moderate approach.
She could win, but at the cost of Veriana Kalproten's life.
Because her opponent wasn't easy enough to defeat while holding back.
"..."
She bit her lip.
The muscles in her entire body screamed, and her fingertips trembled.
The end was approaching.
The biggest problem was that unlike her opponent, who drew energy like an inexhaustible well, her aura pool was quickly reaching its bottom.
'...What should I do?'
She thought of Gerhard who had fled.
If he hadn't run away, she wouldn't have had to struggle this much.
Whether with his full ability or borrowing the power of artifacts, his supporting skills were top-notch, and they could have safely subdued Veriana, albeit with some effort.
That's when it happened.
Peeeeeep-
A whistle sound came from not too far away. The direction was west, where Gerhard had fled.
'A signal?'
Luina realized this was the signal Gerhard had mentioned.
'...He must have a definitive method.'
Pushing back the disappointment that was rising, she kicked Veriana, who was charging like a mad dog, in the chest.
As her opponent fell and rolled on the ground, Luina turned around.
***
"Over here, Luina. Come this way."
"You...!"
Running along the mountain path, Luina spotted Gerhard and shouted.
"Why did you run away!"
"You're asking the obvious. Because it's a demon."
Gerhard moved while guiding the angry woman.
"If you hadn't run away, we could have won easily!"
"...Huh? You're saying it would have been possible if I had been there?"
Gerhard tilted his head.
A knight corrupted by demonic energy. A being that Aint had barely managed to defeat after awakening with Gardner's help.
"That's not possible."
Naturally, Gerhard had set the opponent's level at the highest.
There were two reasons for this.
That Aint was the one to save the world.
And the strength and mystery of a being called a demon.
"It's a demon, Luina. A demon that has appeared after a thousand years can't be that weak."
"What kind of nonsensical confidence is that? That's not a demon, it's Veriana. While it's grotesque enough to be unexplainable unless she's been corrupted by a demon, she's fundamentally human."
"..."
At that point, Gerhard sensed one mistake.
Aint's level.
No matter how much Aint was destined to become a hero who would save this world from demons, no matter that he was being taught by Sir Gardner Alpenfassen's soul, he was still just a first-year academy student.
Though he had shown tremendous growth, instantly rising to second place among first-years, he was still a first-year.
There was a clear average gap between the academy years, and the current Luina Berchef was definitely stronger than Aint Armian.
"...Wait a moment."
Gerhard's expression hardened as he realized that he had been too focused on the two challenging issues of demons and the prophecy book to see what was truly important.
"Are you really saying that the two of us could handle her?"
"Yes. By myself, I have no way to subdue her without killing her, but if you help..."
"Then what are we doing now?!"
"...Pardon?"
"Go and stop her right now! Before she gets any closer!"
Gerhard stretched out his hand toward Veriana, who was charging like a mad bull.
"Hurry and stop her before the precious trap is wasted...!"
──!
─!
That's when the explosions began to happen.
"Ah, no...!"
It started with a small stone that Veriana stepped on.
As her posture faltered momentarily when the stone exploded, magic arrows were shot from all directions.
Crack-crack-crack-
The exploding demonic energy protected its host. Veriana, who deflected all the arrows, displayed a ferocious killing intent and charged again.
Or rather, tried to.

chapters.title: Chapter 26: Merchant’s Battle [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 26: Merchant's Battle [2]
In a split second, the ground beneath her collapsed. Veriana lost her balance and flailed in the air.
And the moment her back touched the ground.
Whoosh-
A magic circle drawn with red Bristy reagent reacted and caught fire.
─!
In the center of the magic circle, which expanded by absorbing mana from magic stones, a pillar of flame that melted everything shot up vertically.
Even so, Veriana didn't fall.
She negated the flames by exploding black demonic energy and eventually crawled up over the hole.
And the next measure Gerhard had prepared went out to meet her.
When her outstretched hand triggered a trap, prepared reagents flew at her.
Crash-
Five vials broke and covered Veriana. Sizzle, the reagent with the property of corroding mana even weakened the demonic energy little by little.
Veriana screamed and staggered, triggering yet another trap. A scroll tore. Zap, with an intense spark, ten lightning bolts fell in a straight line.
Boom-boom-boom-boom!
White lightning penetrated the half-corroded demonic energy. Veriana's body trembled as if being tortured.
"Argghhhhh!"
Soon, a scream with a grotesque voice erupted.
...That was the end.
"Grrrr...."
Veriana, foaming at the mouth, rolled her eyes and collapsed.
Everything happened in the blink of an eye.
Gerhard and Luina watched blankly.
"...Is she okay? Is she possibly dead...?"
"Originally, I planned to switch positions with her as she lost her reason and approached me, then trigger another trap..."
Gerhard was muttering absently, as if he couldn't hear her words.
Only then did Luina check behind them. One step behind where Gerhard was standing, a trap that clearly looked like it had been meticulously prepared was installed.
"After that, I was going to face her together with you when she was in tatters..."
Haha, Gerhard laughed.
"I really didn't need to do that. The two of us together didn't need to."
This is what a demon is supposed to be?
Gerhard's eyes were bloodshot.
***
Among magicians, there's a famous saying.
'A magician is one who prepares.'
'A fully prepared magician can defeat anyone.'
Luina Berchef had fought magicians several times, but she had never properly understood the meaning of those words.
But at this moment, it was different.
A prepared location.
Ready magic traps.
Thoroughly anticipated strategies.
She realized the true meaning of the words that magicians lived by.
She also realized that she hadn't understood until now because they had only been simple duels.
"So this is the true way of a magician's combat..."
"Wrong. This is a merchant's way of combat."
Gerhard cut off Luina's words.
"...Not a magician but a merchant?"
"Think about it."
He extended his finger.
"Scrolls bought with money."
He moved to the side.
"Artifacts bought with money."
"But you didn't use artifacts."
"I was planning to use them. It's just that I didn't need to because she was too weak."
Once again to the side.
"Magic reagents and magic stones bought with money. And the traps made with them."
Money's touch was everywhere.
"It started with money and ended with money. If this isn't a merchant's battle, what is it? Do you think those poor beggar magicians could ever do this?"
No way. Gerhard shook his head.
"It's absolutely impossible for them. Without money, they can't do it even if they were to die and come back to life. And magicians are inherently a group that consumes rather than produces."
"...I understand what you're saying, but you are a magician, after all."
"That is also wrong. I learned magic merely for self-defense and more useful applications, but my essence is that of a merchant."
That's why it was even more regrettable.
The materials that went into waging this merchant's battle, when converted to money, were not insignificant.
"It's still absurd to think about it. If only I had known that she was weaker than expected."
If only he hadn't been intimidated by the name 'demon'.
"No, if you had just told me the truth a little earlier..."
"It was you who ran away without any explanation."
"Since there was no explanation, you should have just followed me."
"Who was it that said to hold on for ten minutes?"
"Do you think it's right to blindly follow without being given any explanation of the reason?"
Ha, Luina let out a hollow laugh. Unable to make sense of it, she shook her head and changed the subject.
"But it's unexpected. In terms of absolute amount, exempting our family from interest for three years would be more expensive."
Honestly, it was questionable that Gerhard, who was rumored to be a money demon, made such an offer.
At first, she had been suspicious, but now she thought the rumors might be a bit exaggerated. Yet today he was so concerned about money again, it was confusing to know which was his true nature.
"It's a different case."
"What case?"
"Do you know why I like money?"
"Do I need to know?"
"Because with money, you can do anything."
"You're not listening to me."
"Money is possibility."
With money, you can do things that seemed impossible.
With money, solutions that weren't there before appear.
With money, you can get people who seemed impossible to obtain.
Money is literally a treasure that can do anything.
"That's why money is precious. That's why money should be used in meaningful places, more valuable places."
Not in a sewer like this, but in places like Luina.
The money spent on Luina wasn't regrettable at all. It was because he saw the possibility that she would become a Royal Knight in the future.
"There was no reason to waste it so emptily against an opponent that we could have just faced together."
Gerhard's cold gaze turned toward the fallen Veriana. Only then did Luina, who now had the leisure to properly examine Veriana, get surprised.
It was natural that she was on the verge of death after being hit by traps and dozens of spells.
Fortunately, or maybe unfortunately, it would be fair to say that she was still alive thanks to the demonic energy.
"I'm sorry to say this in the current situation, but could you please give her a potion? She'll die if we leave her like this."
"...Alright."
Gerhard took out a potion and poured it on Veriana's body.
It can't be helped.
He muttered quietly.
"I'll just have to collect the spent money from the culprit."
That was the way of the world since ancient times. For that, she must not die.
But first, he needed to collect the still intact traps.

chapters.title: Chapter 27: Contract’s Price [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 27: Contract's Price [1]
"...Wait a moment, what do you mean by 'collect'? What does that mean?"
Luina's eyes grew somewhat fierce.
"I don't understand what you're saying. If it weren't for this guy, I would have had no reason to consume these items. Shouldn't he naturally pay the price? Personally."
"Are you saying you won't hand him over to the Judges?"
The Judges.
A group with a long tradition that began with the history of the Empire and continued to exist until now.
They were an organization directly under the Emperor, with the primary goal of finding and destroying demons.
"You mean those folks who are barely clinging to life under the name of tradition without any real purpose?"
They were people who wielded absolute power under the mission of destroying demons, but that was all in the past.
A thousand years was an extremely long time. During that long period, demons had not resurged, and the Judges lost their value.
Yet the reason the Judge system was maintained was only one: because the first Emperor had specified it in imperial law.
To never abolish the Judge system in preparation for when the demons would resurge.
But while it wasn't abolished, its scale and authority had diminished to almost nothing.
"What are you doing now?"
"I'm checking his condition."
Gerhard held Veriana's wrist and sent mana through to examine her inside. But there was no trace of demonic energy to be found anywhere.
'I expected this.'
No matter what happened to Veriana in the future according to the prophecy book, demons had been operating covertly for the past thousand years without being discovered.
There was no way they would reveal their traces so easily.
'Then why did they reveal themselves against Aint?'
Because Aint was the seed of the imperial family that had destroyed them? Were they trying to crush the sprout?
It was something impossible to know unless one was directly involved. It wasn't particularly important at the moment either.
"Try checking for yourself too. As far as I can sense, there's not a single trace of demonic energy."
"How can there be not even a bit when she was emitting such immense demonic energy?"
"So you believe in demonic energy?"
"It was my first time experiencing such energy. It was at a level that couldn't be explained unless it was demonic energy."
Of course, what's more curious is how you knew about such things, but that's another matter.
Luina, who had been half-doubtful, checked internally and was shocked.
"How is this possible...?"
"In my opinion, handing her over to the Judges, who are virtually in name only, would likely result in them finding nothing."
Even if they did find something, wouldn't it be pitiful for her?
Gerhard, who had been looking at Luina with eyes that seemed to reproach her for being excessively cold, continued.
"Marquis Kalproten will abandon her. In the end, she'll just become a demon's toy and then meet her end."
"She lost the right to receive sympathy the moment she sold her soul to a demon. And since when have you been a person overflowing with compassion?"
"What if she didn't sell her soul to a demon?"
"...What do you mean?"
Luina tilted her head, as if she couldn't understand.
"I mean, who really knows whether she just went crazy, ate something wrong, or sold her soul to a demon? If neither you nor I saw it."
"...Are you crazy?"
Gerhard took a step closer. Luina hesitated at his resolute gaze.
"We didn't see anything. Luina Berchef."
He grabbed Luina's shoulders.
"Nothing."
"Such nonsense...!"
"Neither you nor I can feel any demonic power from her. All that's left is a pitiful body on the verge of death as a result. Where exactly do you see a demon?"
"No matter how much you twist words, you can't hide the truth."
Gerhard shrugged.
"I'll extend the interest exemption period by another half year."
"I will never..."
"Nine months."
"Never..."
"Let's make it a full year, exactly."
"...I never saw anything."
The noble knight succumbed to money.
***
There wasn't a single point of light.
In the pitch-black darkness, he couldn't see anything.
He walked aimlessly.
When he thought he was getting tired and there was a sweet taste in his mouth, the darkness lifted.
The center of the dueling area set up in the classroom.
He was standing holding a sword, and in front of him was a man with golden hair.
'Aint Armian...!'
His eyes were bloodshot. The battle broke out in an instant.
He swung his sword. He used everything he had learned so far. His sword was fast and sharp.
But his opponent's sword was heavier. With each collision, aura was chipped away.
Though both were being chipped away, the one who was at a greater disadvantage was him.
'This can't be...!'
He screamed as if in agony, but no sound came from his mouth.
His body became heavier and heavier. His aura was being depleted.
'If I had done that then! If I had blocked there at that moment!'
Perhaps the result would have been different.
But in the end, the one who knelt was him again.
"Winner! Aint Armian!"
The name of the winner called out by the instructor was not his.
Everyone was surprised by the unexpected turn of events. At the same time, the world flipped.
This time it was a reception room. The reception room of Lavidus Hall, given only to the upper ranks.
He scratched the back of his hand and waited anxiously. A moment later, the door opened and Prince Rudger II appeared.
'I'm sor...'
Before he could even speak, his mouth opened on its own.
"...I'm sorry."
The prince quietly stared at him. It was a silence where one second felt like an hour.
How much time had passed? The prince finally opened his mouth.
"What is there to be sorry about? It's just that my expectations might have been a bit high."
"I was unlucky. His mana was denser and more abundant than I expected. Next time, next time I'm confident I won't lose. Please believe me."
"Next time, huh."
The prince patted his shoulder with a soft smile.
"It seems too early to talk about next time."
"Your Highness...!"
"For now, recuperate your body and mind. If there's another opportunity, we'll talk again."
The prince stood up without even listening to his answer.
'Your Highness...! Your Highness! No!'
He desperately called out to the receding back, but no voice came out.

chapters.title: Chapter 28: Contract’s Price [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 28: Contract's Price [2]
The world around him shattered like a glass window, and darkness came again.
Only then did he realize that these were memories of the past.
A past filled with regret, but one that could never be undone.
Once again, the world flipped.
"Disappointing. Despite all the praise given to Armian, Armian, it turns out to be nothing more than a toothless cat."
"Father..., that's..."
"No need for excuses. I'm deeply disappointed."
It was no longer a story of the past.
"To fail such an easy task. I'm deeply disappointed, brother."
It was the most terrible future he could imagine, one that hadn't happened yet but might.
'No...!'
A future that must never happen.
"No!"
The world collapsed.
At the same time, the darkness disappeared. His eyes snapped open.
"Huh, huh...!"
Veriana breathed heavily. Her entire body was drenched in sweat.
"...A dream?"
If it was a dream, it was truly a terrible nightmare.
Thirst arose. She reached out to the side, but there was no water. Only then did Veriana check her surroundings.
"...Where is this?"
It was neither Lavidus Hall where she stayed, nor the chamber of her territory's mansion.
"What was I doing...?"
"You're awake."
At the sudden voice, she turned her head, and someone was entering through the door.
"...Senior Gerhard Goldenheim?"
"You know me?"
"Who in the academy wouldn't know you, senior?"
"That's true. Drink this."
"Th-thank you."
Veriana took the water Gerhard handed over and drank it.
"But where is this?"
"No, that's not what you should be asking."
"Pardon?"
"Do you remember what happened?"
"...Well."
Veriana clutched her throbbing head.
She remembered fragments.
She had rushed at Aint Armian and was defeated once again. She couldn't accept it and did something dishonorable.
And then.
And then...
"...I can't remember after that. What happened?"
"It's sad to have a gap in your memory. Let me personally tell you."
Gerhard placed a small spherical jewel on the table.
It was a recording orb that had been set up while installing the traps, recording the scene at that time.
Flash-
When mana was injected, the recorded video began to play.
"...That's me?"
Veriana was shocked at her own appearance in the video, which she herself couldn't believe. And by the end, her mouth hung open in disbelief.
"...What is this?"
"You sold your soul to a demon, and then attacked us."
"Demon? Th-that's absurd. I don't even know what a demon is. I've never even met one!"
Gerhard knew that better. But it wasn't particularly important.
"Would the Judges who saw this video think the same? What about others? For instance, Marquis Kalproten?"
"...That's."
Veriana's complexion turned pale. And she realized that the senior who had saved her hadn't come with benevolent intentions.
"...What do you want from me?"
"As you can see from the video, I consumed many things to stop you."
"I'll repay you. Double, no, triple."
"And the mental shock I suffered from fighting a demon's servant is also significant."
"That's..."
Gerhard took out a piece of paper from his pocket.
"What you need to do is simple. Sign here. Then everything will be forgotten."
Veriana carefully checked the document.
"...This is an absurd contract. Completely like a slave..."
"You seem to misunderstand something."
Gerhard leaned his upper body slightly forward.
"Do you think I'm making you an offer right now?"
Gerhard's eyes sank coldly.
"You have exactly two choices."
Either be captured by the Judges.
Or sign the contract.
"Choose."
Die, or become a slave.
There wasn't even a need to spend money to persuade her.
***
The monsters' berserk outbreak was not at an ordinary level, and all the professors and instructors of the academy mobilized to calm the situation.
Fortunately, no students died, but the midterm exam was canceled midway.
"Good work everyone. You must have been surprised by the sudden situation, but all exams for the next two days have been canceled, so rest and recover."
All the injured were moved to the medical center within the academy, and Aint returned safely to the dormitory.
"Quite strange."
Sir Gardner Alpenfassen muttered.
"The berserk outbreak was clearly the work of demons."
I felt subtle but omnidirectional demonic energy.
During the thousand years, humans might have forgotten the existence of demonic energy, but at least Gardner hadn't.
"But there was nothing after that. Why?"
"Isn't it good if there's nothing?"
"Don't let your guard down. They are demons. The most terrible and despicable beings."
"They don't do anything without meaning. Everything has a purpose. And that purpose is never beneficial to humanity."
"And if demons are up to something and targeting someone, nine times out of ten, it would be you, Aint Armian."
"...Pardon? Why?"
"Because to demons, the Armian family is an enemy etched deep into their bones."
A thousand years ago, every time demons were defeated and beheaded, they lamented.
"'If only there hadn't been the first Emperor, if only there hadn't been Armian.' If I were a demon, I'd eradicate the Armian bloodline first."
"..."
Aint swallowed dry saliva at the eerie feeling that suddenly arose.
"For some reason, nothing happened this time, but always stay alert and follow my guidance well."
"That's how you'll survive."
"Yes. I'll keep that in mind."
"By the way, it's really strange. Did someone happen to ruin the demons' plans?"
"That's an interesting hypothesis."
Aint chuckled and entered the dormitory.
And at that time, that someone...
"Urgggh...!"
Unable to withstand the headache that felt like it would split his head, he collapsed onto the bed.
["Congratulations, Aint. That's impressive."
"Don't go on like that, Balrosi. It's nothing compared to you."
"No, what's impressive is impressive."
"That's right. Going from 38th to 5th in just half a semester. It's an unbelievable growth rate."
Someone abruptly interrupted. It was a beautiful woman with short orange hair and impressive emerald eyes.
"Aint Armian. Right?"
"You are...?"
"Ariadne Florian. From the magic department."]
[The required course for the knight department, "Field Survival Techniques."
After the midterm exams, students were thrown into the southern forest for a week.
"This worked out well. There's something arranged by His Majesty the Emperor in this lake. Let's secure that and..."]
["Amazing..." Aint murmured. A spirit medicine with an iridescent color...]
["Spirit creature? A thief acting like an owner! It's beyond your ability to handle, so for now, run away...!"]
["Mithril! It's a mithril vein!"]
Parts of the sealed prophecy book were flooding in.

chapters.title: Chapter 29: Mithril Ambition [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 29: Mithril Ambition [1]
"Your Grace, here is the recording orb sent by the young master."
The Duke received the small orb handed over by the butler and stared at it intently.
"Yes, this is it."
Recently, when the Duke was briefly away, the warehouse had been raided by Gerhard.
What was taken was the heart of a Saint Bird, a creature as rare as a Phoenix.
It was one of the treasures stored in the first-class warehouse, worth whatever was asked for it.
"You said Hyde took it personally?"
"Yes."
If Hyde had stepped forward, it was Gerhard's will.
Although he had formally submitted a request for removal, Hyde had personally taken it through a teleportation magic circle before approval was granted.
The teleportation magic circle required enormous magic stones and magicians each time it was used. Therefore, even the Duke didn't use it unless it was truly important.
'To use such a teleportation magic circle and take it before formal approval was granted...'
He must have judged it to be an urgent matter.
