"How, where did you get it?"
"That's a secret, but it's not stolen goods. I just want to say that I acquired it legitimately. Will you buy it?"
Gerhard hesitated a little. When negotiating, it was most important to hide what you wanted from the other party.

chapters.title: Chapter 42: Adamant Deal [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 42: Adamant Deal [2]
If it was revealed, you would be at the mercy of the other party, causing unnecessary expenditure.
But this was adamant. The ore he desperately needed for his grand plan after obtaining mithril.
It was worth getting even if it meant taking a small loss.
'Besides, it's Aint after all.'
He had planned to continuously support Aint anyway. If he could openly support him on the pretext of obtaining adamant, it would be even better.
"Yes, I'll buy it."
"Then..."
"This time, let me ask."
But his merchant instinct protruded unconsciously.
"How much were you thinking of asking for?"
***
A week passed in an instant. No significant incidents occurred after the water dragon, and Gerhard returned to his office and spread out papers.
'Adamant, huh.'
When Aint first mentioned it, Gerhard momentarily lost his composure. It was inevitable given the item.
Besides the value of adamant, he never dreamed that Aint, who had lost the mithril, would bring adamant instead.
'It's unlikely he had adamant from the beginning. If he did, he would have used or sold it long ago.'
He must have obtained it recently.
To have the mithril stolen but get adamant instead.
Is this the hero's luck that the prophecy book spoke of, the one who would stop the demon?
He couldn't help but chuckle, but this was by no means a bad situation for Gerhard.
'If I alloy mithril with adamant, I can create the ideal I've been aiming for.'
His hand holding the pen moved faster. There was no hesitation in his strokes as he drew what he had been thinking about for a long time.
'Did my actions influence things this time too?'
Despite being as careful as possible, he must have slipped up somewhere. That's why Aint found adamant, and the water dragon burst out of the lake.
He was quite surprised, but thankfully things had worked out well.
No, as a result, he had gained not only mithril but also adamant, so it was actually a gain.
'What kind of place was it? An underground underwater cave with both mithril and adamant?'
Perhaps there were other minerals as well. Gerhard, who decided to check again later, saw the water dragon screaming in pain.
Indeed, the Academy professors were top-tier fighters anywhere, and even a spirit creature had no answer against their combined attack.
It just took a little time due to its sturdy build matching its huge body, but it looked like it would soon collapse.
'Using the water dragon's mana hole as a core wouldn't be bad, no, it would be the best method.'
For a spirit creature that could move such a large body and use the power of breath, its mana hole would be extraordinary.
It might not be as good as the hearts of dragons, called the masters of magic, but it would at least be more efficient than using top-grade magic stones.
'Then I should buy it. Within the Academy, what professors catch is used for their private interests. Eight or nine times out of ten, it goes to research lab subsidies.'
The professors would mobilize their connections to seek potential buyers.
'I need a lot of money. I can't handle this alone.'
It wasn't just a matter of money.
He needed the power of his family to use mithril and adamant. With his current manpower, he couldn't smelt the two minerals.
'I should visit my family soon.'
He wasn't worried about persuading the duke. The mithril was in his hands, and the adamant would soon be...
"...I've returned, Young Master."
Gerhard's contemplation was interrupted. When he stopped his hand and looked forward, Hyde was standing there with a slightly tired appearance.
"Hyde? When did you arrive?"
"About an hour ago."
"An hour?"
When he checked outside the window, darkness had already fallen.
"Why didn't you call me right away?"
"You seemed deeply immersed, so I waited, but glancing at the content, it seemed like you wouldn't sleep tonight, so I called you."
"Good job."
Indeed, his body was quite stiff, probably because he had been focused for a long time.
'To forget the flow of time.'
He must have been excited by the appearance of mithril and adamant.
"Did you finish the errand well?"
"Yes. I completed everything. But if it's not presumptuous, may I ask about that? Is it what I think it is?"
"Yes."
"...The materials seemed quite unrealistic."
At this expected reaction, Gerhard smirked and replied.
"Unrealistic?"
"Constructing a body with mithril and adamant. It's impossible."
Given the rarity and value of mithril and adamant, this was natural.
"The Golden Pillar doesn't have that much money. Even the Duke wouldn't allow it. Above all, I doubt whether so much of these two ores could be obtained."
"Do you really think so?"
"Yes, I do."
"What if I've already obtained them?"
"Pardon?"
Gerhard opened his spatial storage. Soon, dozens of boxes were stacked neatly in the spacious office.
"Open them."
"...Is it what I'm thinking? That's impossible, so many..."
"Judge after opening."
Hyde swallowed dryly and carefully opened a box. And his mouth gaped at the beauty of the blue-green light softly emanating.
"Is this also...?"
This one, that one. All the boxes were packed full of mithril.
"Th-this is unbelievable...! Where on earth did you get all this?"
"I mined it myself."
"What?"
"This is all mithril. And I plan to acquire this much adamant soon."
To be precise, he was buying it, but considering the market price of adamant, it was almost like getting it for free.
"No, I'm confused right now, what exactly are you saying?"
"You can't believe it even after seeing it with your own eyes. Hyde, that's not like you."
"...No."
Hyde blankly repeated "no."
"...Fine. Since the mithril is right before my eyes, I'll concede and believe you mined it. But what do you mean by buying adamant? Who's selling a similar amount of adamant?"
"To be precise, I'm not simply buying it with money, but becoming an investor..."
Since it would be a bit complicated to explain, Gerhard just changed the subject.
"That's not what's important, Hyde. This is."
Gerhard handed over the paper, the blueprint he had been drawing in a trance.
"As you know, I've always had a question."
Knights had their horses as partners.
Elves had spirits as friends.
Companions they could always trust and rely on.
"But why don't merchants have such things?"
Hyde couldn't bring himself to counter that it would be stranger for merchants to have such things in the first place.
His shock at the enormous amount of mithril and adamant had not yet subsided, and he was overwhelmed by Gerhard's bursting momentum.
"...So you're finally going to create this? With this incredible amount of mithril and adamant?"
"Yes. If I'm making it, I should make it as solid and sturdy as possible."
Especially since a war with demons was foretold in the future.
"This is an object that requires a tremendous amount of money and the entirety of magical engineering."
Therefore, it was a monster that only truly wealthy merchants could create, making it perfectly suited for merchants.
"It's the merchant's partner I've been dreaming of for a long time."
Also, a reliable bodyguard who would protect him in the terrible age of rampant demons, and a technological advancement that would solve all the problems until now.
"An ultra-giant Ego Golem that possesses self-awareness and moves on its own."
"...That really is an enormous expense... but, does it have to be this big?"
"Because it looks cool."
Nod. Hyde agreed without even realizing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 43: Hidden Dangers [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 43: Hidden Dangers [1]
In the early dawn, before the sun had fully risen, Aint prepared early and went outside.
"You told me to carefully examine the contract and be cautious not to be deceived."
"But is there really a need to worry so much? It's more like I'm bringing my nose to them and asking them to cut it."
With Gardner Alpenfassen's continued warnings and the subtle rumors about the Goldenheim family, Aint became increasingly tense.
"Whew, when I just listen to these stories, it feels like I'm fighting demons."
"...I'm not sure if that means demons are terrifying or that the Goldenheims aren't as scary as I thought."
We'll see. Aint carefully opened the door to the tavern. It was a shop owned by the Golden Turtle Company, as Gerhard had mentioned.
***
A sealed room that didn't allow outside eyes.
"I've written down all your requirements. Read it carefully."
Aint swallowed dryly as he checked the contract Gerhard handed him.
[Adamant Sale Contract]
[Aint Armian and Gerhard Goldenheim fulfill this adamant sale contract with mutual trust.]
[Aint Armian shall be referred to as Party A, and Gerhard Goldenheim as Party B.]
[1).Party A sells 70kg of adamant to Party B. The 70kg of adamant shall be referred to as "the goods" hereafter.
2).As payment for the goods, Party B shall...]
The content of the contract, spanning several pages, was quite lengthy, but summarized, it had three main points:
Aint gives the adamant to Gerhard.
Gerhard pays with adamant equipment, money, and discreet sponsorship.
'That's quite different from your firm warnings earlier, isn't it?'
After confirming that everything he requested was properly documented, Aint signed the contract.
"It's fine with me, but isn't this a loss for you? No matter how I look at it, it's too cheap compared to the price of adamant."
Gerhard asked as he gathered a copy of the contract.
"Isn't that good from your perspective, senior?"
"It's certainly good, but even as a merchant, I'm not so naive as to rejoice at kindness without reason."
"You gave me the Saint Bird's heart. That's not a small thing either."
The Saint Bird's heart was a spirit potion as precious as adamant. Honestly, when he approached Gerhard at Gardner's suggestion, he never imagined he would receive such a thing.
Of course, that wasn't the only reason he was deliberately selling the adamant at a low price.
"Even if I have adamant, I don't have the ability to use it right now..."
"If you put it up for auction, you could have received a much higher price."
"I don't have the power to protect it."
The former imperial family, Armian, still received respect from many citizens, but that was it. Adamant was such a noble material that it could potentially bring swords against the fallen former imperial family.
"It's better for me to dispose of it before rumors spread."
"What if I were to destroy you?"
"You certainly could do that. But you gave me the Saint Bird's heart, didn't you?"
He had willingly handed over a precious item of similar level to adamant, or perhaps even more valuable, without any compensation.
Would such a person take unreasonable measures when he could buy adamant at a relatively cheap price? Aint didn't think so.
The Goldenheims placed great importance on credit. They might exploit loopholes in contracts, but they never broke the contracts themselves.
"So you deliberately took a loss."
Tap tap, Gerhard drummed his fingers on the table. Then he soon nodded.
"I understand."
It was a sufficiently convincing reason.
Including the statement about trust due to the Saint Bird's heart.
Originally, it was an item considered top-grade even in the storage of his family, which possessed countless spirit potions.
If Aint hadn't been the hero who would save the world from demons, he would never have given it away.
"At least I won't be backstabbed."
"Thank you."
"And choosing me as the object of your transaction was a very good choice."
A smile formed on Gerhard's lips.
"If I help you, I help you; as you said, I absolutely have no intention of selling you out or destroying you."
Absolutely.
Gerhard emphasized once more.
'Shouldn't we just consider it as having gained favor because of the adamant?'
From the perspective of Aint and Gardner, who didn't know about the prophecy book, Gerhard's attitude was incomprehensible.
***
It was a satisfying deal.
He had planned to help Aint materially and emotionally anyway, but there was no reason for a merchant to dislike buying goods much cheaper.
"To think that giving the Saint Bird's heart would lead to this."
This transaction was thanks to the goodwill gained by giving the Saint Bird's heart. If he hadn't handed it over in the first place, Aint wouldn't have told anyone about finding adamant.
"Money really is the best."
If his family hadn't had money, they wouldn't have had the Saint Bird's heart, and naturally, the current situation wouldn't have occurred.
Just as he was thinking that...
"...Kugh?"
—!
A massive explosion occurred in his head.

chapters.title: Chapter 44: Hidden Dangers [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 44: Hidden Dangers [2]
Gerhard realized this was the same as what he had experienced before.
As he grabbed his head and collapsed onto the bed, memories flooded into his mind like a tide.
["How about it, Aint? Would you like to join the club with me?"
"Club?"
"Yes. I was invited by the seniors. The Yacht Club, I think. A club where we build relationships on a yacht once a month."]
["You must be Aint."
The man sitting naturally at the head seat was watching him.
Aint bowed his head.
"I greet you, Your Highness the Prince."
"Come now, within the Academy, we're all just students. Excessive courtesy isn't necessary."
[There were countless of them, almost like a wave.
"Monsters!"
"Why are monsters here?"
"The ship is shaking! Turn the ship back to the Academy immediately!"
But the ship was going in the exact opposite direction of their cries.]
[- Aint, behind you!
At Gardner's shout, Aint hurriedly rotated his body. But the opponent was a step faster.
Kwajik-!
A dagger broke through his armor and pierced his chest. Along with the burning pain, an ominous poison energy surged in.
"Kugh...!"
Aint checked the opponent's face. If his memory was correct, it was one of the staff working on the yacht.
"Die, Armian."
The staff member's eyes rippled with a creepy black light.]
["...This is."
]
["Could the Goldenheims be involved?"
]
"Uuugh...!"
Unable to withstand the shock, Gerhard fainted.
He missed all his lectures that day.
***
"...It's uncanny. As soon as one prophecy is resolved, it leads to the next."
Gerhard searched for cold water as he pulled off the blanket soaked with sweat. The cool water entering his body slightly relieved his thirst.
"Is this the third time?"
Even though it was already the third time, there was no sign of getting used to this pain. It would be stranger if one became accustomed to the pain of a burning brain.
"This time it's the sea. This damned Aint, incidents happen wherever he goes."
Whether it was because he was a hero destined to defeat demons and save the continent, or because he became a hero by bringing incidents with him, was unknown.
"A yacht club, huh."
A club was a small gathering where students built relationships with each other.
It was an activity encouraged by the Academy, ranging from simple tea times to monster hunting, quite diverse.
"This time he'll manage well on his own, so I'll just..."
Among them, the Yacht Club could be described as a small political arena that only students from prestigious families could join.
"have to..."
The gathering was once a month, and Gerhard, who valued connections, was naturally a member and attended regularly unless he had other business.
"go..."
That wasn't all. It was none other than he who had provided a luxury yacht to the club, which originally just held simple tea times, encouraging them to go out to sea.
"...I provided the ship, and a demon's minion disguised as a company employee snuck in to target Aint?"
No wonder Aint ruins me.
Gerhard's face distorted horribly.
***
While Gerhard, who had fainted and awakened, was fuming about demons...
Ding-
"Yes, welcome."
The bookstore owner, standing at the counter, greeted the customer.
"Do you have the book 'Basics of Cooking'?"
"You can find that in section C21."
"Thank you."
After searching for the book in that section for about five minutes, the customer returned to the counter.
"It doesn't seem to be there!"
"If it's not there, then all the displayed copies must have been sold. Wait, let me check in the storage room."
The bookstore owner went into the storage room at the back. The storage was full of books, and a strong musty paper smell wafted through.
"Let's see..."
That's when it happened. A black shadow suddenly rose behind him.
"I report to you."
The bookstore owner continued to search for the book without responding, but the shadow began its report regardless.
"According to our confirmation, Aint Armian never met Veriana Kalproten who was running wild due to demonic energy."
"And?"
"According to Your Excellency's original plan, the defeated Veriana Kalproten should have pursued Armian's mana, but it appears someone intervened in between."
"Intervention?"
The bookstore owner found and pulled out the "Basics of Cooking" book that was deeply shelved.
"We couldn't identify exactly who it was. The traces were thoroughly erased..."
It was because Gerhard, who anticipated the demons' tracking, had completely erased his traces.
"So you couldn't identify them?"
"...I apologize. I will try tracking again."
"No need. If you say that much, it must be unavoidable. It's not good to push too hard, so stop."
"I apologize."
"I was wondering why there was no mention of demonic energy at all, so that's what happened."
He lightly dusted off the book.
"No one should know about us... was it coincidence?"
If it wasn't coincidence, there was no explanation. To humans, demons were no different from legendary beings, and it was impossible for someone to know in advance and thwart his plans.
It was strange that there was no mention of demonic energy at all, but it was somewhat understandable if they didn't know it was demonic energy in the first place.
"Be careful from now on, but don't get too fixated. We can do better next time."
"...I will do my best."
"Aint Armian. We can't just leave him be."
For some reason, since entering the Academy, Aint Armian's growth rate had exceeded imagination.
He was convinced this was the arrangement of the first emperor.
"That cursed seed must have done something. It's obvious."
That's why he couldn't leave Aint Armian alone.
At first, he just wanted to test him, but everything was explained when the guy who was ranked 38th suddenly defeated Veriana Kalproten, who was ranked 2nd.
"Yes, that would be good."
"Please share your wise opinion."
"Lure Aint Armian out to sea. If successful, that cursed bloodline will disappear, and even if it fails, it could cause division in the Empire."
"Yes. I will follow your orders."
"We cannot yet handle the Empire, so it's most important not to be discovered. Don't disappoint me twice."
At those words, the shadow trembled slightly.
"...I will keep that in mind."
At his gesture, the shadow disappeared.
The bookstore owner, now alone, smiled again on his hardened face.
"Customer, I found the 'Basics of Cooking' book here."

chapters.title: Chapter 45: Traces of a Demon [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 45: Traces of a Demon [1]
The professors and administrators of the Academy held a meeting about how to handle the water dragon's carcass.
More precisely, it was a discussion about how to process the byproducts of the water dragon and who would receive the most benefits.
The body of a spirit creature like a water dragon was itself an enormous source of money and research materials.
"I believe I should have the largest share," Professor Grad from the Knight Department argued passionately.
"I drew the water dragon's attention from the front and inflicted critical wounds. Thanks to that, we were able to hunt the water dragon relatively easily."
No one could deny that he was the first to rush at the water dragon to prevent student casualties, and that he had faced the dragon head-on, leading to a relatively easy hunt.
But in the face of greed, such things became somewhat trivial.
"Wait a moment, Professor Grad. Without my lightning magic, the water dragon would have rampaged for much longer."
"It was my spear that pierced the water dragon's heart, Grad."
"If contribution is measured solely by who killed the dragon, I would be wronged, as I evacuated as many students as possible."
As the voices of the professors at the scene grew louder, the head of the General Affairs Department tried to calm them down.
"Isn't it more important to decide who to sell it to, how, and for how much, rather than distribution? We can divide it afterward."
"...That's not incorrect."
"I agree."
Since the value of a spirit creature's body decreases over time, some professors nodded in agreement.
"You'll handle that for us?"
"Of course. The sale will be in the Academy's name, so naturally we should step forward."
"And?"
"We don't ask for much. Just a small fee for our trouble..."
"That's absurd!"
"Stop this nonsense!"
While the General Affairs Department generally oversaw matters within the Academy, they couldn't claim rights to the byproducts of monsters that appeared during practical training.
The department head, who had tried to subtly step in, was rebuffed and folded his arms.
"But aren't you professors busy? Selling something like this isn't a trivial task and requires considerable effort."
"Hmph, the Academy is overflowing with nobles and wealthy families."
Even the wealthiest family on the continent had students at the Academy.
"No, wait. I don't want to sell it. I'd like to receive the byproducts directly."
"Me too. Especially the water dragon's mana hole..."
"Then buy it with money. At the market value."
"That's absurd!"
The professors were divided between those who wanted the byproducts distributed directly and those who wanted to sell them at the highest price possible before distributing the proceeds.
After quite some time, they finally reached a conclusion.
"Let's sell the water dragon's carcass to whoever offers the highest price. If you want the byproducts, pay more than that. The money will then be distributed to everyone according to their contribution."
"Let's do that."
The first contact priority was, of course, the Goldenheim family.
***
The sun rose. With the chirping of sparrows, Gerhard finally stretched, loosening his stiff body.
Knock knock-
"Come in."
"Did you not sleep at all?"
"I've always pictured it in my head, but when I actually try to create the blueprint, there are numerous obstacles."
Dozens of papers and empty ink bottles were scattered throughout Gerhard's room.
"Well, it is quite an ambitious project..."
A colossal golem reaching 10 meters in height.
Many parts of its body composed of mithril and adamant.
Functions that seemed almost godlike.
Plus an ego that could judge and move on its own.
There were numerous problematic areas.
"But it's a golem made of adamant and mithril. Without these functions, it would be a waste of ore, a white elephant."
"That's certainly true, but I wonder if an ego golem is really possible..."
An ego golem was something that had never appeared in this world.
If it had been possible, it would have been invented already, and if it did appear, it would be akin to a revolution in the magical world.
"Don't doubt. I have seen the possibility."
The proof was the Ego Sword of "Lord Gardner Alpenfassen" left by the first emperor.
If mithril, an ore that could contain even souls, could house a soul in a sword made from it, there was no reason it couldn't dwell in a golem.
"Certainly, I didn't know mithril had such potential..."
Magic dealing with souls was an exceedingly complex field to begin with.
"Assuming it's possible, what kind of soul and how will you insert it?"
That was the biggest issue in Hyde's view.
It was questionable whether there would be a soul that voluntarily wanted to become a golem, and if it was forcefully inserted, whether it would obey Gerhard was also a concern.
"I'll insert layers of obedience imprints. It's unthinkable that something I created would refuse my orders."
"If you insert the soul of a living person, the magical world might immediately label you a demon."
Occasionally there were madmen who ignored ethics and such, but like all organizations, the magical world also outwardly emphasized not crossing certain lines.
"Don't worry, would I just insert any soul?"
"...I still have a lot of life I want to live."
Hyde took a step back.
"...Don't talk nonsense."
"Then who are you thinking of?"
"A spirit."
Gerhard didn't even know magic that could capture and insert the soul of a living human.
Such talent didn't exist even within the vast network of the Goldenheim family. If such a thing were possible, it would likely be called a disaster rather than a talent.
But spirits were different.
They were soul entities to begin with, and they possessed a certain level of intelligence. One couldn't deny they were perfectly suited for an ego golem.
"...Indeed, with spirits there might be some possibility. But..."
Just then.
"Young Master."
A new visitor arrived. It was an employee of the Golden Turtle Company.
"What is it?"
"A visitor has come to the company."
"Visitor?"
"Well..."
Somehow, Gerhard felt like the scent of money was wafting through his nostrils.
***
"I expended a lot of effort for you, Gerhard. Everyone said the Goldenheims would drive down the price, but I said there was no way you would do that."
Gerhard quietly savored his coffee.
He had wondered what the conversation would be about when suddenly called to meet, but if it was this topic, he was always welcome.
"They accused me of taking money from you, but I told them it makes sense to sell to the wealthiest merchant."
"Indeed, you've never received money from me."
He had merely picked up a money pouch that had fallen in his house.
"Exactly. Those who don't properly understand keep saying I took money from you and all that, ugh."
Grad brazenly affirmed it.
Without such a thick face, he wouldn't have been able to continuously take money from Gerhard anyway.
"So to conclude, our family is the first choice, right?"
"Yes. I came as the Academy's representative."
"But is it appropriate to contact a student separately like this?"
At those words, Grad made a dumbfounded expression.
"That's rich coming from you, who contacts staff separately more than anyone."
"I wonder."
"The Academy has already officially sent a letter to the Goldenheim family."
This meant the meeting with Gerhard was a means to make the deal more certain.
"A water dragon. There are some parts I'm interested in."
"We're not selling it by parts. If you want to buy, you have to buy it all."
"Then that changes things a bit."

chapters.title: Chapter 46: Traces of a Demon [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 46: Traces of a Demon [2]
There was no particular reason why he couldn't.
Gerhard had already directly examined the water dragon's carcass as an assistant professor.
The teeth and bones were exceptionally hard, suitable for making weapons; the blood and eyes were rich in mana, good for reagents; and the scales could be made into armor or other defensive gear.
For a spirit creature with no wasted parts, it didn't matter much whether he bought all or part of it.
But there was no reason to give the impression of being dragged along.
"Let's not play games when we both know what's what. What do you want?"
"What does any merchant want? To get better goods at a cheaper price."
"Though limited to within the Academy, this is strictly speaking a kind of auction. I can't give it to you cheaper at my discretion."
Gerhard understood this as well. And he had anticipated this would happen once the water dragon's carcass was handed over to the Academy.
After all, the water dragon's carcass was coveted by magicians as magical material and by knights as material for weapons and armor.
He never intended to haggle from the start. He knew that if he tried to lower the price, he wouldn't be able to acquire it.
"But you can give something else, can't you?"
But there was no reason not to use this opportunity. While he couldn't save money, he could get something additional in return.
"...What do you want?"
"Exclusive rights."
"Exclusive rights?"
"If the Academy decides to purchase ships, I want an exclusive contract stating that they will only buy ships from the Golden Turtle Company."
"Ships, suddenly?"
It was sudden indeed. But for Gerhard, who had read the future, it wasn't sudden at all.
Monster attacks and a sunken yacht, with noble children adrift at sea.
After that incident, the Academy would realize that land battles weren't everything and would establish a naval combat course.
And naturally, that course would need ships.
'And it's not just a one-time sale.'
It would be a course focused on naval combat, seeking out monsters and engaging in battles.
Naturally, the ships would sustain continuous damage, leading to substantial repair costs.
If they were completely destroyed, new ships would need to be purchased... In other words, this was a long-term business with enormous interests at stake.
"...How many ships would the Academy buy anyway?"
The Academy itself didn't use that many ships. At most, just regular liners traveling across the continent.
But those ships traveled under the escort of the Imperial Navy, so there wasn't much need to frequently replace them.
"I'll handle that. Just sign the contract. Then I'll buy the water dragon's carcass at a suitably high price. And perhaps a money pouch might fall in your mansion."
It was a flow that couldn't possibly make sense, but Grad's eyes changed with greed.
"...I don't have the authority, but I'll suggest it to the Chancellor."
"Yes, thank you."
'Grad alone won't be enough; I'll need to use other connections to add pressure.'
Gerhard bowed his head.
***
"..."
"..."
A heavy silence hung in the air. Gerhard waited quietly until she spoke.
"It was an utterly incomprehensible action."
"Utterly?"
"Isn't it obvious? Skipping all classes to be a temporary assistant professor? There's no greater case of losing the big for the small."
Gerhard couldn't agree with Luina's words.
It wasn't losing the big for the small; it was gaining the big for the small. If he hadn't stepped forward, he wouldn't have obtained so much mithril and adamant.
'Ah, would I have obtained the mithril even if I hadn't gone?'
Perhaps even if things had flowed according to the original future, Aint might have sold the mithril to him due to the butterfly effect of the Saint Bird.
But whatever that future might have been, it was undeniable that the current result was much better.
"It was a necessary action. I needed to push myself to keep up with your grades."
"Don't try to gloss over it like that. Is it right to skip other classes to keep up with grades? What if there had been practicals or exams during that week?"
Gerhard and Luina were a pair.
From his perspective, it was natural for them to attend classes together: "Magical Survival Techniques," "Combat, War, and Magic," and "Exploration of Magical Beasts and Monsters." From her perspective, they should attend "Field Survival Techniques," "War and Practical Combat Techniques," and "Exploration of Magical Beasts and Monsters" together.
But with Gerhard disappearing for a week, Luina had lost her partner.
"It's fortunate there were no practicals, but what if there had been?"
"I considered all that before I went."
"Is that what matters?"
"...I apologize for not consulting with you in advance."
It was the truth, but Gerhard couldn't push back strongly. The reason was the same as with Aint.
Aint Armian was the hero who would save the world and the one who would cause his downfall, so he had to tread carefully, and Luina was the catalyst for that, so it was the same with her.
"Since no major problem occurred, I'll accept it. However, I hope there won't be such incidents in the future."
"I'll keep that in mind."
Fortunately, Luina easily accepted his apology.
"By the way, was there anything special while I was serving as a temporary assistant professor?"
"Nothing much. During the past week, most classes focused on theory."
When practicals took place for one year, it was common for professors and assistant professors from other years to step in and help.
Therefore, most second-year classes remained theoretical.
"Ah, there was one interesting thing."
"Interesting thing?"
"In the third-year duels, the top students from the Knight Department and Magic Department faced off."
"That must have caused a stir."
The Academy basically emphasized harmony and cooperation, but humans are inherently beings with a sense of belonging.
In a broader sense, they were all Academy students, but with different fields and departments, there was a certain competitive spirit between the Knight Department and Magic Department.
Even beyond the Academy, the competition between knights and magicians had a deep history.
"Yes. And the third-year Magic Department top student, senior Riana, defeated Barog, the top student from the Knight Department."
"Barog must have been labeled a traitor."
"Half-jokingly, he's also accused of match-fixing."
"Match-fixing? Was money wagered on the outcome?"
Gerhard tilted his head at the unexpected statement. Was there room for such things in a simple duel between the Knight Department and Magic Department?
'Betting pools were often set up for duels...'
He had facilitated gambling among students, but in a pride battle between the top students of the Magic and Knight Departments, there was no room for match-fixing.
At least, that's what he knew.
"...Your train of thought naturally goes in that direction?"
Gerhard didn't shy away from Luina's subtle gaze.
"Money is truth. Any means to earn it is right."
"I'm not particularly interested in your values. And it's not about gambling anyway."
"Then why mention match-fixing?"
"Apparently, the top students of the Knight Department and Magic Department are lovers. So questions are circulating about whether he deliberately lost."
"...Now that's an interesting issue."
Since there had been no update in his information network about lovers, it must have been recent.
'The Hermim family is quite wealthy, and Barog Hermim tends to be a spendthrift.'
If actively recommended jewelry or expensive artifacts, he would likely buy several without much difficulty.
'I should try suggesting it.'
There was nothing as lucrative as selling to nobles.
"And now for the main point."
"Speak."
This meeting was the first arranged by Luina herself.
She had called Gerhard saying she had something to discuss, and he didn't think the main purpose was to blame him for disappearing for a week as an assistant professor without notice.
"I believe I've found traces of a demon."
"...What did you say?"
While he hadn't anticipated such a matter in his wildest dreams.

chapters.title: Chapter 47: Zweihänder’s Shadow [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 47: Zweihänder's Shadow [1]
"...I think I must have misheard."
"You heard correctly."
"You found traces of a demon? When exactly?"
"Exactly three days ago, after dinner. Around 7 PM. I was engaged in a duel requested by a classmate. During that, her power suddenly surged."
Luina answered calmly.
"Who?"
"Bella Hoenne."
"Second-year Knight Department, ranked 19th, daughter of Viscount Hoenne. A wealthy family."
The Hoenne viscounty was a prosperous territory and one of the main clients of the Golden Turtle Company.
"What do you mean by her power surging?"
"Exactly that. Not just physical strength, but the amount of aura suddenly increased."
"That's not enough."
Tap tap, Gerhard's fingers drummed on the armrest.
"Any physical changes?"
"None."
"Since she wouldn't take drugs and cause a scene in a duel, it's likely the effect of an aura cultivation method."
"Are you saying I'm mistaken?"
"Could it be that you're too fixated on the weight of the word 'demon'?"
"I felt demonic energy for an instant."
"...Now that changes things."
Gerhard uncrossed his legs.
"Any other witnesses?"
"None. Only the two of us were in the dueling room."
"Are you sure it was demonic energy?"
"It was an extremely faint energy and very momentary, but that unique ominousness is not easily forgotten. Of course, I can't be absolutely certain."
Luina's voice trailed off at the end. She herself had some lingering doubts.
"As far as I know, Bella Hoenne is your friend. One of your two closest friends along with Aina Lium."
"...How do you know that?"
"That's not what's important. I'm asking if you're being overly sensitive because she is your friend."
"...Honestly, I can't say that's not the case."
Luina couldn't be sure if it was truly demonic energy.
It was extremely faint, it was extremely brief, and there was not a single reason why her friend Bella Hoenne would make a contract with something like a demon.
"Bella is a diligent student. She's always enthusiastic about classes and training, and she likes books, so she frequently visits the library and bookstores."
"And?"
"I searched for information about demons in the library, and I learned that demons target vulnerabilities in the heart. But Bella is always cheerful and has a good relationship with her family. I can't imagine how she would have come into contact with a demon."
Nevertheless, having witnessed the case of Veriana, and aware that demons were once again manifesting in this world, Luina had come to Gerhard.
To verify it for sure. Because she didn't want to believe it.
"Tell me exactly what happened."
"...Well..."
***
That day was no different from any other.
"Luina!"
She attended classes as usual, and classes ended as usual.
"Would you like to have a duel today?"
"Anytime."
And she dueled with a friend. It wasn't a frequent occurrence, but it wasn't particularly rare either.
"Today will be a bit different."
"Oh?"
"Yes. I've been feeling my skills improving lately."
In the dueling arena prepared for student duels, Luina and Bella faced each other with swords drawn.
They were using real swords, not wooden ones, and had put on armor for safety.
"Did you bring a safety scroll?"
"Yes."
The safety scroll was a necessary item for dueling with real swords, activating a magic barrier when an impact beyond a certain level was delivered.
"I'll go first."
Bella's hand tensed on her sword. Her weapon was a Zweihänder, as long and massive as her height.
Rather than nimble thrusts or slashes, it was a sword perfectly suited for her style, which used weight and strength to crush opponents.
The massive Zweihänder began to move, cutting through the air.
Instead of avoiding the approaching sword, Luina moved to meet it.
—!
'The strength...?'
A heavy impact traveled through the sword.
It was different from before. Her sword had become heavier and more powerful than before.
Realizing that Bella's claim about feeling her skills improve wasn't a lie, Luina's gaze became more serious.
Kagagak-
She twisted her wrist to deflect the Zweihänder. Just as she was about to thrust at the clearly exposed opening, Bella quickly retreated.
'She's fast.'
It wasn't just her strength. Her speed was also different from before.
After one clash, a moment of peace arrived.
"How is it?"
"...It's definitely different from before. Heavier and faster."
"I thought so, right?"
Bella smiled brightly.
"Lately I've been feeling like I can control my body better. Like I'm overflowing with strength? But hearing it directly from you makes me feel even better."
She took her stance again.
"Then I'll go again."
"Yes."
—!
Sword clashed against sword.
There was no sense of testing the waters. Bella advanced with full power from the start, and Luina had to match her.
—!
A shockwave erupted. A faint aura wrapped around Bella's Zweihänder.
Instead of being flustered, Luina forged her own blue aura to counter it.
'I can't win with strength.'
From the beginning, Bella's aura cultivation method was focused on physical destructive power to match her swordsmanship. A head-on confrontation would be a bad move.
In the midst of a storm of sword strikes, Luina calmly evaded them.
"As expected of Luina!"
With that brief exclamation, the power imbued in the sword doubled. Feeling her wrists and arms becoming increasingly numb, Luina sensed there was a limit to how much she could evade.
Kagagak-
As she deflected the sword, Luina kicked Bella in the abdomen. She stepped back, and Luina immediately followed.
The massive Zweihänder was effective for destructive swordsmanship that utilized its weight, but conversely, its size posed clear limitations in extremely close combat.
But at that moment.
—!
The raised Zweihänder bent at a strange angle to block the space between them.
Luina's sword shook violently, and fragments of shattered aura flew in all directions.
The massive shockwave pushed Luina back.
"How...?"
It was different again from before. Especially the aura, which felt rougher and gave off a strange feeling. Unsettling yet somehow familiar.
'Like...'
"I won't go down easily!"
Red aura surged up, enveloping not just the sword but Bella's entire body.
Luina's train of thought was interrupted. The strange feeling she had briefly sensed was no longer perceptible, as if it had been an illusion.
——!
The sword strike, which she narrowly evaded, struck the ground, causing the solid dueling arena floor to cave in.
"It's hard to control."
"...Bella. Did you take a spirit potion or something?"
"I've certainly taken some. Seems like it's finally showing results."
Bella smiled as she readied her sword.
"I'll go again."
***
"...That's what happened."
"So for a moment her aura output increased, and you felt a faint demonic energy."
"At first, I didn't think of it as demonic energy. But the more I reflected on the situation... I started to think it might have been demonic energy."
Bella Hoenne is ranked 19th. While certainly not lacking, there was a clear difference in level between her and Luina.

chapters.title: Chapter 48: Zweihänder’s Shadow [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 48: Zweihänder's Shadow [2]
It was definitely strange that this gap had narrowed drastically in such a short time.
"How is Bella's condition?"
"She's fine. Unlike Veriana, there were no visible abnormalities in her body, and she didn't lose her sanity. There were no special abnormalities after the duel either."
"Is that so?"
"It could have simply been my misunderstanding or misperception, but..."
Gerhard cut off her words.
"But you want to check properly just in case?"
"Yes. It's not just anything, but a demon."
"I agree. If there's something strange, it should be checked."
Honestly, Gerhard had thought he could easily learn about demons by capturing Veriana.
But that wasn't the case. Even after investigating Veriana, known to be a demon's minion, or directly questioning her after her demonization, nothing substantial emerged.
"...I shouldn't be saying this as the one asking for help, but do you have a method?"
"No."
Still, it was right to try everything possible.
Assuming Bella was indeed using demonic power, there was one commonality between Veriana and Bella.
They both neither met a demon nor made a contract.
"It seems to have seeped in without her knowledge. Honestly, I question if that's possible, but let's investigate by comparing their paths and looking for common places they visited."
"That's the best we can do in the current situation. Thank you for your help."
"The problem of demons is a continent-wide issue. Of course I should help."
"Then I'll go to Bella and..."
"No, there's no need for that. Everything will come out by tomorrow. For now, go back. I'll call you again tomorrow."
After sending Luina away, Gerhard called Hyde.
"I'll find all of Bella Hoenne's past movements."
"Veriana's too. Even before you started following her."
"Yes."
Subsequently, it took less than a day for a detailed report of both their movements since the start of the academic year to be placed on Gerhard's desk.
"...Dormitory, Academy, downtown."
"Yes, at the Academy it's mostly just classrooms, dueling rooms, and the library, and downtown it's just restaurants and bookstores."
"The same as that Veriana fellow."
But there was nothing strange about that. Students who didn't live this kind of life were rather rare.
It was the extremely ordinary daily life of an Academy student.
"I'd like you to arrange a meeting with Luina and Bella."
"Have you found a clue?"
"No, because there are none, I want to meet her directly."
He could have just dismissed it as coincidence. But a deep unease remained in Gerhard's mind.
Of course, the possibility that it was nothing was higher.
However, having confirmed the existence of demons through the prophecy book and through Veriana, if there was even a small possibility for Bella, it was right to verify it for sure.
After all classes ended, Gerhard met Bella with Luina at a café.
"Gerhard? Why are you here...?"
"Bella Hoenne. It's the first time we're meeting like this, having arranged a separate place. I asked Luina."
"You wanted to meet me? Why?"
"It's nothing special. Luina..."
—!
At that moment, a roaring sound echoed in Gerhard's head.
Along with terrible pain, dormant prophecies surged in.
A sky red like blood, terrible stench and demonic energy.
Gerhard felt a sense of familiarity with this situation. It was the same as that day, when he saw the prophecy about Andromalius.
The Academy was no different from hell.
In the distance, a magic circle red like blood emitted light, and monsters and humans who had lost their sanity were rampaging everywhere.
They were students. People from the Academy. Residents of the island.
Aint's surprised face was visible.
["Everyone is strange!"
Not just students, but Academy staff and island residents too.
Demonic energy that had been unknowingly absorbed had been dormant in the students' bodies, and with the advent of the demon Andromalius, it began to activate.
There were easily hundreds of them.]
[- It's demonic energy! They're infected with demonic energy!
"Are you saying the students made contracts with a demon?"
Nevertheless, students infected with demonic energy were making the Academy even more chaotic.]
Time accelerated.
Aint was placing his hand on the chest of a fallen student.
[Aint followed Gardner's instructions and injected mana into the fallen student to examine their interior.
The First Noble Knight, who had slaughtered more demons than anyone except the Empire's first emperor, finally figured out the cause after much consideration.
]
The surroundings changed again abruptly.
Aint was suddenly running toward the source of the ominous demonic energy, the red magic circle.
[- Goodness. That's not just a demonic energy triggering circle! That's...! A summoning circle! A summoning circle!
]
The cry of Lord Gardner Alpenfassen struck Aint's head.
And again, the flow accelerated. Aint was closer to the magic circle than before, and he met a knight he could trust with his back.
["Aint! Help me! Bella, Bella!
"Calm down, senior. It will be fine."
"Bella is strange!"
"She's infected with demonic energy. If we defeat the demon, she can return to normal. I will make sure of it."]
["Absolutely."]
'So it really was demonic energy...?'
He had suspected it, but wasn't certain.
But the prophecy book was telling him. Luina's anxiety was correct, and if those infected with demonic energy were left unchecked, a great calamity would occur.
'This connects to what came before.'
More precisely, it was the story of a time before then. Before Aint fought Andromalius, and before Luina turned her back to him and made the knight's oath.
'I must prevent it.'
The Academy in his memory was complete chaos. Since the infected humans were students or island residents, they couldn't bring themselves to kill them, which caused even greater damage.
That situation had to be prevented at all costs.
"...Gerhard? Are you okay?"
"Is your head hurting again?"
"I'm fine."
Gerhard blinked a couple of times and shook his head.
After enduring the gaze of two pairs of eyes on him, he took a moment to catch his breath and organize his thoughts.
"Luina."
"Yes."
"How much can you trust Bella Hoenne?"
"She's a friend I've been with since childhood. I trust her the most."
"What are you two suddenly talking about?"
Bella asked about their unexpected conversation.
"Bella Hoenne, the reason I asked Luina to arrange this meeting..."
Originally, he had planned to just meet her directly and conduct an investigative inquiry. Even though Luina trusted Bella, just to be sure.
But after confirming the prophecy book, his thoughts and plans changed.
"is because your head is full of demons."
"What?"
"There's a need to beat those demons to death."
With clear evidence before his eyes, the solution was also clear.
"Let's go to the temple."
To show evidence to those who cannot coexist with demons and collaborate with them.

chapters.title: Chapter 49: Gray Crystal [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 49: Gray Crystal [1]
"...What nonsense are you talking about? Demons?"
Bella made an incredulous expression.
"Gerhard!"
Luina was also startled by the sudden escalation. But Gerhard paid no attention.
"Luina, leave this entirely to me."
"...You're saying you can tell just by looking once?"
"I've found definite evidence."
"Really?"
"No, what are you two talking about right now?"
"Bella Hoenne."
Gerhard's voice dropped lower.
"I understand this is confusing. Demons, being possessed by demonic energy. It sounds absurd."
Bella's gaze grew increasingly fierce, as if questioning whether he truly understood.
"But you need to trust me completely."
"That's such nonsense..."
"If you can't trust me, trust your friend, Luina Berchef. Has she ever harmed you or told you meaningless lies?"
"...Well, that's true."
Demons.
Bella suspected that her good friend might have fallen for Gerhard's serpent-like tongue and was saying strange things.
Honestly, that seemed most plausible.
"No."
"What?"
"I didn't brainwash Luina."
"...How did you...?"
"That's right, Bella. Am I the type of person who would fall for such things?"
"That may be true, but demons... My head is full of demons? It's strange. How can someone say such things boldly without being insane?"
Although demons had not appeared for a thousand years, causing humanity to forget much about them, they were still objects of fear.
Monsters that nearly destroyed the continent.
Evil beings warned about by the first emperor.
The Judges, who remained even though they had become nominal, were proof of this.
"I say it boldly because I think your head is full of demons."
"You must both have gone mad. There's no other explanation, right?"
"Whether we're mad or not can be determined at the temple."
"Why go to the temple, of all places...!"
"Because the temple's magicians are more sensitive to demonic energy than anyone else."
The holy power that appears in novels and plays, said to be the antithesis of demonic energy, didn't actually exist.
However, the Dragon Faith Order had crossed an irreversible river with demons over the position of mastery in magic, and a thousand years ago, they were more zealous than anyone in eradicating demons.
That stance continued to this day, and they had steadily developed artifacts and magic to search for demons. If asked to name those who could best find demons in this world, Gerhard would definitely choose the Dragon Faith Order.
"If they find demonic energy in your body, we're right. If not, you're right."
Then I will formally apologize. Gerhard declared.
"I stake the name of Gerhard Goldenheim on it."
"...Isn't the head of a person who claims to apologize too stiff?"
"Because I haven't done anything wrong yet."
"..."
"Bella, just once."
"Luina..."
Honestly, Bella couldn't understand the current situation at all. Everything was out of the blue and ridiculous.
She was told she'd made a contract with demons when she'd never even seen one.
'Could this be a demon's prank?'
Maybe she was actually sleeping in bed, and everything was a nightmare created by a demon.
Bella unconsciously pinched her cheek.
"That won't make it a dream."
"...Unnecessarily perceptive."
Rubbing her sore cheek, she asked.
"What will you do if demonic energy is really there?"
"Purify it. There's no other way, and I don't intend to hand you over to the Judges. Ah, we'll need to investigate your activities though."
"My activities?"
"We need to know where the demonic energy seeped in to deal with it."
"Haven't you already investigated?"
"Shh, Luina. Being quiet in times like this is helping."
"...I see."
'...When did these two become so close?'
Bella let out a hollow laugh at the sight of the two whispering loud enough for all to hear, like a comedy duo.
Despite the seriousness of the conversation, honestly, it didn't feel real.
How could anyone easily believe that demons and demonic energy, which had been absent for the past thousand years, would suddenly appear?
"...Fine. Let's go. I have nothing to hide. But if nothing is found, you'll need to apologize to Luina too."
"To Luina?"
"Yes. For seducing innocent Luina and getting her involved in your strange actions."
"There's a slight discrepancy in your words, but if that's what you want, I will."
Screech, Bella roughly pushed her chair back and stood up.
"Well, is there anything more to drag out? If you want it so badly, let's go right now."
"Wait a moment."
"What now?"
Gerhard pointed to the half-filled cups.
"Even if we're leaving, finish what's left. This coffee is made with the finest beans from Mount Argond."
Slurp, he savored his coffee.
***
"Was what I saw really correct?"
Luina was following behind Bella, keeping a slight distance alongside Gerhard.
"Yes. You saw correctly, and your friend is contaminated with demonic energy. Of course, it's extremely faint, so it's not like Veriana's case where she lost her sanity."
Nevertheless, traces of demonic energy remained. This was because, unlike Veriana who had resolved everything, it was accumulating gradually.
"If it's true, then Bella..."
"That won't happen. She didn't make a direct contract with a demon; she was infected without knowing. That's also why we're going to the Order instead of the Judges, to prepare for any eventuality."
While there was room to negotiate with the apostles of the Dragon Faith Order, it wasn't the case with the Judges.
Those who existed to destroy demons had become nominal because demons didn't exist, but they were capable of doing anything to regain power.
There were even precedents where Judges had fabricated fake demons.
If Bella was taken to the Judges and demonic energy was discovered, she would definitely be a dead person.
Naturally, this would sour relations with Luina, and Aint would be added to the mix.
From Gerhard's perspective, that was something he wanted to avoid.
'Bella must live. She must live, discover the demonic energy, and serve as evidence.'
For Luina, for Gerhard who needed Luina's favor, and for the continent.
"...Thank you."
"There's nothing to thank me for."
"Stop whispering, you two. Is this really the right way?"
Bella stopped walking, folded her arms, and asked bluntly.
"You said we were going to the temple, but why are we suddenly visiting all the places I usually go to first?"

chapters.title: Chapter 50: Gray Crystal [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 50: Gray Crystal [2]
If she hadn't met or made a direct contract with a demon, there was a high probability that demonic energy was present in a specific location or had seeped in through contact with a specific object.
'If we discover the medium of demonic energy in Bella's activities, that would be best.'
Of course, it would be fine even if they didn't.
However, if they discovered something that injected demonic energy in her activities, it would be more certain when she was examined at the Dragon Faith Order.
"Just do as you're told."
Of course, there was no reason to explain this openly on the street where people were walking around.
"Is that what you call an explanation?"
"Please, Bella. Just this once."
"...Seriously, Luina. You and I need to have a talk after this is over."
"Anytime."
Grumbling, Bella entered the bookstore. The characteristic smell of paper permeated the air.
"Welcome."
The clerk greeted them with a bright smile, and Gerhard and Luina followed Bella, peering around various parts of the bookstore.
'Nothing special here either.'
But he mentally checked it. He wasn't particularly sensitive to mana, so it could simply be that he wasn't sensing it.
"You come here often. Have you finished reading the book I recommended last time?"
"Yes. It was quite interesting. Especially the ending of Adran and Hela left a strong impression."
"If you'd like, I can recommend other books as well."
"I'd love that."
After Gerhard had circled the bookstore once and came out, Bella was talking with the bookstore owner.
"Book recommendations?"
"Bella enjoys reading romance novels."
"A common hobby."
Gerhard's gaze, which had been on the back of Bella's head, shifted absently to the bookstore owner. He was an ordinary person with no particular peculiarities.
When their eyes met, the owner seemed slightly surprised, as if recognizing Gerhard, but soon he bowed his head.
"Nice to meet you, Mr. Gerhard."
"You know me?"
"From a business perspective, I can't not know you, Mr. Gerhard. I also frequently receive goods from the Golden Turtle Company."
"So you're a customer."
"You came with your friends. Would you like me to recommend a book for you too, Mr. Gerhard?"
Gerhard shook his head. Since most decent books were already available in the company and his family, there was no need to buy them.
Or he could just go to the Academy library.
"That's a pity. There's a book I think you'd like."
"I'll look at it next time when there's an opportunity."
"Yes, please do visit again."
With the bookstore as the last stop, their tour of Bella's daily routine was complete.
"Follow me."
"This isn't the direction to the temple."
"It would be troublesome if your demonic energy was revealed openly when we went to the temple, wouldn't it?"
"Is it right to assume I'm infected with demonic energy from the start? I've never met a demon and my mind isn't strange."
After going around in circles, they arrived back at the original café.
"Why are we back here?"
"Follow me."
Specifically, it was the fifth floor of the café. There was a sealed room that Gerhard always used when meeting Luina.
"You've arrived, Brother."
There was already a guest in the sealed room.
"You're early."
"I always come running right away when you call, Brother."
"You must be excited at the thought of making money."
"With money, the Order can flourish more."
Everything according to the Dragon's will. Janice briefly pressed her palms together.
"But there's someone here I haven't seen before."
"Janice Biance?"
Bella and Janice recognized each other a beat late. Instead of introducing them to each other, Gerhard continued the conversation.
"Yes, instead of going to the temple, we'll verify through Janice. Janice, you brought it, right?"
"Of course. I guarantee there's nothing as certain as our Dragon Faith Order's items when it comes to searching for demonic energy or demons. We've been developing them steadily for a thousand years."
Demons had disappeared, but the Dragon Faith Order had always been prepared. This was due to the first pope's prophecy that demons would return someday.
"So it can sense all demonic energy? Even if there's just a tiny bit of demonic energy on the roadside?"
"Brother, do you have no conscience?"
Janice let out a hollow laugh.
"Unless it's adequately concentrated, it's impossible to find without contact or manipulation. At least with current magical technology."
"That's unfortunate."
If it could detect all surrounding demonic energy, they could find the source of where it seeped in.
"But did you really sense demonic energy? Why suddenly this...?"
"There's a person infected with demonic energy."
"Who is... Could it be this person?"
"Yes."
Janice tilted her head in disbelief.
"I don't feel anything."
"That's why I told you to bring that artifact."
"Did she really make a contract with a demon?"
"She didn't make a contract with a demon."
"Then why are you certain there's demonic energy?"
"That's exactly what I want to know."
Janice and Bella glared at Gerhard with identical expressions. Instead of answering, Gerhard folded his arms and nodded.
"We just need to try it and see."
"I don't mind since you're paying for the artifact, but this seems like an overreaction on your part, Brother."
Inside the wooden box that Janice took out from her bosom was a transparent crystal ball.
Countless tiny rune characters were inscribed on the surface of the clear orb.
"Since the person paying is telling me to do it, I will. You there...?"
"Call me Bella."
"Senior Bella Hoenne, I see. Feel free to speak comfortably. Could you hold the crystal ball with both hands?"
Bella placed both hands on the crystal ball. As Janice held the opposite side, the rune characters on the crystal ball began to emit light.
"Mana will seep in and observe your interior. Please don't resist."
"That's easy. Let's finish quickly and receive an apology."
Mana enveloped Bella's entire body, and she swallowed a groan at the unfamiliar sensation.
"...Can that reveal it?"
"Theoretically. If that can't reveal it, nothing can."
Aint Armian and Lord Gardner Alpenfassen might have other methods, but at least for now, that was the case.
"I shouldn't be saying this as the one who created this situation, but I truly hope nothing happens."
"We'll see."
With Gerhard's ambiguous answer, the mana that had explored Bella's entire body returned to the crystal ball.
At that moment.
Woong-
With a faint vibration, the previously transparent crystal ball slowly turned gray.
It wasn't very intense. It was so faint that one might overlook it without focused attention.
But what was important was that it had changed.
"..."
After staring at it for a moment, Janice made the sign of the cross and began to pray.
"Great Dragon God, today I send you one wicked evil being who dared to accept a demon by your side, please look down upon your servant."
"...What?"
"...Hmm?"
Whoosh, flames flickered in Janice's hand.
"Here comes one, Dragon God!"
———!
An explosion occurred.

chapters.title: Chapter 51: Sacred Light [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 51: Sacred Light [1]
As long as demons go around claiming to be the masters of magic, the Dragon Faith Order is an organization that can never coexist with them.
A religion whose very existence is denied cannot survive.
Therefore, the Dragon Faith Order’s hatred of demons was, in some ways, similar to that of the Judges.
But even so, no one expected them to suddenly cast magic like this.
"...I, I’m innocent!"
As the explosion subsided and the smoke cleared.
There stood Janice with her hand of flame extended, Luina blocking it with her sword, and Bella who had collapsed on the floor screaming, her legs having given out.
"Well done, Luina."
Gerhard sighed as he caught Janice’s wrist. Even he hadn’t anticipated this situation.
"Stop, Janice."
"Brother, she’s an evil being. An evil being who made a contract with a demon is openly attending the Imperial Academy... I never dreamed I would see such a thing in my life. The only good evil being is a dead evil being. Let me make Senior Bella Hoenne a good evil being."
"I said stop."
Gerhard growled low.
"Even if it’s you, Brother, when it comes to demons..."
"I was the one who knew this first and asked you for the artifact."
"...That’s true, but."
"I guarantee that Bella Hoenne has neither met a demon nor made a contract with one."
According to the prophecy book, Bella was merely a victim.
And the prophecy book had not lied to Gerhard, at least not so far.
"But there was demonic energy."
"You don’t necessarily have to make a contract with a demon for demonic energy to exist. There’s also the case of infection. You should know that."
"Are you saying there’s someone in the Academy infecting students?"
Janice’s eyebrows twitched. Though she framed it as "someone," that someone would definitely be demon followers.
"Isn’t that an even bigger problem? We should immediately inform the Order and the Empire... but you think they would go into hiding and become impossible to find?"
"Yes. I’ve already made extensive efforts to find those spreading demonic energy."
He had thoroughly examined the daily routines of Bella and Veriana, and through Hyde, searched places likely to contain demonic energy, but no answers emerged.
"That’s why I came to you."
"To borrow the power of the Dragon Faith Order?"
"Because the Dragon Faith Order seems least likely to be connected to demon followers."
Even if demon followers were hiding throughout the continent, the Empire, and even the Academy, the place that would hold out the longest would naturally be the Dragon Faith Order.
Because they had deeply rooted hatred for demons.
Of course, someone might exploit that blind spot to hide, but if we’re that suspicious, there’s not a single trustworthy person in this world.
"I already believe that evil beings are hiding all over the Academy."
It was clear. Otherwise, the riots when Andromalius descended couldn’t be explained.
’There were easily hundreds who were infected and went berserk.’
He didn’t know exactly when Andromalius’s descent would happen.
However, he felt it would be impossible for a small number of people to infect so many without being detected by anyone.
"Their goal is probably to use those infected with demonic energy to destroy the Academy from within."
"Why would they do that?"
"Because the Academy is where the future of the Empire, and by extension, the continent, resides. If this place is trampled, the future disappears."
Janice understood.
"But if that’s the case, shouldn’t we block it in advance? Even considering they might go into hiding, it seems better to prevent problems from occurring at the Academy."
It was a reasonable opinion. It would be better than letting the future of the continent be fatally wounded, even if it meant the evil beings would hide deeper.
But Gerhard knew the future. A future where demons eventually descend in large numbers and the entire continent is engulfed in war.
"But wouldn’t it be better if we could uproot them with minimal damage?"
If the evil beings escape, they will return as an even greater calamity.
Even if the saplings suffer a little damage, it’s better to uproot them to prevent the great tree from falling.
"Do you have a method?"
"I have something in mind."
After hearing the full explanation, Janice understood.
"But wouldn’t it be better to confess to the Order and get help?"
"I didn’t say don’t talk about it. Just don’t make it public. Share it only with a select few you absolutely trust, and maintain maximum security."
"Alright."
Khuhu, Janice smiled sinisterly.
"A method to backstab those evil beings. As expected of you, Brother. I’ll gladly follow."
"Before that, do you happen to have magic or artifacts that can eliminate demonic energy?"
"Of course. All magicians in the Order learn a magic called ’Sacred Light’ that burns demonic energy."
It was the duty of an Order that could not coexist with demons.
"Good. Erase the demonic energy in that person’s body."
"Ah, yes. Bella, faithful one, would you extend your hand?"
"...You won’t kill me, right?"
"Of course not. The Order punishes demons and evil beings, not innocent victims."
The saint smiled benevolently. Having gone through many unexpected things, Bella obediently extended her hand.
"Oh, but since this is my first time using this magic, I’m not sure how it will go. I wonder if it will work... Is it okay to burn the interior of a living person?"
"...What?"
Bella’s startled question was cut short.
——!
Hot heat and pain surged from within Bella.
"Kyaaaaaah!"
"Hmm, it seems extremely painful."
"This sealed room is perfectly soundproof, so there’s no need to worry."
It was a special sealed room that absorbed not just sound but all vibrations and impacts.
"Pain accompanies the punishment of evil, so this too is the natural order. Please feel free to scream as much as you want, cursing the demon that made you like this."
"..."
Luina could only stare blankly as her friend collapsed, foaming at the mouth.
***
"Whew, perhaps because it’s my first time using this magic on a person, it was quite difficult. Well, I’ll be going first. I’ll conduct my own investigation too."
"Alright."
After all the treatment was finished, Janice left first, leaving Bella unconscious and slumped over the table.
"...Is she going to be okay?"
"Probably."

chapters.title: Chapter 52: Sacred Light [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 52: Sacred Light [2]
When he brought his finger to her nose, she was still breathing. Although her complexion was a bit pale, she didn’t look life-threateningly ill.
"Take her to Bless Hall."
"I will."
"Apply red makeup to make it look like she’s drunk."
"Do we have to go that far? If she returns heavily drunk in broad daylight, Bella’s dignity..."
"No one even imagined that evil beings could be hiding in the Academy. There’s no harm in being cautious."
Ah, and since she needs to smell like alcohol, sprinkle some on her face too. Gerhard started to take out a rather expensive wine from the storage cabinet in a corner of the sealed room but hesitated.
"Since we’re just spraying it on her body, it doesn’t need to be premium quality."
"How much does that cost..."
"It’s 20 gold."
"They sell cheap wine at taverns."
Gerhard called someone to buy a bottle of wine. Luina prepared to carry Bella.
"Do you have a spare robe? No matter what, we should at least cover her face as much as possible."
"There is."
A clerk brought a robe, and Luina covered Bella with it.
"By the way, since when have you been thinking about this plan?"
"Since I found traces of evil beings through Veriana. They wouldn’t end it with just one attempt."
"Don’t forget your promise."
"Promise?"
"You promised to lend a hand whenever dealing with demons."
Luina’s eyes sank coldly.
"I won’t leave alone the evil beings who dared to endanger Bella."
"Yes."
Shortly after, Luina sprinkled the wine that the clerk had bought all over Bella’s body, then carried her away.
"...Using Janice and the Order’s power to erase the demonic energy from all infected humans. As discreetly as possible."
This way, the chaos the evil beings desired could be minimized.
"The best would be to prevent the demon’s descent itself..."
Unless the prophecy book revealed more, he still didn’t have a sense of how to do that.
"For now, I need to focus on what’s next."
The Yacht Club. That’s where the evil beings will begin their full-scale activities.
On the yacht owned by the Golden Turtle Company, which Gerhard lends to the club free of charge and operates, someone disguised as an employee of the Golden Turtle Company attempts to kill Aint.
"In the end, cooperation with Aint is essential to stop the demons."
But suddenly bringing up demons would be nothing short of madness. It would be fortunate if it didn’t arouse Aint’s suspicion.
"All matters require preliminary work."
The demons will try to kill Aint or at least isolate him from the students through this incident, but the opposite will happen.
Aint will live, and Gerhard will openly become his patron.
"While investigating suspicious individuals who had infiltrated the company, I discovered they had infiltrated as yacht staff. But I didn’t know they were evil beings."
That’s how they’ll come to witness the evil beings together with Aint.
Diving into the detailed settings would make it much more complex, but to summarize, it was like this. Knowing the future made setting the stage not too difficult.
Gerhard’s eyes sank coldly.
***
<Why are you suddenly shivering?>
’No, I just felt a sudden chill.’
Aint shook off the sudden chill and focused again on the lecture.
"So this creature called a cyclops, despite having only one eye..."
The subject was "Exploration of Magical Beasts and Monsters." It was a mandatory course and an important five-point subject.
<How’s your physical condition?>
’Not bad.’
Perhaps thanks to his struggle against the formidable water dragon for survival, he had digested nearly half of the residual magical power from the Saint Bird’s heart, which he couldn’t fully absorb even with Lord Gardner’s help.
<A blessing in disguise. You got adamant, replenished magical power.>
’And I also gained a reliable patron.’
<Rather than a patron, it was a transaction in the end.>
<Just don’t let your guard down. Although adamant is valuable, those nouveau riche will try to drive down the price as much as possible.>
Aint was aware of this point. While he had approached them humbly, it would be a mistake to expect much consideration.
<The best approach is to make those nouveau riche aware of the gravity of the situation... They’re not fools, so if they sense danger to themselves, they’ll open their purse strings.>
’Then the best would be to let Senior Gerhard directly witness the existence of demons. But do demons really exist?’
Aint had never seen demons or their followers, not after obtaining Gardner, not even in his entire life.
<I’d prefer they didn’t exist, but they’re definitely operating covertly. My awakening is proof of that.>
Gardner asserted.
<Back to the main point, it’s not a bad idea. If it’s demons, even the Goldenheims will recognize the seriousness of the situation.>
<...Though not all of them would.>
’What do you mean by that?’
<People often say of a ruthless merchant that he’s ’one who would sell goods even to demons.’ The original of that saying is the Goldenheim family. The Goldenheim clan actually sold goods to demons.>
’...Good heavens.’
Aint was shocked. He knew the Goldenheim merchants were terrible, but he never dreamed they would sell to demons.
<Now do you understand why I dislike the Goldenheims?>
’I understand.’
Listening to various stories, the lecture time quickly ended. Someone approached Aint as he was organizing his textbooks.
"Aint."
"Balrosi."
"What are you doing after the lecture?"
"I don’t have any specific plans. Just training, I guess?"
"Always diligent."
Balrosi smiled good-naturedly.
<This guy is quite peculiar. I can tell he’s a good person, but I can’t understand why he’s so kind to you.>
’Honestly, I wonder about that too.’
Balrosi Viston was clearly a good person. But one couldn’t simply avoid suspicion just because someone was good.
Especially since Aint carried the Armian name, and the current emperor bore the Schwaben name.
Why would the heir to the Viston family not be wary of the Schwaben imperial family?
’Of course, the Viston family is almost on par with the imperial family...’
But there would still be discord, so why approach despite that?
He wondered why Balrosi was building a friendship with Aint, who had nothing but the faded glory of his family.
But he couldn’t ask directly, so he could only ponder it internally.
"Then would you like to come somewhere with me after this?"
"Where?"
Balrosi took out a small note. It was an invitation.
"You haven’t joined a club yet, right?"
"Not yet."
Clubs were gatherings of students encouraged by the Academy. Typically, students with similar interests gathered for hobbies or academics.
"Yacht Club?"
"Yes. It’s a place where you can only join with a recommendation from an existing member. With an invitation, you can bring one person along."
He explained that the main members of the club were children of prestigious nobles or merchant companies.
"I received an invitation for this month’s gathering recently, and if possible, I’d like to go together with you."
"With me?"
"Yes."
<From your perspective, it’s a den of tigers. He wants you to go to such a place together? Is this guy crazy?>
Gardner was right. Most high nobles were wary of Armian because they were mindful of Schwaben.
Moreover, the prince of Schwaben was also in the Yacht Club.
<Still, it might not be bad to go once.>
<The late emperor left an arrangement near the sea. If our route happens to overlap, we might gain something there.>
<The Schwaben guy will probably glare at you like you’re a thorn in his eye, but you don’t have much more to lose anyway.>
’Just how many arrangements did the late emperor leave?’
<When dealing with demons, no matter how many, it’s never enough.>
Aint nodded at Gardner’s words.
"Does that mean you’ll come?"
Balrosi misunderstood this as an answer to him, but there was no need to correct him.
"Yes."

chapters.title: Chapter 53: Contract and the Trap [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 53: Contract and the Trap [1]
"It was a good deal."
Professor Grad had delivered full value for the money.
He had played a smooth bridging role to enable the contract to be formed as Gerhard wanted.
"We were glad to experience the dignity of the Golden Turtle Company."
Gerhard and the Vice Chancellor exchanged contracts and shook hands.
With this, the water dragon’s carcass became entirely the property of the Golden Turtle Company.
[1). Party A has priority rights for the sale of vessels (including all ships, warships, cruise ships, etc.) within the Academy for the next 20 years.
2). Party A shall sell some water dragon byproducts to Party B at reasonable prices.
3). Party B shall...]
The contract contained numerous clauses, but the key points were three:
The Academy would sell the water dragon’s carcass to the Golden Turtle Company.
The Academy would grant the Golden Turtle Company priority rights for vessel sales within the Academy for the next 20 years.
The Golden Turtle Company would provide the byproducts of the water dragon that the Academy needed at reasonable prices.
’Good. Everything I wanted is included.’
The first was obvious, and the second was Gerhard’s requirement.
The third was the condition put forward by the Academy in exchange for Gerhard’s requirement.
’A spirit creature’s carcass is most expensive when sold intact without being dismantled.’
Buying the carcass at a high price and then providing byproducts at a low price — normally, there could be nothing more foolish.
But now was the time to take a step back to pursue greater profits.
For the Academy, it was beneficial to obtain byproducts cheaply with the relatively unimportant priority rights for vessels.
’They must be wondering why I want priority rights for such a small-scale vessel business.’
For Gerhard, who knew how much the Academy’s warship business would grow, it was a much more profitable deal.
It was a rational transaction where no one lost.
"Thank you for your work."
"It’s nothing. It’s not like making contracts is something new."
After completing the satisfactory contract, Gerhard stepped outside and stretched his stiff body.
"Now that I’ve laid the groundwork, I just need to get father’s permission."
The reason it was specifically stated as "priority rights for sales" rather than "exclusive sales rights" was because he hadn’t yet received permission from his father.
Until the incident occurred, there was no rational basis to persuade his father.
But Gerhard’s temperament wouldn’t allow him to give up on a business that was clearly a gold mine.
The result was "priority rights for sales."
’The best I can do without causing problems even if things go wrong.’
It was literally just priority rights, so there was no need to do anything immediately.
The next steps could be postponed until after the prophesied events occurred.
"How’s the setup going?"
"The installation is complete."
This meant that the work to install recording devices on the cruise ship, which would be the stage for the Yacht Club, was finished.
With this, they could monitor every move of the evil beings.
"What about the staff list?"
"I’ve placed it in your office, but..."
"Is there a problem?"
"I couldn’t find anything particularly unusual."
"I would expect that."
If they were easily exposed, would they be demons? They’d be fools.
