But Gerhard decided to assume they were false. Commonsensically, it was unimaginable that she would deceive the head of her family and act independently.
"How are you doing with the final exams?"
"Not bad. I certainly can’t beat the noble one from the Dragon Faith Order, but just below that, well."
"I see."
Well, as a companion of the great hero acknowledged by the prophecy book, she naturally would have that level of talent.
He was in no position to worry about others when he was buying victories with money.
***
Although he secured first place in "Combat, War, and Magic" through outstanding improvisation and appropriate strategies, the final exams weren’t over yet.
There were several other subjects, and most importantly, the other 5-credit courses, "Magic Survival Skills" and "Research on Magic Beasts and Monsters," remained.
"Combat, War, and Magic," "Magic Survival Skills," and "Research on Magic Beasts and Monsters" were distinctly different subjects, but they were inseparably related.
Naturally, the broad outline of the three exams was similar.
"The setting for the ’Magic Survival Skills’ exam is the northern snow region. There, you must survive for four days. Nothing will be provided separately, and your enemies are not only the harsh environment but also monsters."
Fortunately, there was no competition between students in this exam, but on the flip side, the level of monsters was high.
However, the results of this exam were somewhat different from the previous one.
The academy students weren’t fools. Having been caught off guard several times, they made their own preparations, which became prominently evident in the "Magic Survival Skills" exam.
Especially Rudger and Carlo were confident.
"You’re not the only one who can use them, right? The Schwaben family might not be as rich as Goldenheim, but we have enough money to be recognized anywhere in the empire."
"If the conditions are the same, there’s no reason for me to lose to you."
In the midst of year-round blizzards and attacking monsters, Gerhard and Luina survived until the end.
However, perhaps due to the help of artifacts, there were more survivors than expected. Since it was a relative evaluation rather than an absolute one, the assessment among survivors diverged based on other factors.
Carlo Deneb.
He and Allia Torta, who had hunted the most monsters with the most powerful firepower among the second-year students, secured first place, while Rudger and Almon ranked second.
Gerhard and Luina were pushed to third place.
To make matters worse.
"I’ve heard the stories. The exam fervor has overheated, leading to frequent use of artifacts, reagents, potions, and other items."
"So we’re going to cool down that fervor a bit. For this ’Research on Magic Beasts and Monsters’ exam, all external items are prohibited."
The worst situation had befallen Gerhard.
"...Even if I don’t use artifacts, my skills don’t disappear, right?"
"They do. I receive more help from money than you think."

chapters.title: Chapter 101: Three Times Inevitable [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 101: Three Times Inevitable [2]
The test for "Research on Magic Beasts and Monsters" was simple: hunting large monsters using dummies.
The main evaluation score was based on how quickly and with what level of cooperation they could capture ten dummy monsters with different characteristics that appeared in sequence.
"But I think you know the characteristics of monsters better than anyone and how to utilize that knowledge."
"Well, anyone qualified to enter here would have memorized the characteristics of most magic beasts and monsters."
"But you know the most efficient ways to deal with them based on those characteristics, don’t you?"
"Of course I do."
"That’s enough."
It really was enough. When Gerhard recited the efficient methods for handling monsters, Luina executed them faster than anyone else.
"...Your skills?"
"I’ve been working hard not to be a burden. Thanks to that, I’ve had some small achievements recently."
With Luina’s unexpected performance, they secured second place in "Research on Magic Beasts and Monsters."
"We’ve won again."
"I’m glad I can finally show my true abilities to His Majesty."
Rudger and Almon took first place, but it didn’t significantly affect the overall trend.
After all the collaborative exams ended, individual exams followed.
[Academy 2nd Year 1st Semester Final Exam Magic Department Rankings]
[1st. Gerhard Goldenheim
2nd. Carlo Deneb
3rd. Rudger Schwaben
4th...]
[Academy 2nd Year 1st Semester Final Exam Knight Department Rankings]
[1st. Luina Berchef
2nd. Almon Donertz
3rd. Harold Volkan
4th...]
After the exams ended, the results everyone had been waiting for came out.
Gerhard and Luina, who had been causing upsets since the beginning of the semester, finally took first place.
[Academy 2nd Year 1st Semester Magic Department Rankings]
[Top. Gerhard Goldenheim
Runner-up. Carlo Deneb
3rd. Rudger Schwaben
4th. Daisy...]
And the year rankings, which evaluated the combination of practical sessions, the previous midterm exam, were announced.
[Academy 2nd Year 1st Semester Knight Department Rankings]
[Top. Luina Berchef
Runner-up. Almon Donertz
3rd. Allia...]
The rankings at the top, which had been half-fixed throughout the school year, had been reversed.
***
Almon, who hadn’t lost the top position since admission, dropping to runner-up, and Gerhard, who was only ranked 10th, rising to the top in just one semester, were certainly big issues.
"...Gerhard is really the top student now?"
"From 10th to top in one semester. He must have been hiding his abilities. Why did he hide them until now and only reveal them now?"
"Luina has finally become the top student."
"Congratulations, Luina!"
"I can’t believe I’ve dropped..."
"It’s the first time I’ve lost the top position."
Many students gathered in front of the year ranking chart, which was announced along with the final exam results.
Some were just surprised at the upset, some congratulated, some were angry, and some burned with competitive spirit.
"...I’m the top student now."
But the very person who caused the upset didn’t seem particularly happy.
"You don’t look that pleased considering it’s the top position you’ve been wanting."
"It’s not that... It feels like I didn’t achieve it entirely with my own hands. It would have been impossible without your help."
"You’re thinking unnecessarily."
This straight-laced person even cares about such things? Thinking how different they were, Gerhard smiled slightly.
"We formed a pair, and a pair is a community. We achieved the grades together, so there’s no need to worry about the supplementary aspects. I, too, wouldn’t have gotten such results without you."
"Is that so?"
"It is."
"Was I ever a burden to you?"
"Not even once."
"I see."
Luina nodded slightly.
Still.
"I need to work harder next time."
"By all means. Anyway, congratulations on becoming the top student. With this, you’ve taken one step closer to your goal."
"Yes, congratulations to you too. I look forward to working with you next semester as well."
"Likewise."
Luina bowed her head slightly and went to her friends.
"You look good."
"Rudger."
"Honestly, it was unexpected. I never thought you would rise so rapidly as soon as the second semester started. It’s fair to say I was completely off guard."
"You didn’t seem that way during the final exams, though maybe during the midterms."
"The midterms were significant."
That was true. Because the midterm exams were all replaced with written tests, Gerhard benefited greatly from that.
Even though the final exam results were weighted more heavily than the midterm results in this comprehensive ranking due to its uniqueness.
"Anyway, congratulations. But remember, there won’t be a second time."
"Wasn’t it not your position to begin with?"
"Don’t you feel the vicious glare of the original owner?"
Not far away, Carlo was seen biting his lips while looking at the ranking chart.
Honestly, he was the one who suffered the most loss due to Gerhard’s rise.
’Originally, Luina and Carlo would have been a pair.’
If that had been the case, the results would have been quite different.
But that didn’t mean he needed to care about Carlo. It was a bit unfortunate, but that was all.
"Do you have any plans for the vacation?"
"I’m thinking of returning to my family."
"What a boring vacation plan."
It wasn’t particularly boring. When he thought about what he would do after returning to his family, he actually felt excited.
After exchanging a few more words, Rudger disappeared, and Gerhard moved a few steps to check another ranking chart.
[Academy 1st Year 1st Semester Knight Department Rankings]
[Top - Balrosi Viston
Runner-up - Aint Armian
3rd - Veriana Kalproten
4th - Barosu Drage...]
"Hmm."
Aint Armian was also showing impressive results, making his 38th place in the entrance exam seem unbelievable.
"Not bad."
It was a pity he wasn’t the top student, but that wasn’t because Aint was lacking; it meant Balrosi Viston was that exceptional.
It really wasn’t bad at all.
***
Balrosi Viston, who showed friendliness without reason from the start.
Ariadne Florian, who was more desperate for connections than Balrosi.
Luina Berchef, whom Aint approached first after falling for her at first sight.
And Barosu Drage, who became close after working together as mercenaries during the vacation.
Aint Armian had a total of four companions.
While he didn’t know who else might join later, these were all the people Gerhard had confirmed through the prophecy book for now.
’And among them, the one who would make contact with Aint the latest was the disciple of the Mercenary King, Barosu Drage.’
With the descent of Andromalius, Barosu would fight alongside Aint, and they would become close because of it.
But Gerhard intended to twist that future a bit.
"Barosu Drage. I’d like to make a request to you and your mercenary band."
"Senior Gerhard? I always welcome requests. Above all, if it’s from Senior Gerhard, you’ll pay handsomely."
Barosu smiled with greed all over his face.
"The request is..."
Through the prophecy book, he knew what requests Aint would accept.
Gerhard wanted to include Barosu and his mercenary band in that request.
Since the flow had been changed several times by him, there was a possibility that the danger to Aint would be greater than what was in the prophecy book.
’It would be most reassuring if I prepared and went myself, but I can’t do that.’
Andromalius would descend just before the end of the vacation.
For that day not far away, shouldn’t he have at least one secret weapon?
’Barosu Drage and his mercenary band should be sufficient.’
Barosu Drage was ranked 3rd, no, 4th in the Knight Department and had the talent to become Aint’s companion, and his mercenary band was composed of outstanding individuals chosen by the Mercenary King.
It was enough for Aint’s bodyguard.
Even if he made them companions a bit early, the future wouldn’t change significantly.
Gerhard, who had just completed a contract with Barosu, stretched.
The long, long first semester of the second year had finally ended.

chapters.title: Chapter 102: The Gorgon Hunt [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 102: The Gorgon Hunt [1]
After the final exams, the academy enters a long vacation.
The atmosphere at the academy was quite excited with the upcoming break. Students gathered in small groups in the courtyards, their faces bright with anticipation, sharing plans and exchanging contact details with promises to write. The scent of early summer blossoms wafted through the open windows, mingling with the distinctive magical residue that perpetually hung in the air.
Some prepared to return to their homes, while others planned to stay at the academy to make up for lacking studies. The library would remain open, though with reduced hours, its towering bookshelves offering solace to those dedicated few who chose knowledge over leisure. The practice fields, too, would be available for those determined to hone their combat skills during the quiet months.
"What are your plans, Luina?"
"I’m thinking of returning home. Although the situation at home is improving, I should lend a hand, even if briefly."
Indeed, even though the Berchef family was gradually improving, the monsters coming from the north hadn’t completely disappeared.
"What about you?"
"I also plan to return to my family. I have things to do. When do you plan to come back?"
"Why do you ask?"
Why? Because "you need to return before Andromalius is summoned."
"Just asking."
"I plan to come back about two weeks early to prepare for the next semester."
"I see. Understood."
So Luina’s participation in the battle against Andromalius was already foreseen, without any need for intervention.
"If you ever need my help later, feel free to contact me anytime."
"I’ll be fine."
"Take this. It’s a direct communication orb. Though the range is only about 3 kilometers."
"Isn’t that pointless then?"
The distance between Berchef and Goldenheim was easily thousands of kilometers.
"Just take it. This is..."
A preparation not for the vacation but for what comes after at the academy.
Gerhard swallowed his words.
"This is?"
"Nothing. Have a good journey, top student."
"Top student... It feels unfamiliar, but not bad. Yes, I hope you have a pleasant vacation too."
After parting with Luina, Gerhard returned to the company’s office.
Since he would be away from the academy for quite some time, there were many matters to handle beforehand.
"Haven’t you already handled everything?"
Hyde looked questioningly at the busy Gerhard and asked.
"This isn’t company business, it’s something else."
"Materials, I presume."
"Correct. I need to make sure they’re properly arriving at the family, loaded onto ships, and check the status of the remaining materials."
Of course, it was unlikely anything would go wrong, but there are no absolutes.
"Prepare a magic circle heading to the family."
"Not by ship?"
"Time is money. And don’t miss anything about Aint Armian’s movements."
Gerhard checked the documents related to the water dragon.
***
<So, are you planning to go home?>
"No."
A salty sea breeze blew past. Aint stood at the stern, gazing at the vast ocean.
"My father would genuinely be happy with my achievements now. So would the family retainers."
The Armian family had fallen, and many people had left. But conversely, those who remained became even closer.
"That’s why if I go once, I won’t be able to leave easily. I’d better stick to the original plan before I get weak-hearted. Besides, I’ve already sent a letter to the domain."
The ship steadily progressed southeast.
Their destination wasn’t Luthar, where the Armian Kingdom began, but the southern Pandrein continent.
<Pandrein has more untouched areas compared to Luthar. Because of that, there are more monsters, and naturally, stronger ones too.>
<It’s the most optimized place for you to gain real battle experience.>
"I see."
Aint nodded.
"But isn’t that information from a thousand years ago?"
<...Huh?>
For the first time, Gardner’s surprised voice was heard.
"But you’re probably not wrong. Even after a thousand years, I’ve heard that Pandrein is still underdeveloped."
Although it had developed incomparably from then, everything was relative.
<That’s what I meant.>
Several days later, the ship arrived at Lamons, a port city in the Kingdom of Pragia.
"Outwardly, there’s not much difference."
<While Pandrein had less population compared to Luthar, they weren’t isolated from each other.>
<By the way, Pragia. It’s a name I hadn’t heard during my lifetime.>
"It’s a country established about 500 years ago."
It was a nation that supported and encouraged mercenaries based on its vast territory and abundant resources to survive against strong monsters.
The most powerful country in the Pandrein continent, except for the Empire.
<Let’s first register as a mercenary and look for a suitable request.>
"Yes."
Lamons was the largest trading city in the Kingdom of Pragia, and its scale was considerable. Naturally, people flocked there, and the mercenary guild was no exception.
The ten-story mercenary guild was bustling with people.
The first floor had a tavern-like layout, similar to other mercenary guild branches.
There were dozens of tables and a bar, and on the large pillar-cum-bulletin board in the center hung dozens of request papers.
To one side were counters and guides.
Aint went straight to the counter.
"Welcome. How can I help you?"
"I’d like to take the mercenary test."
"Could you give me your name and identification tag?"
"My name is Aint, and I don’t have an identification tag, but I have this."
Aint held out his academy student ID. While it didn’t have detailed information, it was engraved with the seven stars symbolizing the academy.
"Are you an academy student?"
The clerk’s gaze changed at the sight of the student ID, which was almost impossible to forge or impersonate due to complex magical engravings and the Empire’s severe punishment system.
"Yes."
"If it’s not rude, may I ask what year you’re in?"
"First year."
"Academy first-year students are automatically given a Level 4 tag. You can raise your rank through additional tests, so please let me know if you’d like to take them."
Following Gardner’s advice that a Level 4 wouldn’t allow him to take the desired level of requests, Aint was about to answer.
"I’d like to take the test..."
"Huh? Aint?"
At that moment, a shadow fell behind him. It was a man with short brown hair, black eyes, and a muscular body covered with small scars.
"Barosu? What brings you here?"
"I should be asking you that. For me, this place is as comfortable as my home."
Come to think of it, Barosu Drage was the disciple of the Mercenary King, who could be considered the spiritual pillar of the mercenary guild.
It wasn’t particularly special for him to come to the mercenary guild during vacation.

chapters.title: Chapter 103: The Gorgon Hunt [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 103: The Gorgon Hunt [2]
"That’s true."
"Are you trying to become a mercenary?"
"I wanted to experience mercenary work during the vacation."
"Mercenaries sure seem easy to everyone. Every Tom, Ditch, and Harry wants to become a mercenary for fun."
Barosu’s lips twisted upward. Just as Aint’s brow twitched, he continued.
"But you’re not just anyone, so I understand. Hey."
"Yes, yes! Mr. Barosu!"
The guide, recognizing Barosu, answered in a tense voice.
"He doesn’t need to take the test. This friend is the runner-up of the academy’s first year. You can register him directly as Level 3."
"Runner-up, you say?"
"Yes, his skills are certain."
Thanks to Barosu’s testimony, the mercenary registration was completed in an instant. A silver tag with the number 3 engraved on it was placed in Aint’s hand.
"Thanks, that was easy because of you."
"No need to thank me. With your skills, it would have been just a matter of sooner or later anyway. If you’re done, please move aside. I have business to attend to."
"Sure."
As Aint stepped aside slightly, Barosu immediately took his place.
"Where’s the Abelar Subjugation request?"
"Are you planning to participate in that?"
"Yes. I plan to lead the entire mercenary band."
"With your direct participation, this subjugation will surely succeed. I’ll register Barosu and the entire Black Spear Mercenary Band."
"Thanks."
After finishing the registration in an instant, Barosu stood up.
"If you’re looking for mercenary work worth doing, you should also join the Abelar Subjugation. With your skills, it wouldn’t be bad."
"What exactly is that?"
"Get the details directly through the guild."
Barosu brushed past Aint and left. Aint sat down in front of the guide again.
"Abelar Subjugation? What is that?"
"It’s a domain that has been devastated by rampaging monsters. The domain has now become a monster’s lair, with an estimated number of monsters nesting there close to five hundred."
Therefore, the Kingdom of Pragia had made a large-scale request to the mercenary guild, and so far, about three hundred mercenaries had applied to participate.
"It’s dangerous, but the reward promised by Pragia is quite substantial, and above all, a gorgon has been discovered."
"A gorgon?"
A gorgon was a monster with horns on its head and its entire body covered with metal scales harder than steel.
Its front legs resembled those of a lion with sharp claws, and its tail was made of a snake—a large beast.
It was undoubtedly a formidable opponent.
But it was also popular because its carcass could fetch a large sum of money.
"That’s why as many as three hundred mercenaries have gathered."
<That’s very tempting.>
<A gorgon is a stronger monster than an ogre, and with hundreds of monsters, a chaotic battle will unfold. It’s perfectly suitable for experiencing war.>
With Gardner’s comment, Aint nodded.
"Then, can I also participate in that?"
"Of course. The participation restriction is Level 3 or higher, so Aint, as a Level 3 mercenary, is absolutely welcome."
That day, Aint received the request for the Abelar Subjugation.
It was exactly the request that Gerhard had seen through the prophecy book, where Aint would encounter the demon species.
***
The gathering place for the subjugation force was a place called Ginchef.
A small barony that lived in daily anxiety due to its proximity to Abelar, which had been devastated.
Three hundred mercenaries and five hundred royal soldiers gathered in one place.
Waaaaa—
The domain residents cheered for the subjugation force that had gathered to eliminate the source of their anxiety.
"Level 3 mercenary, Aint. Identity confirmed."
Aint, after being confirmed by the receptionist, joined the ranks. The mercenaries, sprawled everywhere in a level that could hardly be called orderly, were munching on the meat and bread they had been given.
"Please come this way for meals. Let’s fill your stomach substantially before heading into battle."
Aint went to the meal station, received his ration, and sat down on any chair to eat. It wasn’t particularly good.
’I realize once again how excellent the academy’s dining halls were.’
<Of course. They’ve gathered the best talents; they can’t feed them cheap food.>
That’s when it happened.
"It doesn’t seem to suit your taste."
Someone sat down beside him.
"Barosu."
"So even the great bloodline has refined taste, it seems."
"I’m just not used to it. But who are these people?"
It wasn’t just Barosu who sat nearby. Thirty mercenaries. The aura they emitted was quite impressive.
"My subordinate mercenary band. The Gray Spear Mercenary Band is quite famous in this industry."
He had heard of them.
A mercenary band formed by mercenaries chosen by the Mercenary King for his disciple.
Since its establishment, it had handled more than dozens of requests but had never failed once.
"You don’t know much about mercenary work, right?"
"Naturally, since it’s my first time."
"If you want, you can join us and move together."
"What? Is that okay?"
Barosu nonchalantly tore into the meat.
"You won’t be a burden, and you’re an Armian."
"If you’re looking at my family, there’s nothing to it now."
"But I don’t think it will continue to be nothing."
"On what basis?"
"The basis that you went from 38th to runner-up in one semester. The basis that you beat me."
I’m just extending a hand to be friendly.
"I only believe in the skills I’ve experienced. And you beat me. I really like strong individuals. And someone who has set foot in the mercenary industry is also a fellow mercenary."
With a smile full of goodwill, Aint pondered for a moment.
<It’s not a bad idea to accept. As you said, they’re veteran mercenaries, so there will be much to learn.>
<While you would be considered strong anywhere on the continent, you never know what might happen in the field.>
<Especially since it’s your first time, I think it’s good to be prepared for any contingency.>
"But will it be okay? The prince won’t like it."
"Even the imperial family can’t touch me."
<How arrogant. How dare he insult the imperial family?>
’It’s not Armian but Schwaben.’
Aint calmed Gardner, who was getting agitated.
"In that case..."
"Great, Aint. It seems we can get along well."
Barosu shook hands with Aint, smiling brightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 104: Demon Ambush [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 104: Demon Ambush [1]
"We march!"
Waaaaaaa—
Please succeed and return safely!
Long live the Kingdom of Pragia!
The subjugation force of nearly eight hundred departed from Ginchef amid the people’s passionate cheers.
The kingdom’s regular army and mercenaries moved separately, keeping some distance, and Aint joined the Gray Spear Mercenary Band with Barosu.
"So this is the famous descendant of the Armian family?"
"The one who defeated our young master with one hand?"
"But can such a noble person adapt to mercenary life?"
"Maybe? Being an Armian, even a hundred years ago, they were foot... urk!"
"We’re talking about a great family, show some respect. Pleased to meet you. I’m Hector."
The mercenaries approached one by one to greet him. Each had hands full of scars and calluses.
The one who practically managed the rough Gray Spear Mercenary Band was a mercenary named Hector. A huge 2-meter tall figure with a muscular build, covered in scars.
"I’m Aint."
"Huhu, I really wanted to meet you after hearing that our young master couldn’t even put up a fight."
"Don’t fabricate stories, Hector. It was a close call."
"Young master tends to downplay things when they’re unfavorable to him."
"It’s the truth, I tell you."
Barosu, who grumbled with a hollow laugh, whispered softly.
"Don’t worry. They’re a bit rough, but they keep their mouths shut. Your identity as an Armian won’t leak outside."
"Thanks."
"Come with me for a moment."
Barosu struck the side of his horse and galloped lightly forward. Aint followed.
"Have you heard the operation plan?"
"Yes."
It wasn’t a particularly elaborate plan. The subjugation force would enter Abelar as is and sweep away all the monsters in the area.
Furthermore, they would subjugate the gorgon that was acting as the leader at the center of Abelar.
To do this, they planned to systematically annihilate the monsters from the outskirts inward.
At least, that was the plan until just now.
Wooooo—
Boom boom boom—
"Emergency! Emergency!"
"Multiple monsters appearing at the front!"
"Gnoll, Dire Wolf, Grizzly Bear, Griffin, and two other types of monsters spotted!"
"Prepare for battle!"
Along with the urgent battle horn, shouts could be heard from here and there.
As if the previous sloppiness had been a lie, the atmosphere among the Gray Spear Mercenary Band members changed dramatically.
"Captain!"
Even their way of speaking changed. Barosu gripped his weapon and led the mercenaries.
"We’ll cut through the enemy formation from the front."
"Yes! Prepare to advance!"
"Yes!"
The Gray Spear mercenaries, all mounted, moved forward. The distance to the group of a hundred monsters was rapidly closing.
"Aint, you stay at the rear. Since you’re not yet in sync with us, that would be better."
"Okay."
Aint obediently followed behind them, riding the horse he had purchased separately.
"Split their formation in half, wheel around, and tear them apart."
"Yes."
"Prepare to charge."
"Prepare to charge!"
They were only about 30 mercenaries, but there wasn’t an ounce of fear in their eyes.
"Charge!"
"Chaaaaarge!"
Thump thump thump—
The horses began to gallop wildly.
"It’s the Gray Spear Mercenary Band!"
"Follow them!"
"Crush the monsters!"
Mounted mercenaries recognized the Gray Spear Mercenary Band and followed behind. The spears, which were only thirty in number, quickly doubled.
"Charge!"
"Charge!"
Thirty-one black spears sharpened their edges toward the enemies.
Black aura bloomed at the tips of the spears.
And then.
———!
Crack—
Bang!
Clang—
Kyeeeek!
Neeeigh!
The two groups collided. A chilling roar shook the battlefield.
Dire Wolves with holes all over their bodies flew through the air, turned into bloody pulp. Red droplets of blood scattered in all directions.
The cavalrymen, momentarily hesitant, spurred on as they trampled the ground mixed with corpses.
The gray spears chased after the blood of new enemies.
"Don’t stop!"
"Don’t fall behind!"
It was like a storm. They pushed, pierced, and tore apart everything that stood in their way as they advanced.
Kroaar!
The monsters charged without concern, not knowing fear.
But that only hastened their deaths.
In front of the thirty-one spears charging as one, all monsters met the same fate.
The path they had taken was left as a bloody road, mangled with the blood and corpses of monsters.
***
<These guys aren’t mercenaries, I’d believe it if they were called knights. Trusting their comrades and jumping into the midst of monsters without the slightest hesitation. This is the perfect example of a charge.>
<I’d like to show this to those pretentious so-called knights.>
Gardner’s admiration was no different from predicting the outcome of the battle.
The enemy formation was split in half by the Gray Spear Mercenary Band, and when the monsters’ attention was focused on them, other mercenaries attacked from behind.
The entire field was filled with corpses, and the disgusting smell of mixed human and monster blood assaulted the nose.
"...Urgh!"
At that horrific scene, Aint unconsciously gagged.
He thought he had experienced quite a lot of real battles, but this was his first time witnessing a fight where dozens or hundreds of creatures died.
"Hehehe, you can really tell he was raised nobly."
"True. During the fight, he beheaded enemies without hesitation, but now?"
The mercenaries snickered, and Barosu handed over a towel.
"Wipe your mouth."
"Thanks... Isn’t this a rag?"
It was too dirty and smelly to be called a towel.
"I used it to wipe off some blood while dismantling monsters."
While Aint was vomiting, most of the mercenaries were dismantling the monsters’ corpses to claim their share.
Barosu was doing the same.
The completely dismantled corpses were being gathered and burned in one place by the kingdom’s soldiers who arrived late.
"Urgh. I feel like vomiting more."
"Bear with it. Isn’t this the kind of experience you became a mercenary for?"
"That’s true, but..."
Is there really a need to wipe my mouth with a rag used to wipe monster blood?
Anyway, compared to a war with demons, this would be a drop in the bucket. Thinking that he couldn’t be weak over just this much, Aint forced himself to get up.
"Captain Barosu. The commander summons you."
At that moment, a messenger approached.
The subjugation commander referred to Count Passen of the Kingdom of Pragia, who was currently leading the subjugation force.
"I’ll go."
Barosu followed the messenger into the command tent and only came out about two hours later.
"According to the scouts, the monsters are scattered in small groups in all directions. Therefore, the forces will be divided accordingly."
"That means mercenaries should move autonomously by mercenary band, right?"
"Yes. The rights to the corpses will belong to the subjugators, and additional compensation will be provided based on the evidence of subjugation."
Having the rights to the monsters killed was a basic aspect.
The other mercenary bands seemed to have received the message as well, as they were preparing to leave the camp one by one.
"What about the kingdom’s soldiers?"
"They’ll also be divided into small units and scattered."
"What if the monsters regroup?"
"That’s why they distributed maps marking the main gathering places within the domain."
A total of 12 places.
Originally villages and cities where citizens would have been living, the idea was that if the monsters regrouped and became large-scale, forces should gather at the nearest meeting place to join forces.
There were also flares to be fired in emergency situations.
"Good. Then let’s go hunt the gorgon."
"Indeed, that’s our request. Aint, what are your plans?"
"...Hmm. If it’s not rude, can I continue to follow you?"
With this first battle, Aint profoundly realized.
Thanks to his swordsmanship and aura characteristics, he was optimized for facing magic beasts, but apart from that, he still lacked in many areas.
He judged that it would be better to learn about reality by piggybacking on a veteran mercenary band than wandering alone and dying a lonely death.
"By all means, if that’s what you want."
"Thanks."
"Then you should pay us."
The vice-captain abruptly extended his hand.
"Money?"
"If you think about it, isn’t this an escort request? Shouldn’t there be compensation?"
"Hector."
"I’m joking. Since you’re a friend of our young master, of course we’ll do it for free."
He chuckled while brushing his unkempt beard.
"Thank you."
"Who knows? Maybe someday we’ll receive a favor from the imperial family."

chapters.title: Chapter 105: Demon Ambush [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 105: Demon Ambush [2]
The Gray Spear Mercenary Band continued to ride for the entire day. Their target was the gorgon, and they advanced toward the center teeming with monsters faster than anyone else.
Thanks to this, Aint could genuinely feel the worth of becoming a mercenary.
"Are you sure it’s hundreds? Not thousands?"
Aint panted heavily, shaking off the blood on his sword. The rotten smell vibrating throughout his body was enough to numb his nose.
"It seems like there are many because they keep swarming without giving us a break, but the actual number isn’t that high."
Barosu replied while skinning a griffin.
Of course, he meant that it wasn’t to the extent of exaggerating to thousands.
"How much further to the gorgon’s nest?"
"At this pace, we’ll need at least two more days. Our movement is slower than expected because of the many monsters."
"That’s right. There seem to be more monsters than expected."
"If that’s the case, wouldn’t it be easier when we hunt the gorgon? Since the gorgon is fierce, other monsters don’t approach its vicinity, so having many monsters elsewhere isn’t a problem."
"True, if we’re at this level, the others must be taking even longer."
The mercenary band members each added a word to Aint’s question. Perhaps due to spending two days together on the battlefield, a kind of bond seemed to have formed.
Aint chewed on dried meat.
"You’ve become a full-fledged mercenary in just two days."
Whether he had adapted, the dried meat went down well even on this corpse-covered ground.
"The day will soon be over, so let’s stop here for today and look for a place to set up camp..."
That’s when it happened.
The wind blew.
The moment he felt something faint mixed and carried by the wind, Aint had a strange feeling.
How should he describe this?
<It’s unpleasant.>
Yes, it was unpleasant. It was disgusting and filthy.
Instinctive repulsion and aversion.
And it was a sensation that had become somewhat familiar to Aint by now.
<Aint!>
Gardner sent a fierce warning.
The back of Aint’s neck turned cold.
"Dodge!"
Aint drew his sword. At that moment, black masses fell like hail.
———!
The pure white trajectory he drew deflected the black flashes.
With a roar, the subsequent shockwave shook the earth.
"Wh-what...!"
"We’re under attack!"
The band members were startled and assumed battle positions.
Aint steadied his faltering stance while rubbing his tingling arm.
"You blocked that?"
A very small and low voice. But it was still clearly audible.
"As expected, His Excellency’s judgment is always correct. You’ve become a level that can no longer be ignored."
"Who are you!"
"What are you, bastard."
The members held their spears tightly, wary of the unusual energy.
"I have no interest in small fry, so get out of the way."
Ah, of course, that doesn’t mean I’ll let you live.
"No one will leave this place alive today."
"Arrogant bastard...!"
"Everyone, stay alert!"
They felt uneasy but didn’t back down. Fighting spirit gradually intensified.
"Aint. What is this guy? You seem to know."
"...It’s a demon species."
"Demon species?"
Momentarily surprised by the unexpected name, Barosu soon wore a faint smile.
"We’ll get the details later, but for now, this is good."
"Good?"
"Then the Gray Spear Mercenary Band will be the first to subjugate a demon species since the Great War. Did everyone hear that?"
The members responded to Barosu’s shout.
"Yes, of course!"
"A demon species. I didn’t know that worms who sell their souls to demons actually existed, but this will certainly make our mercenary band more famous."
"The request fee will increase too!"
"That’s good, I like it."
"The most important thing is more request fees!"
Hehehe, the mercenaries laughed cheerfully.
"These worms dare to consider who as their prey...!"
The demon species’ eyebrows twitched.
"Know your place...!"
Whoosh—
A black flash, with a different feel from what the demon species had fired, grazed the demon species’ ear.
"You dodged that at this distance?"
Barosu muttered as he took out another throwing spear.
"Indeed. So, you have some value worth selling your soul to a demon for."
"You worm-like bastard...!"
The demon species roared.
The battle began.
***
It started with throwing spears.
Exactly 31 flashes were shot out simultaneously.
Boom!
A black barrier deflected all the flashes.
Immediately after, the band members collectively kicked the ground. Black aura was sharply forged at the tips of the gray spears.
The demon species quickly extended its fist. Magic energy swelled up. When the fist reached the dozens of spear tips, there were no longer humans there.
Only a 3-meter giant wrapped in magic energy.
——!
Thirty-one spears struck the giant’s outer skin. None of the spears were sharp enough to pierce it.
"Kheuk...!"
Barosu, who had collided head-on with the fist at the front, screamed and was thrown backward. But there was no time to dissipate the impact and regain his posture.
"You must be the leader of these."
Because the black giant immediately followed.
Boom!
The specially crafted gray spear bent as if it would break. Another fist fell, but he blocked that as well. Barosu forcibly swallowed the blood that welled up.
"You crazy monster...!"
Fortunately, there wasn’t a third time. Because Aint, who had approached unnoticed, brought down his sacred sword.
———!
A vastly different sound and result from the band members.
The two energies writhed violently like a battle between light and darkness, and part of the demon species’ outer skin was split. It screamed in pain.
In the meanwhile, Barosu, taking a breath, extended his spear forward.
A blade, honed as large and sharp as possible by squeezing the aura hole, pierced the demon species’ heart.
—!
An explosion occurred as aura and magic energy collided. With a strong rebound, Barosu stepped back.
Indeed, his full-powered strike definitely had an effect on the creature. The spear had pierced the outer skin of magic energy.
But that was all. It was just a small scratch, and even that was quickly mended.
’This is a crazy monster, isn’t it?’
It was quite different from the result Aint had produced.
Barosu recalled an old legend. The legend of the Armian, known as the antithesis to demons.
"Everyone, support Aint!"
"Yes!"
The experienced mercenaries realized what the most certain path to victory was.
And that sight irritated the demon species.
"You flies!"
The magic energy that had been swirling around its entire body was released at once. With a roar, the emitted shockwave made the mercenaries retreat in unison.
Only Aint, with his antithetical power, was able to withstand it, and the demon species immediately took a breath. A massive magic energy concentrated and was spewed out.
Aint extended his sword forward.
—!
Light and darkness collided. Pieces of severed darkness splashed in all directions.
In that brief gap, the demon species had already reached right in front of Aint.
Bang, a fist fell vertically. The sword that barely blocked it trembled.
Clang, the sword that deflected the fist climbed up the forearm. The demon species stepped back, and Aint advanced that much.
—!
——!
In an instant, more than ten exchanges occurred. With each one, the earth shook, and the space was marked with wounds.
Amidst that fierce battle, the mercenaries moved. Hunters who had killed countless monsters.
From both sides and the rear. Spears found the glaringly exposed gaps as the demon species was preoccupied with Aint.
But it was a trap.
Black thorns sprouted from the body of the real hunter who had been waiting for the flies’ attack.
"Kugh...!"
"Be careful!"
Rip, some dodged, some blocked, and some were pierced. The processes were different, but the results were the same. No one was able to wound the demon species.
Except for Barosu.
He advanced, heightening his senses. Avoiding and deflecting dozens of thorns, he ignored the small wounds.
And right in front of the demon species, he leaped high like a grasshopper.
The 3-meter high back of the head was visible.
The black-shining spear pierced the space. No, it tried to pierce.
At that moment—
"Foolish one."
An eye opened on the back of the demon species’ head. Soon, a mouth opened, and concentrated magic energy was fired.
The black spear shattered part of the magic energy. However, the impact sent Barosu’s body flying through the air.
And the thorns of magic energy didn’t miss that opportunity.
Crack—
A flash pierced Barosu.
"...Barosu!"
"Captain!"
"Captain...!"
His body fell like a puppet with cut strings.

chapters.title: Chapter 106: Dark Revelations [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 106: Dark Revelations [1]
On an early morning with chirping sparrows.
Gerhard sat in the garden, dragging his tired body. Servants brought coffee and light refreshments.
"Are you alright?"
"I’m tired."
How many days had it been since he stayed up all night?
"Why don’t you rest a little?"
"I can’t do that."
He was aware that he was pushing himself too hard, but with the scheduled descent of the demon Andromalius, there was no room for leisure.
"Count Landgard frequently expresses his dissatisfaction."
"Dissatisfaction? That cranky dwarf always grumbles. But when you see him at work, his eyes never stop smiling."
Landgard was one of the most renowned craftsmen on the continent who had pledged allegiance to the Goldenheim family.
Gerhard was currently receiving help from Landgard and other family craftsmen and wizards.
"Dwarleo’s help is really significant. He catches and improves parts that I hadn’t even recognized."
Having the assistance of an outstanding wizard was indeed convenient.
"Hmm?"
At that moment, someone unusual caught Gerhard’s senses.
It was a person he had never seen before. A tall figure of about 2 meters. His muscles looked extremely solid, and small scars were engraved all over them.
A man who appeared to be in his mid-40s.
"He doesn’t seem to be from the family."
What made Gerhard’s neck cold was that he couldn’t sense anything from the man.
It was one of two possibilities.
Either there was truly nothing, or he was a strong individual beyond Gerhard’s reach.
"Isn’t that where the Duke’s study is?"
"Is he coming from meeting my father?"
If so, he wasn’t an enemy. Indeed, an enemy of the Goldenheim family wouldn’t dare enter deep into the family quarters.
’Who could meet my father so early in the morning? His face seems somewhat familiar.’
While thinking that, their eyes met.
"...!"
Gerhard flinched at the feeling of facing a predator. Raw, unprocessed anger was boiling.
"What...!"
Hyde hurriedly blocked Gerhard’s view.
"I have no intention of harming him, so step aside."
The man had already approached right in front of them.
When he gently pushed Hyde’s shoulder, Hyde was pushed aside without being able to resist.
Their eyes met once more.
"So it’s you. The one who sent that child there."
The moment the growling tone pierced his lungs, lightning struck in Gerhard’s mind.
The world turned upside down.
["So it’s you. The one who was there with that child."]
The man looked a bit older. But his aura remained the same.
No, it was even more menacing and more ferocious. The raw anger made one’s heart tremble.
["Yes. I’m sorry."
"You don’t need to be sorry. It’s just that the child was weak, and I didn’t teach him properly."]
Aint bowed his head. He also looked much more mature than now.
The man calmly forgave him, but the deeply rooted anger hadn’t disappeared at all.
["How was it? The child’s end?"
"...He was braver than anyone."
"...Stupid kid. I taught him to be a mercenary and to only look at money and life, not justice or courage."]
A hollow laugh flowed, empty yet somewhat proud and regretful.
["Who was it? Who killed that child."
"...A demon."
"A demon?"
"...It was Andras."
"A demon. What happened to it?"
"I killed it. With Barosu’s help."
"...I’ve heard rumors that demon species are active. Yet I thought it wouldn’t be much related to me, but it killed my disciple."]
The man gave a self-deprecating smile.
["They took Barosu from me, so I also intend to prevent them from achieving what they want."]
["I will spend the rest of my life killing demons."]
A burst of hatred and killing intent that Gerhard couldn’t dare imagine was released. Just as his mind was becoming dizzy, his consciousness returned to reality.
’...Barosu dies?’
Wait, then this man is...
Gerhard tried to ignore the headache and examined the man’s appearance. Somehow, he thought the man looked familiar, and it was because he had seen him through the registry.
"...The Mercenary King."
A person with the title of mercenary or knight.
One of the ten greatest knights.
"You forgot the honorific, young blood of Goldenheim."
"...It’s an honor to meet you."
"I heard you made a request to Barosu. Why?"
"...That’s."
An ominous feeling brushed his spine. Could something have gone wrong?
"...Because I thought Barosu was the right person."
"Yes, he is the right person. Not because he’s my disciple, but because Barosu is truly an outstanding mercenary."
Hmhmm, the Mercenary King laughed lowly.
"I don’t intend to blame you. It’s not like you did something wrong, and there’s nothing strange about making a request to a mercenary."
In the first place, it was Barosu’s choice to accept the request.
"Nevertheless, I thought that if it weren’t for your request, the child wouldn’t have ended up like that."
"...What happened to Barosu?"
"Ask your father about that. And try to stay out of my sight as much as possible from now on. I know rationally that it’s not your fault, but emotions are different."
The Mercenary King, suppressing his hatred, disappeared.
After he disappeared and Gerhard was freed from the pressure, he took a rough breath.
"Are you alright...!"
Hyde, who couldn’t do anything under the Mercenary King’s pressure, bit his lip and examined Gerhard.
"I’m fine...!"
His head felt like it was about to burst, but it was nothing. Nothing at all.
That wasn’t what was important right now.
’Something happened to Barosu!’
That meant something had definitely happened to Aint, who would have been with him.
Surely Aint hasn’t died, has he?
’What if the demon species’ vigilance increased because of the future I twisted, and they deployed stronger forces?’
Damn it, Gerhard gritted his teeth.
That’s when it happened.
"Young Master, here you are. His Excellency is calling for you."
A servant came looking for him. Gerhard immediately headed to the head of the family’s study.
"Welcome. Judging by your expression, it seems you’ve encountered Garet."
Garet Schreiner. The Mercenary King’s real name.
"Yes. What’s going on?"
"Garet has asked for our help. He wants us to track down the culprit."
The information network of the Goldenheim family, spread like a spider’s web, could be proudly considered superior to anyone else’s on the continent.
That was also why the Mercenary King had come.
"...By culprit, you mean?"
"They say Garet’s disciple, Barosu Drage, was seriously injured in the Abelar subjugation and still hasn’t regained consciousness."
"...!"
Gerhard let out a sigh of relief.
Sorry for Barosu, but the demon species who succeeded in their operation wouldn’t leave witnesses...
The fact that he’s alive means...
’Aint didn’t die.’
It meant hope hadn’t been extinguished.
***
"What did you discuss?"
"Serious matters."
According to the original prophecy book, Aint would withstand the demon species’ attack alone. But why, this time, did such a situation occur even with Barosu and the Gray Spear Mercenary Band?
’There’s only one possibility.’
It meant that the future Gerhard had changed caused a butterfly effect.
And that meant the future ahead might also change unpredictably.
’I tried to make minimal preparations for Aint’s growth, but that might not be nearly enough.’
Perhaps a demon other than Andromalius might appear, or instead of students simply being infected with magic energy and going mad, something more terrible could happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 107: Dark Revelations [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 107: Dark Revelations [2]
More minimal safety measures were needed.
Measures that would prevent things from going the worst way, like with Barosu.
After finishing the letter, he enclosed a small jewel in the envelope.
"I don’t need to tell you who to send this to, right?"
"The greedy professor at the academy."
"And this too."
"There’s one more?"
"Send it to Luina."
"Yes."
Hyde received the letters.
***
After the long winter, which was longer than in other regions, the half-melted snow turned the ground into a quagmire.
A silver knight galloped on a pure white horse. The muddy quagmire posed no obstacle, and as the brilliant blue light of the sword flashed, monsters fell with screams.
"Follow Lady Luina!"
"Chaaaaarge!"
Thirty knights charged all at once.
The charge, honed as sharp as an awl, split the monsters in half.
"Good work."
Since the monsters weren’t many, the battle ended quickly.
Luina wiped the blood off her sword and fed a carrot to her horse, which was exhaling rough breaths.
"You did well too, my lady. Things have really stabilized a lot."
Although she had returned to the family in less than half a year, there was quite a difference from before she left.
The walls had been repaired extensively, and most of the monster nests that had formed throughout the domain after that day had been subjugated.
"His Excellency has worked hard."
"It’s thanks to everyone’s efforts. Let’s head back now. This seems sufficient."
Since the main purpose was reconnaissance, there was no need to stay longer after confirming that there were no new nests near the domain.
"Yes."
The reconnaissance team, purely composed of knights, returned to the domain.
"My lady, His Excellency is calling for you."
"My father?"
The Baron Berchef was in his study. As if he had been waiting for Luina, two cups of tea and refreshments were placed on the table.
"Welcome."
"According to the reconnaissance, no new monster nests were discovered near Alsen."
"Good work. Have a cup of tea first. There’s chocolate that you like."
"I’ll enjoy it with gratitude."
Luina, who had been lacking sugar, unwrapped a chocolate and put it in her mouth.
’...It’s a bit lacking.’
Although it was certainly luxurious, it felt insufficient, perhaps because she had become too accustomed to kraken ink chocolates.
"Take this."
"What is this?"
"A letter has arrived for you."
It had the seal of Goldenheim, but it wasn’t from the head of the family.
"Gerhard?"
"When I heard that you had become friends with Gerhard and formed a pair, it was honestly hard to believe, but it seems it’s true. Looking at how you exchange letters during vacation."
"...It’s not like that. Did you open it by any chance?"
"I’m not so dishonorable as to freely open my daughter’s letter. Though I did want to open it right away."
Luina opened the letter.
There wasn’t much content.
[Demon species spotted.]
It was information and a warning for Luina. It was saying that there could be battles with demon species after the vacation ended, so she should prepare sufficiently.
’It seems like he’s also asking me to come a bit earlier.’
That’s probably right.
"May I ask what the content is?"
"There’s nothing particularly special."
Since she had agreed to keep the secret about Gerhard and the demon species, she couldn’t tell.
"If there’s nothing special, you can show it to me, right?"
"Why do you want to see it?"
"The Goldenheim family are grateful people who lent us money, but at the same time, they’re people who have shackled us with the chains of debt. I’m not sure if it’s right for you to be friendly with Gerhard Goldenheim."
"Gerhard promised a three-year exemption from interest."
"I know. Thanks to that, we’ve been able to breathe much more easily."
Nevertheless.
"The suspicion hasn’t disappeared. Why? Why would that family, obsessed with money, make such a promise to you and keep it? Given the large amount borrowed, the interest is not insignificant. Why would they willingly give that up?"
"That’s..."
"No matter how much I think about it, there’s only one answer I can come up with. But I don’t want you to be married off like being sold because of debt."
Luina’s face lightly flushed.
"...It’s not like that!"
"Then can’t you show me?"
"..."
"I think that letter is from that dishonorable Gerhard who is oppressing my precious daughter. I’ve had to suppress the urge to open it many times since it arrived."
"..."
Under the baron’s cold gaze, Luina bit her lip. After hesitating for a long time, she asked.
"Then please promise that you will not speak of this content to anyone."
"I will."
"On your honor as a father?"
"I will."
Luina carefully handed over the letter. After looking at it for a long time, the baron stood up.
"Father?"
"Follow me."
"Where are we suddenly going?"
"You’ll know when we get there."
The place they arrived at was deep within the family quarters.
"Open the door."
"Yes, Your Excellency."
The door guarded by soldiers opened, revealing stairs leading underground.
"I’ve always wondered. Those who don’t know well might think of the north as just a hell overflowing with monsters, but the reality is different."
Monsters were close to beasts, but ultimately, they were living creatures on this continent. They had their own laws and ecosystem.
"But that day was different. An unimaginable number of monsters flooded in, and the domain collapsed."
They barely managed to hold out, but it was literally just barely. Most of the domain was destroyed, and numerous troops and citizens died.
Without the help of other domains and the Empire, and the loans from Goldenheim, Berchef would never have been able to rise again.
"It was something that could never have happened."
So while rebuilding the domain, they sought the cause.
"And I discovered it. It was just recently."
"What are you talking about?"
Creak—
The door to the underground storage opened.
There was a corpse.
A corpse that was filthy, disgusting, and instinctively unpleasant.
"...Could this be?"
"Your suspicion is correct. Thanks to this, I was able to understand the reason."
Why that disaster occurred that day.
How dozens of different species of monsters came down as one.
"They weren’t coexisting to invade us."
They were just driven away after losing their territory to a stronger force.
"Magic beasts have nested in that polar region."
"...!"
"So answer me clearly, Luina."
The baron met his daughter’s eyes.
"What is happening at the academy?"
Luina could not keep the secret until the end.

chapters.title: Chapter 108: Countdown to Chaos [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 108: Countdown to Chaos [1]
While Luina was spending several sleepless nights blaming herself for betraying her honor.
In Gerhard’s mind, the future was being drawn once again.
["People are acting strange!"
<It’s magic energy! They’re infected with magic energy!>
"Are you saying the students made contracts with demons?"
<No, that’s not it. If that were the case, I wouldn’t have missed it.>]
When the content revealed by the prophecy ended, the next future would emerge. This time was no different.
[- It’s Andromalius! These crazy fools, summoning a demon in the middle of the academy!
"We have to stop it...!"
The aura of a real demon, not a demon species or a magic beast, was incomparable.
The suffocating pressure and thick magic energy that came just from its existence frightened Aint.
"Huff, huff, huff...!"
His heart rate increased and his breathing became rough.
<Are you alright?>
Nevertheless, Aint slapped both his cheeks and barely held onto his sanity.
"I have to be. I came here to stop that thing."
He had no certainty that he could do it, but he felt a sense of duty that he had to.
It wasn’t some petty sense of justice or a chosen people complex.
If he didn’t stop it, everyone would die. The continent would perish, his future would disappear as well.
It was an instinctive attachment to survival.]
There was also the hero’s internal conflict.
[- It’s the branch of the World Tree! The branch of the World Tree is becoming the most powerful source of magical power for the summoning circle!
<Damn those academy people. When did they bring it in? No, did they fail to properly manage such an important thing?>]
["Senior! What are you...!"
"Aint Armian. You said it."
To become your knight.
And I had refused it.
"It was because of pride, but not anymore. I’ve come to know you, and your cause."
So this is my destiny.]
[Luina charged toward the demon, Andromalius. The blue sword energy shone brilliantly.
"No...!"]
There were futures that Gerhard already knew.
["...Senior, Senior!"
At the sight of Luina slowly falling, Aint shed tears of blood.
At that moment, the aura that he thought had completely dried up began to surge.
Inspired by Aint’s anger, it continuously welled up like an inexhaustible spring.
<Aint, it’s dangerous!>
It was the power of light sealed in the sword. It exceeded the level that his body could handle, but that didn’t matter anymore.]
There was also a future he was seeing for the first time, but that was certainly hopeful.
"So it really begins now."
Are we really going to fight against a demon?
Even for someone like Gerhard, it was inevitable to feel tension.
And there were also questions.
"Yes. Ariadne Florian is protecting the branch of the World Tree."
Gerhard got up from the bed, grabbing his head. His clothes and bed were soaked as if he had taken a bath in sweat.
"But why did the academy get caught off guard in an instant without knowing anything?"
Ariadne Florian was a character who would become Aint’s companion, so the conclusion was one of two possibilities.
Either she was a demon species disguised as a companion, or she had been overcome by demon species and handed over the branch of the World Tree.
Considering that Aint Armian had a way to find demon species, the latter possibility was higher than the former.
That’s why, even though he knew, he deliberately didn’t mention that part. It was something that had to happen eventually, and Aint had to grow more because of it.
Though he had attached Veriana as a precaution against the worst, he didn’t think it could perfectly block the demon species.
"Young Master, are you awake?"
Knock knock, Hyde opened the door and entered.
"Are you feeling ill? Your sweat..."
"I just had a bit of a restless sleep."
"It seems more than just a bit..."
"Nevermind. What is it?"
"A letter has arrived from Luina Berchef."
A reply, perhaps. Gerhard unfolded the torn letter stamped with the seal of the Berchef family.
[I’m sorry. I failed to keep my promise to maintain the secret. I have no excuse, even if I had ten mouths.]
At the unpleasant beginning, Gerhard’s brow twitched.
[I had no choice but to tell my father everything. About what happened at the academy, about the magic beasts and demon species.]
[I will certainly pay the price for this.]
She told him everything?
What if things go wrong and the future gets twisted? What if Aint doesn’t grow as foretold in the prophecy book?
A person calling herself a knight breaking a promise made on her honor?
’No, calm down.’
Luina is a steadfast knight. If she broke a promise made on her honor, there must have been a compelling reason.
Gerhard calmly read the rest of the content.
[...Do you remember why our family was in danger? The incident where the domain was devastated by an unprecedented large-scale invasion. I didn’t know, but my father had been investigating it.]
[...It was magic beasts.]
...What?
Crumple, Gerhard’s hand clenched as he read the letter.
[In the north, far north of the Berchef domain, traces of magic beasts nesting were discovered. Father thinks monsters were pushed away by the magic beasts. I think the same.]
"...If that’s the case, could it be."
On the first day when he was struck by lightning and learned about the prophecy book, the two things that remained most vividly in Gerhard’s memory were:
The falling Gerhard.
And the large-scale magic beast legions moving south from the north.
"Is it starting from the north of Berchef...?"
Gerhard was filled with joy. When the cause of a problem is known, it’s as good as half solved.
Moreover, the location was good.
If the Berchef, who have lived by battling monsters from the beginning, deliberately prepare defenses?
’Perhaps we can block the advance of magic beasts more easily than expected.’
Just knowing this fact was a significant achievement. Enough to overlook Luina’s breaking of the promise.
’Of course, that won’t do.’
It was a thoroughly understandable reason, but since she said she would pay the price herself...
What should I take from her?
"What’s in the content that makes your face unfold after being wrinkled?"
"It’s about demon species. And it’s not particularly bad news."
Gerhard got up from the bed.
"I need to wash up first. Bring my clothes."
"Yes."
"And prepare immediately. I’m curious about how things are going."
Everything he wanted to accomplish after returning to the family had been achieved.
It was now time to return to the academy, and the moment of the decisive battle was approaching.
In the broader context, this was just the beginning, but it was the first encounter with a demon.
***
If there’s something lost, there’s also something gained.
Due to an unexpected variable, Barosu was seriously injured, and an unexpected person learned about the demon species, but just as he obtained unexpected information from Luina.
"...I’m sorry."
And just as her trust in Luina was somewhat broken, he could gain her sense of guilt and regret.
While returning to the academy and unpacking in Lavidus Hall, a visitor came.
Luina Berchef immediately bowed her head in apology.
"Regardless of the reason, it was my oversight not to keep my promise."
"It’s fortunate that you’re aware of it."
Honestly, if Gerhard were in the same position, he wasn’t confident he could keep the secret either. He had even spoken to his father first.

chapters.title: Chapter 109: Countdown to Chaos [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 109: Countdown to Chaos [2]
But that was that, and this was this. There was no reason not to seize a weakness willingly offered.
Especially when the other party was a future Royal Knight.
"I won’t blame you right now. But I don’t know what kind of request I might make in the future."
"One thing, anything I can do, I will accept."
"Good."
After tentatively wrapping up the conversation, Gerhard changed the subject.
"So, what does Baron Berchef of the Borderlands plan to do now?"
"Since only a small number of magic beasts have been discovered so far, he said he would investigate more thoroughly."
Does he intend to blow it open after gathering sufficient signs and evidence?
Anyway, once the demon is summoned, it can no longer be a secret, so it didn’t matter as long as it was blown open after that.
"I see. There might be a battle soon."
"Is it what you mentioned in the letter?"
"Yes."
No, it was a lie. Not a demon species, but a demon.
"It’s a different entity from what we’ve faced so far. It won’t be easy, so it’s good to prepare mentally in advance."
He didn’t bother to correct that it was a demon. The difference between a demon and a demon species was just one character, but the weight was different.
If Luina learned about the demon, she would try to borrow external power rather than resolving it with our strength.
Such as the academy or family.
And that was also the natural course. That’s why it had to be hidden until the end.
"Yes."
Luina nodded, determined.
’Honestly, it’s a bit worrying, but we’ll be able to stop it.’
Even if it’s a demon, in the prophecy book, it was at a level that Aint could handle sufficiently. Probably because it was a hastily arranged summoning.
For the sake of the future, it had to be handled by Aint, by Aint’s hands.
’It’s not like there aren’t points that make me wonder.’
The reason demon species move as carefully as possible is probably because their preparations aren’t complete. That’s why the summoned Andromalius was defeated by an Aint who was still not fully ripened.
Why would they, who had been moving so carefully, suddenly take the reckless action of summoning an incomplete demon?
’It’s because they were anxious about Aint growing faster than expected.’
At least that’s how it was in the original history. Probably. Attempts to kill Aint had failed several times in the original history.
’Nothing changes.’
Andromalius will be summoned, and Aint will kill it.
And he becomes a hero and grows, going on to completely exterminate demons.
That was the future ahead.
***
Veriana blankly looked up at the sky.
’What was I trying to do?’
Lately, she had been experiencing a foggy head frequently.
’I keep forgetting things, am I getting old?’
She hadn’t heard of forgetfulness coming at the age of 20.
"Ah."
A clock placed on one side of the wall caught her eye. 2:10. Belatedly, she remembered the seasonal semester class at 3.
"Right. I was going to go to class. Or was I already on my way? There’s still 50 minutes..."
Suddenly, her gaze turned forward. She found Ariadne who was staring blankly at a wine glass with a similar expression.
"...Why are you here?"
"I don’t know either. Why am I here?"
Veriana and Ariadne stared at each other blankly.
"Eyes like rotten pollack."
"...Huh?"
"Senior Gerhard? What brings you here?"
The human and the elf tilted their heads in incomprehension.
"What are you two doing? I called you here. Is your memory at the level of a mudskipper?"
Gerhard reached out and picked up two notes placed on the table.
[To the tea house.]
They were notes Gerhard had sent to the two.
"Ah, come to think of it, I came here to meet you, Senior..."
"Come to think of it, I did too..."
The elf and human looked at each other and frowned.
"...Don’t tell me."
And Gerhard recognized the seriousness of the situation.
***
A few weeks before Gerhard and Luina returned to the academy.
Veriana Kalproten was leisurely tilting a wine glass.
She was one of the few students who remained at the academy during the vacation period.
’There’s nothing to gain by going home before showing something to make up for it.’
For a loser who had lost in a duel that should never have been lost, the only path left was exile.
It was ultimately an escape, but it couldn’t be helped.
"So you didn’t go back?"
"That’s right."
Veriana took a sip of beer.
Fortunately, there was an appropriate excuse. The seasonal semester that the academy held during vacation.
After sending a letter saying she would push herself harder as a pretext for the defeat, she stayed at the academy.
"Such a childish excuse."
"...And why did you stay?"
"Who knows."
The red-haired elf, Ariadne, propped her chin and munched on a cracker topped with prosciutto and cheese. The bittersweet and salty flavor wasn’t bad.
"Just because?"
The superficial reason was her friendship with the newly appointed spirit studies professor, and the internal reason was the protection of the World Tree.
"By the way, I wanted to get close to Aint, but somehow among the first years, I ended up talking to you first."
It wasn’t a coincidence.
It was rare for students to stay at the academy during vacation, and the few remaining students naturally had more contact.
’The Kalproten family isn’t too bad either.’
Although not a sovereign household, it was a wealthy family closely following below. With wide domains under its command and many forces, it was called a great noble family.
From any perspective, becoming friends would bring more gain than loss.
"That Aint, Aint. Are you all about Aint too? What’s so lacking about me compared to Aint?"
"Skill."
"...I admit it because I lost."
Veriana barely acquiesced with a trembling brow.
"And family."
"It seems to me that the Kalproten family is much better than the Armian family, which has completely collapsed."
"But you’re not a sovereign household."
"Damn sovereign households...!"
Certainly, there was a weight that came with the name ’sovereign household.’
Not just simple honor, but substantial rights as well. There was a wall that could never be crossed between sovereign households and ordinary nobles.
Especially Armian, which may have completely shrunk in power, but still remained a great family in the hearts of the people.
It’s said that even Schwaben hesitates and can’t change the name of the empire because of this.
"But for someone who hates Aint, you seem to get along well with him?"
"That’s...!"
"Anyway, you’re isolated in the department, and so is Aint. I want you two to overcome that hardship together."
"What’s important is that I have a recording orb that recorded the moment you became a demon transformation."
It was because someone who held his leash wanted it.
"Aint Armian is already chasing other demon species. If you stick by his side, you’ll eventually encounter the one who made you like this."
But it wasn’t solely because of that.
Revenge. Veriana wanted to find the culprit who had polluted her and turned her into a demon transformation to get revenge.
"...That’s your misconception."
But since she couldn’t tell the truth, she shook her head and took another sip of beer.
"I’ll say so."
"Thaanks for letting it go."
I really don’t like these elves.
’But maybe I should have gone back home regardless of how I would be treated...’
Veriana tried to push down the intense anxiety with alcohol.
"Ah, by the way, could you come to the forest later for a moment?"
"The forest?"
"Yes, you asked why I stayed earlier? Actually, a branch of Mother Tree is planted here, and I’m guarding it."
"...What?"
Startled by the sudden secret, Veriana blinked in confusion.
"Is it okay to tell me something like that?"
"Originally, it’s not. But it seems there’s a problem with the branch of Mother Tree. I think I’ll need help in case of an emergency."
"Why me?"
"Senior Gerhard said so. That you could be trusted to ask for help."
"...What?"
Ariadne smiled brightly and leaned forward, lowering her body.
"Demon transformation."
A quiet whisper penetrated her ear.
"He said if I mention that, you would unconditionally help while keeping the secret."
"...Gerhard Goldenheim, you damn human!"
"You have a bad way of speaking about Senior. I’ll tell him everything."
"Whether you tell him or not..."
Wait a minute.
"Then you also know about demon species...?"
"I’ve fought magic beasts to the point of exhaustion. You could call me the Hero of Reversal."
"...What nonsense are you talking about?"
What do you mean.
"I’m saying I might need your help."
Ariadne shrugged.
"Am I such a pushover that I’ll help unconditionally when you ask?"
"So you’re not going to help?"
"Damn it."
Veriana cursed.
Despite getting heated, she felt like crying at her situation where she couldn’t refuse.

chapters.title: Chapter 110: Memory’s Betrayal [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 110: Memory’s Betrayal [1]
The story that demon species were targeting a branch of Mother Tree.
Normally, it would have been an unbelievable tale—something from children’s fairy tales or the exaggerated rumors that occasionally circulated among first-year students—but because the one who said it was Gerhard Goldenheim, with his piercing golden eyes and reputation for unfailing accuracy, and because she had already encountered magic beasts with her own eyes during the spring expedition to the northern forests, Ariadne had no choice but to believe it. The memory of those beasts, with their twisted forms and eyes that gleamed with an unsettling intelligence, still haunted her dreams.
’Even if I hadn’t met magic beasts, I might have pretended to accept it? That would have been fun in its own way.’
Of course, since it was all to gain Gerhard Goldenheim’s favor—the third-year student whose magical prowess was legendary even beyond the academy walls—the feeling was entirely different. His acknowledgment would mean more than any academic achievement she could hope for this term.
Anyway, she intended to do her best to protect Mother Tree, carefully following the ancient protection rituals that had been passed down through generations of elven families, which was also why she remained at the academy when everyone else returned home for the mid-season break. While her classmates enjoyed family feasts and hometown celebrations, Ariadne spent her evenings studying protective enchantments and her mornings inspecting the sacred branch, her footsteps echoing through the empty corridors of the usually bustling academy.
After several weeks like that—weeks of solitude broken only by occasional letters from her sister Nania and brief encounters with the few professors who had stayed behind—an anomaly was discovered in the previously quiet fragment of Mother Tree. It was subtle at first, just a slight discoloration at the edge of one leaf, easily missed by anyone who wasn’t looking for it specifically. But to Ariadne’s trained eye, it was as alarming as a scream in the night.
"...Part of it is contaminated?"
When did this happen?
Though she wasn’t attached to it like providing 24-hour security, she had faithfully come to check its condition two or three times a day.
’This couldn’t have happened in just a few hours.’
It was more likely that it had been slowly seeping in, but only now became noticeable.
Even though it was a branch of Mother Tree, it wasn’t as if smooth communication was possible, so this seemed more plausible.
’Just as Senior said, demon species at the academy...’
There was no other explanation. She decided to examine the recording orbs that Gerhard had installed.
But besides herself, no one had been captured.
’How?’
Ariadne, faced with a cascade of questions, examined various places around the branch.
The answer was underground. The contamination was starting from the roots.
"...It seems like this isn’t a problem I can solve alone."
If Gerhard had been there, she could have run to him, but unfortunately, he wasn’t. Then there was no choice but to find a suitable alternative.
Someone trustworthy and strong.
Ariadne first sought out Veriana. Since Gerhard had revealed the secret for use in emergencies, there was nothing to hesitate about.
"There you are, Miss Ariadne."
As Ariadne was about to go find the Spirit Studies professor next, someone called out to her.
"Teaching Assistant Imelda?"
Imelda was a teaching assistant brought by the newly appointed Spirit Studies professor Nania, and she was an elf.
"I’m sorry to ask suddenly, but could you go to Professor Dominic’s office right away?"
"What’s the matter?"
"Actually, Professor Dominic requested Professor Nania’s cooperation regarding research, but something came up suddenly and she can’t go."
Imelda added that it was research on integrating spirits and illusion magic.
"You’re asking a student to do this?"
"...Well."
"Fine, it’s okay. If it’s a request from my sister, I mean, the professor, it’s worth doing. Blood ties and regional ties are important, right? Oh, since you’ve come to the academy, academic ties too, I guess."
"...That’s."
"You said Professor Dominic, right?"
Ariadne disappeared with a smile.
***
"...So, it’s research on incorporating spirits into illusion magic. I needed help from people who can handle spirits most smoothly within the academy."
Professor Dominic, who had just finished explaining, pushed up his slipping glasses.
"I understand. Why my help is needed."
Spirit arts was a field particularly dependent on talent, and also a field where none were more excellent than the elves.
"It’s not something I should say to a student, but would you be able to help?"
"Yes, of course."
"Thank you very much. Ah, look at me. A guest has arrived and I haven’t even brought tea. What would you like?"
"Any suitable tea will do."
Professor Dominic brought tea and refreshments himself. He mixed an appropriate amount of creamer into the coffee and stirred it with a teaspoon.
"What Ariadne will actually need to do is simple. Illusion magic and spirits... I think the creamer is a bit insufficient."
More creamer was added, and he stirred with the teaspoon again.
"...I’m thinking of incorporating spirits into various elements of illusion magic to create more organic illusion magic. Illusion is ultimately about deceiving others’ senses, and if..."
A spoonful of sugar was added.
"If a living soul is combined, it becomes..."
Another spoonful. Ariadne unconsciously shifted her gaze to the teaspoon making circles in the cup.
"You like it quite sweet."
"A bit childish, isn’t it? But I can’t handle bitter things well."
Professor Dominic continued his explanation with an awkward smile. Meanwhile, another spoonful of sugar was added, and the teaspoon continued to swim in the cup.
Her eyes kept being drawn to it.
"...Do you understand?"
"So when realizing the magic circle, I just need to place them in designated positions and perform the movements you require. It doesn’t sound difficult."
"Yes. Not today though..."
After additional explanations, Ariadne left Professor Dominic’s office.
’Wait, then does that mean my sister Nania isn’t in her office right now?’
If she was busy enough to miss an appointment with another professor and send a student as a substitute, she must be quite occupied.
’Then who should I go to...’

chapters.title: Chapter 111: Memory’s Betrayal [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 111: Memory’s Betrayal [2]
At that moment, someone called her.
"Miss Ariadne."
"Teaching Assistant Aron."
"What brings you to the faculty building?"
"Professor Dominic called me and I helped him a little."
"Really? Professor Dominic asking a student for something, that’s unusual."
Aron smiled slightly and pulled forward the book he was holding.
"Oh, by the way, can I ask you something too?"
"What is it?"
"This is a book on spirit studies, but I don’t understand the content..."
He carefully opened the book.
"Nothing..."
At that moment, their eyes met.
Ariadne felt a subtle light emanating from Aron’s pupils.
"Assistant, your eyes..."
"Eyes? What about my eyes?"
"No, nothing..."
Looking again, they were just ordinary eyes. Why am I suddenly like this? Ariadne shook her head.
"Where were you heading anyway?"
"Hmm, well..."
Where was I going?
Looking out the window, the sunset was approaching.
"To my dormitory. I feel tired, so I’m going to get some sleep."
"It is getting a bit late. Take care, see you next time."
"Yes."
Ariadne bowed slightly and disappeared.
***
That evening, after waiting for two hours at the meeting place, Veriana returned to Lavidus Hall, grinding her teeth.
"Damn Gerhard. He said it was a secret, but he’s spreading it all over the neighborhood."
Some method was needed.
Definitely.
And the next day, Veriana, who was about to confront Ariadne, felt a strange sense of déjà vu.
"Ah, by the way, could you come to the forest later for a moment?"
The same place.
The same person.
And even the same conversation.
Even the beginning was identical to yesterday.
"The forest?"
"Yes, actually, a branch of Mother Tree is planted here, and I’m guarding it. But it seems there’s a problem with it."
"Originally it’s not allowed, but you want to ask me for help because of a problem?"
"Huh?"
Ariadne frowned slightly.
"Gerhard told you that I could be trusted to ask for help, and even told you that I had become a demon transformation?"
"...How do you know that?"
Her eyes widened.
Hey. What are you doing?
