"Do I look like an idiot to you just because I lost to Aint?"
Veriana growled fiercely.
***
"...So I cursed at Ariadne, that stupid pointy-ear! Saying the same thing over and over, saying the same thing over and over! I thought she had dementia!"
Veriana proudly concluded her recollection.
"What happened next?"
"...Pardon?"
"I’m asking what happened after that."
"...Well."
She tilted her head.
"What did I do after that?"
"You probably didn’t do anything."
"Right, that must be it. If I had done something, I would remember more."
"You’re a genius, Veriana. So logical! As expected of the third-ranked in the Knight Department!"
"Not third, runner-up!"
"Are you an idiot? Aint is the runner-up!"
"Third place is good too!"
Gerhard let out a hollow laugh at the sight of the man and woman staring at each other and spouting nonsense.
It was a headache figuring out how to solve this. If only there was a method.
"How is it?"
"Brother is right. They’re affected by magic energy."
"I suspected as much, but it’s true."
"Yes. Judging by the brain being affected, it’s a mental-type magic. Tracing the remnants, it’s nothing impressive, just simple suggestion..."
The Saint, after examining the heads of the two, showed slight anger.
"The magic energy has accumulated bit by bit from frequent use, half-blocking the mana flow in the brain. That’s why they’re having memory problems. Those garbage demon species. They should all be exterminated."
"How many times would it take to get to this state?"
"At least more than ten times...?"
"What, these fools..."
They fell for the same trick not just once or twice, but more than ten times?
Was the demon species competent, or were Veriana and Ariadne just idiots?
"Is there a treatment method?"
"The magic energy itself is very minimal, so it’s not that difficult. It’s just that it’s the brain, so even a small amount causes problems. So..."
"It costs money?"
"As expected, brother understands at a glance."
He was truly consistent. But somehow that was reassuring. At least this guy didn’t seem to have been affected by demon species.
After all, a money ghost was scarier than a demon species.
"Using ’Holy Light’ on a person’s brain will definitely cause problems. You experienced it last time, didn’t you?"
"Do we really need to try it to know that?"
It seems like we could know that well enough without trying.
"Magic is also a science of verification; until definite results are seen, it remains unknown. Anyway, since the brain is a more sensitive part, I want to work more gently using holy water."
"Exactly how?"
"By using purification magic while their heads are submerged in holy water."
He went on to explain that the holy water would be absorbed comprehensively through the submerged skin and pores, as well as through the mouth and nostrils as they struggled.
"Is the purification magic safe?"
"I can assure you it’s much safer compared to ’Holy Light.’ It’s less effective, but with the help of holy water, we can somewhat cover for that."
"Then do it immediately."
There were many things to learn from these two idiots. Above all, what the state of the World Tree branch was.
"However, since it involves touching the brain and nerves, the pain will be quite substantial."
"It doesn’t matter. It’s not my body."
"Indeed, the soundproofing here is quite excellent. Then, how about the cost?"
"I’m not their guardian."
"The Fridien and Kalproten families should be able to pay sufficiently. I’ll proceed that way. Could I borrow two basins?"
When the shop’s clerk brought two small basins, Jayce poured holy water into each.
"...Huh? What are you—!"
"What is... this—!"
And he grabbed the back of the heads of the two dazed individuals and submerged them in the holy water.
"Guwaaaggglblrblp...!"
"Kyaaarrrlglblp...!"
Bubbles rose with their violent struggles.
"Everything is God’s will. This too is a trial placed before you. If you endure with patience, evil will eventually be punished."
A seemingly sacred light seeped into their heads.
"S-save... mmblblb!"
"You will not die. Only demons die."
May the blessing of mana be upon you.
"I-it’s going in through my nohlrrlrlr...!"
"Yes, it needs to enter through your mouth and ears as well."
"You crazlglglblp!"
"It seems the purification is not complete yet. Repent. You were seduced by magic energy and abandoned mana, but the great mana is generous."
Jayce reverently bowed his head, applying more force to his hands pressing down on their heads.

chapters.title: Chapter 112: Corrupted Origins [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 112: Corrupted Origins [1]
"....."
"....."
Two people, a man and a woman with their hair soaking wet from holy water, stared blankly at the ceiling.
"Your lifeless eyes suggest the purification is still incomplete. As a Saint, I cannot allow inadequate work, so once more..."
"No, that’s enough!"
"You call yourself a Saint?!"
Ariadne Florian and Veriana Kalproten jumped in surprise and spat out curses. Jayce smiled contentedly at their reaction.
"The purification is complete, brother."
"Good work."
"Yes, brother, could I possibly get two sheets of paper?"
Gerhard Goldenheim handed over some paper from a private room. Jayce scribbled something on them and handed them to Ariadne and Veriana.
"What’s this...?"
"An invoice."
"An invoice?"
"I’ve removed the demonic energy from your minds, so naturally you must pay for it, don’t you think?"
Veriana quietly accepted the invoice, but after checking the numbers written on it, shouted angrily.
"What, you swindler...! This is daylight robbery!"
"That’s right! Veriana is absolutely correct!"
Despite their angry voices, Jayce calmly shrugged his shoulders.
"Expensive, you say? I, a Saint, personally removed the demonic energy from the minds of noble-blooded individuals like yourselves. How is that expensive?"
"...Well."
"I suppose my services aren’t that cheap. I’ll pay it as is, whatever."
"Your change of attitude is too quick!"
"It’s good that people with large ears are so generous." The Saint smiled in an extremely worldly manner.
"That’s the first time I’ve heard that."
Could the words ’elf’ and ’generous’ coexist? Gerhard snorted.
"...Fine."
When Ariadne accepted the invoice, Veriana couldn’t stay angry anymore. After all, there was nothing wrong with what Jayce had said.
"Then I would appreciate it if you could pay as soon as possible. Brother, I’ll be going now."
"You said you’re busy?"
"Yes. As the Saint of the Order, I have many duties during the festival..."
Soon it would be the founding anniversary, when the first Emperor defeated King Colomo and declared the establishment of the Empire.
A festival would also be held at the Academy, and Jayce had to preside over the event as the Saint of the Dragon Faith Order.
"I’ll let you know if we find any clues about the demonic species."
"I appreciate it."
Jayce disappeared.
"Well then, let’s start properly again."
Gerhard propped his chin and glared at Ariadne and Veriana.
"What happened to you two during that time?"
"Um..."
Ariadne blinked.
"I don’t think anything special happened. At least not in my memory... or did it?"
"...Even with the demonic energy removed, the memories themselves aren’t fully restored."
Actually, it would be more accurate to say that the memories from before losing their memories due to demonic energy were flowing smoothly, but memories from when they were contaminated remained vague.
"What about you, Veriana?"
"...I don’t think there was anything special for me either. If there’s one thing that remains, it’s that I listened to this pointy-eared one saying the same thing in the same place, just at different times. Several times."
"What did she say?"
"Well, that’s..."
The answer came from Ariadne.
"That there was a problem with the Mother Tree! Probably. Or not? Well, it should be right. And following your advice, I was looking for Veriana to hire a reliable chess piece. Probably?"
With those words, Gerhard could more clearly conclude how the demon had been summoned in the original history.
’They put a suggestion on Ariadne, the caretaker, to prevent her from reporting the anomaly, and proceeded with their plan in the meantime.’
That future had changed with Gerhard’s intervention.
Originally, Ariadne would have known about it alone and then forgotten, but because of Gerhard, it had also reached Veriana, who had remained instead of exiting the scene.
Plus now there were Gerhard and Jayce as well.
’Perhaps...’
He thought they might be able to prevent the summoning of Andromalius now.
Although he didn’t know the exact date of Andromalius’s summoning, he knew it was before school reopened.
It was the time when students were returning one by one to the Academy, and the island that had been quiet during the vacation was becoming lively again.
There were still two weeks left until school reopened, and considering that not many students had returned yet, there was still some time.
The plan to catch the demonic species and prevent the summoning during that time seemed entirely feasible.
Of course, it was just a possibility; he didn’t actually intend to do so.
’Perhaps the demonic species are already aware of this meeting as well?’
Ariadne would be a major target for their surveillance.
"Tell me. Who are all the people you met during the vacation?"
"There were quite a lot. Professor Nania Beris, Professor Ilayer, Professor Grad Xant, Professor Deoni, Assistant Miller, Assistant Aron Praine, Assistant Pierce, Senior Nofen, Senior Clio, Oh, I also met Professor Vallenod! And Professor Rosalia Wienderk! And..."
Gerhard, who had been writing down all the names that were endlessly coming out, stopped his pen.
"Are you going to name everyone at the Academy?"
"But I met them all during the vacation."
"I’m asking if there’s anyone suspicious."
"I don’t know. I feel like there was someone, but it’s hazy, like being in a fog."
Not helpful at all. Gerhard’s gaze turned to Veriana.
"It’s the same for me. No one particularly suspicious..."
"This is giving me a headache."
He thought he had found a good lead, but he was mistaken.
’Well, it wouldn’t be easy to catch them anyway.’
These were beings who hadn’t left a trace despite operating covertly for quite a long time. There was no way to find their traces so easily.
’When I think about it, Andromalius being summoned is clearly the opposite of their actions so far. It’s certain that Aint is that dangerous to them...’
Otherwise, there would be no reason for it.
"I guess we should check the World Tree branch first."
That was the only option for now.
"...Let’s go."
"Let’s go!"
"Me too?"
"No, you’re not needed."
Gerhard rose from his seat.
***
"Oh my goodness, Mother Tree! Why have you become like this!"
Even without Ariadne wailing loudly, the condition of the World Tree branch looked serious.
The branches and leaves were all stained pitch black, and even the surrounding ground was contaminated black.

chapters.title: Chapter 113: Corrupted Origins [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 113: Corrupted Origins [2]
It looked like the infiltration was complete.
And that wasn’t all.
Crack-
"Ouch...!"
When Ariadne reached out her hand, demonic energy burst out, causing a violent rebound. She screamed and took a step back.
"...This is serious."
The funny thing was that despite being in such a state, almost no demonic energy could be felt from the outside. Whether it was due to the excellent concealment magic of the demonic species or the special nature of the World Tree branch, he wasn’t sure.
"Ariadne, can you purify it?"
"I really hate to say this, but it’s impossible."
Ariadne explained that not a bit of forest energy remained.
"That’s no longer the incarnation of the Mother Tree, but something else wearing its guise."
It was similar to an undead. Just because you raise an undead from a dead corpse doesn’t mean the undead is the same person as the owner of the corpse.
Although it might inherit some of the abilities that the original body had.
"So it’s already too late."
"...It’s my fault. If only I hadn’t stupidly fallen for mind magic...! There must have been several chances to reverse it!"
Ariadne muttered with bloodshot eyes.
The importance of the World Tree to elves could be guessed from the name they called it.
Gerhard couldn’t even begin to imagine how an elf would feel seeing an incarnation of such a World Tree contaminated by demonic species.
’Would it be similar if I were to completely fall from grace?’
Imagining it was truly horrifying. Crunch, Gerhard ground his teeth, cursing the demonic species.
"I’ll definitely catch whoever did this and tear them limb from limb! I swear on my name! I’ll make them feel to the bone what the price is for daring to touch the Mother Tree!"
So first!
Ariadne pulled out her staff. The surrounding mana began to gather around her like a storm.
"Let me put the incarnation of the Mother Tree at ease."
"...What?"
At her sudden impulsive action, Gerhard rushed between the contaminated incarnation and Ariadne.
"Wait, stop, Ariadne. No matter what, it’s still an incarnation of the World Tree. Are you saying you’ll just destroy it? As an elf?"
"It’s a hundred times better for me to destroy it with my own hands than to let it be used by those demonic creatures. My father would praise me for it."
No, maybe the Mother Tree would be angry that her incarnation had been completely corrupted by demonic species. Ariadne looked dejected.
"Anyway, destroying it is the right thing to do!"
"But won’t that completely void the contract with the Academy? Are you okay with that?"
"...Well."
The World Tree’s incarnation was by no means solely the property of the elves.
It was the result of a deal between the Academy and Fridien, and it would be hasty to completely smash it based solely on Ariadne’s judgment just because it had gone a bit (?) wrong.
"...Then what do you suggest? Do you have a way?"
"What were you planning to do?"
"I was going to ease the Mother Tree’s final journey and report to my father. After all, this is a problem I can’t solve on my own."
"I have a better method."
"What is it?"
"First, we get help from Jayce. And we also get help from the holy water that healed your mind."
Ariadne wore an unconvinced expression.
"Pouring a top-grade potion on a corpse won’t bring it back to life."
"This case is different. It’s the World Tree branch."
"Hmmmm."
"I’m also thinking of getting help from Aint. If the legitimate successor of Armian, known as the natural enemy of demons, might have at least one method. Isn’t it better to place some hope rather than giving up like this?"
"Well, that’s true..."
Hearing her halfway convinced tone, Gerhard nodded.
Contrary to his words, he had no intention of healing the World Tree branch. His purpose was merely to buy time with all sorts of excuses.
To leave the World Tree as it was so that Andromalius could be summoned.
There would be some damage to the Academy, but Aint’s growth was ultimately for the benefit of all humanity, so it was a beneficial direction for everyone.
In the process, the World Tree branch would become the medium for summoning, but why should he care? If the demon destroyed the World Tree branch, no one could say anything.
It wasn’t even the real World Tree, and there was no way a mere young incarnation could stand against a demon.
"Trust me. Have you ever lost out by believing my words?"
"I haven’t particularly gained anything either? We don’t have that kind of history between us."
That was true. He had habitually spoken to her as he would to Luina Berchef.
Certainly, the approach should be different for Ariadne compared to Luina, with whom trust had been built throughout the first semester.
"Is going through the battlefield together not enough?"
"It’s a business trip."
"To a merchant, those who go on business trips together are comrades."
"Not to elves."
Then for Ariadne Florian, a method befitting her should be used.
"Fine. Emond Altriark, the Knight Faculty professor in charge of third-year students."
"What?"
"I’ll introduce you."
"...Oh."
After a momentarily blank expression, she instinctively nodded.
"Okay!"
He was of the Altriark Frontier Count family lineage, another pillar supporting the Empire.
Although far from succession, being a direct descendant with the Altriark name was what mattered.
"I’ll trust you, senior. We are comrades who fought together after all."
"Not because of connections?"
"I can’t say that doesn’t have an influence. But still..."
Ariadne’s eyes momentarily lowered heavily.
"Even if it’s just a corpse, I can’t bear to see the Mother Tree’s branch being used by those demon bastards. When I said I would destroy it with my own hands rather than that, I meant it."
Her will to smash it immediately if things went even slightly wrong was palpable.
"I’ll keep that in mind."
Ah, and this is the main point.
"By the way, are you good at spirit magic?"
"Is that like asking a monkey if it knows how to climb trees?"
"If you help me, I’ll introduce you to one more person."
"Who is it?"
Ariadne’s eyes sparkled brightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 114: Broken Skies [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 114: Broken Skies [1]
The demonic energy explodes.
The mercenaries fall, and Barosu Drage charges into the gap.
’No...!’
He screams as if wailing, but no voice comes out.
—!
With a thunderous sound, Barosu is thrown back.
Demonic energy extending like tentacles pounces on his fallen form.
Immediately after, his body, which had remained motionless until now, moves forward.
Flash-
A pure white light flickers, cutting off all the demonic energy.
The light, which shines brilliantly using anger as nourishment, charges directly toward the evil.
"Impossible...! Already at this level? Indeed, I can never let you live!"
With the evil’s roar, light and darkness collide.
At that moment, Aint Armian opened his eyes.
"....."
He had realized it was a dream about halfway through.
A replay of the past that wouldn’t have happened if he had been just a little stronger.
<Your clothes are soaked with sweat. Did you have that dream again?>
"Yes. I just can’t seem to shake it off."
<Unnecessary anxiety.>
<That filthy demonic creature ultimately fell to your sword.>
<He was injured, but ultimately woke up, and there was a healer’s opinion that he could recover if rehabilitation went well. You don’t need to worry and be anxious anymore.>
Gardner Alpenfassen was right.
Barosu had suffered a critical injury and was in danger, but he survived the crisis.
It was a blessing in disguise—not only was the demonic energy completely driven out by the elixir brought by the Mercenary King, but it even led to growth due to it.
And the demonic species had fallen to Aint’s hands.
"...Can we really call that a victory?"
But it wasn’t such a smooth process.
He became angry at Barosu’s injury, struggled desperately to survive, and in that struggle, gained new insights.
He could only say he was lucky.
<It’s not something like luck.>
<Enlightenment only comes to those who are prepared.>
<Well, you should thank that upstart Gerhard. If it weren’t for the Saint Bird’s heart he gave you, it would have been you who became a corpse.>
Indeed. Aint nodded.
Due to the butterfly effect caused by Gerhard’s intervention, Aint was rated more highly.
They didn’t know that as a result, a stronger demonic species had come.
"I know. I know all that..."
<Are you afraid that if a mere demonic species was this difficult, how would you face a real demon?>
At the pinpoint accurate words, Aint carefully nodded.
At this moment, neither his lineage as an Armian bloodline, nor his brilliant light swordsmanship said to be the natural enemy of demons, nor his pride in being chosen by the first Emperor was of any help.
<Yes, indeed, the current you might not be a match for demons. No, you are not. I can assert that.>
"...But the current me is different from the previous me, right?"
<...Was that too obvious?>
"It’s something you hear quite often in plays. I didn’t expect to hear it in real life."
Still, it’s somewhat comforting. Aint smiled faintly.
"You’re right, Gardner."
When he first enrolled, Aint was ranked 38th. A bit special, but not that extraordinary within the Academy.
That had changed.
By meeting Gardner, he defeated Anton who had been ranked 10th.
He grew even more while avoiding the demonic species’ ambushes and fighting the sea serpents.
And now, though his life had been somewhat in danger, ultimately Aint was the one who survived.
What if it had been Aint before entering the Academy? He would have died without even putting up a proper resistance, let alone achieving victory.
As Gardner said, Aint was clearly growing. At a frightening pace, too.
"Barosu almost died, but in the end, he survived, and I won against the demonic species. The Mercenary King now knows about the existence of the demonic species and has vowed to destroy them, so things have actually turned out well."
Yes, the situation had improved considerably.
"Unless a demon suddenly pops out of nowhere, there shouldn’t be any problems."
Aint felt hopeful.
<Right, and demons aren’t bugs crawling on the street that would just pop up out of nowhere.>
Knock knock-
"Lord Aint, Barosu Drage is asking if you’d like to have dinner together. Would that time be convenient for you?"
"Absolutely."
Having shaken off his idle thoughts, Aint’s face was exceptionally bright as he left the room.
***
"I still can’t believe it even with my own eyes. You killed that monster?"
"You didn’t actually see it with your own eyes, did you?"
"Ah, so the trash who got knocked out before even fighting properly should just shut up?"
"Are you trying to make me look like garbage?"
"That’s right."
Pffft, Barosu and Aint burst into laughter simultaneously.
"How’s the mercenary work? Is it manageable?"
"I’m getting a bit used to it now."
After Barosu woke up, Aint’s daily life became relatively monotonous.
Along with the surviving members of the Black Spear Mercenary Band, he carried out various missions, building up practical experience and familiarity with mercenary life, and visited Barosu after each mission ended.
"Ogres! Spread out and surround them!"
"Don’t face them head-on! Slowly wear them down and nibble away at their strength!"
From relatively easy extermination requests...
"This isn’t supposed to be gnoll territory...?"
"Protect the carriage. The carriage must not be damaged. It’s carrying things more valuable than all your lives combined!"
To merchant convoy escorts.
"I’d like to reach Albes in three days."
"To traverse it in three days, we need to go through Kalkan Gorge."
"That’s why I’m hiring mercenaries. The compensation is high because it’s dangerous."
To VIP escort missions.
In just forty days, Aint had become a seasoned mercenary who had perfectly completed seven missions.
"At least looking at your appearance, I could believe you’re a mercenary. If someone said an Armian bloodline was wearing tattered leather armor and doing mercenary work, no one would believe it."
"Even I couldn’t have imagined myself doing mercenary work until recently."
He was imperial royalty, even if fallen.
They say even bankrupt rich families can last three years, so what about an imperial family that had ruled the empire for nearly nine hundred years?
At the very least, he shouldn’t have had to wear smelly leather armor, sleep on the ground, and eat dried, withered jerky.
<That’s why this mercenary journey is even more valuable.>
<Complaining about tough jerky? In my time, I chewed and swallowed magical beasts while fighting demons.>
Aint chose not to respond to these remarks. Barosu checked the calendar and said:
"You’re leaving tomorrow?"
"Yes."
"Now that I think about it, the new semester is just around the corner."

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Broken Skies [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 115: Broken Skies [2]
The vacation that seemed so long now had only two weeks left. Even if he departed right tomorrow, it would be about a week after arriving at the Academy.
After that, the second semester would finally begin.
"...I was supposed to go too, originally."
"Get better soon and come back."
"I’ve taken a leave of absence for this semester."
Though he was recovering quickly, considering rehabilitation therapy, it would be unreasonable to return to school within this year.
With his body in this condition, there was no way he could keep up with the other students.
"Well, taking a semester off isn’t a big deal; I can catch up diligently with seasonal courses, but it’s a bit disappointing to miss the festival."
The Empire’s Founding Anniversary.
This day, when the first Emperor declared the establishment of the Empire, was the greatest holiday in the Empire, continuing for a thousand years, and festivals were held throughout the territory. Naturally, the Academy was no exception.
In particular, the Knight Faculty’s mounted spear competition and the Magic Faculty’s magic tournament had special significance.
"It would have been the perfect opportunity to break those knights’ jaws in the mounted spear competition and make the name of the Black Spear Mercenary Band known...!"
Indeed, Barosu’s mounted combat skills were beyond imagination. If he had participated in the mounted spear competition, he would certainly have achieved significant results.
"I’ll do well in your place."
"Why would you? Even though we’ve been mercenaries together long enough to call it the Black Spear Mercenary Band, I should handle my own business."
Well, still.
"Don’t lose while carrying our mercenary flag. If you’re going to lose, don’t say you lived with our mercenary band. It would damage our reputation."
"I’m ranked higher than you, you know?"
"Individual ranking and reputation are different matters."
Aint and Barosu looked at each other and chuckled.
He felt inexplicably warm inside. For Aint, this mercenary journey was beyond merely gaining practical experience; it was about gaining a reliable friend—no, a comrade.
"Anyway, I’ll be going."
"Okay, see you next time."
Aint returned to the Academy by taking a boat back the same way he had come.
After the yacht club incident, there were now quite a few patrol boats monitoring the Academy’s waters.
’Come to think of it, wasn’t there a new course on naval combat being established?’
After experiencing that chaos, they had no choice but to pay attention to sea battles as well.
The ship glided across the sea and arrived at the Academy. The port was overflowing with students returning, just like Aint.
<Where are you going? You should now be heading to Lavidus Hall, not such smelly places.>
"Ah. Right. That’s true."
He remembered that his dormitory had changed after becoming the second-ranked student, and he had moved his belongings right after the semester ended.
"To think I’d return here based on my own abilities. It feels quite novel."
Aint admired the classical appearance of Lavidus Hall. Previously, he had been a visitor coming to see Veriana, but now he was also a proud resident.
"Welcome, Lord Aint. I’ll escort you."
As he entered the lobby, the maids greeted him warmly. Aint coincidentally met Veriana, who was just coming out.
"Veriana, it’s been a while."
"Aint? Looks like you’re back now. Seems you’ve gotten lazy since becoming second-ranked?"
"Not particularly. Where are you going?"
"I’m going to see Senior Gerhard."
"Senior Gerhard? Let’s go together. Come to think of it, I have something to talk about too."
About the demonic species encountered in the Kingdom of Pragia. Though he had sent a letter once in between, there were many things to discuss in person.
"...Do as you please."
Veriana nodded with a reluctant expression.
"Did you go home during the vacation?"
"I didn’t go. I took seasonal courses."
"Ah, right. You mentioned that."
"What about you? Your aura seems a bit more... sharp now."
"I went to the Kingdom of Pragia for a bit."
"Pragia? Did you do mercenary work?"
"How did you know?"
"It’s obvious."
There were two places in this world with the most mercenaries. One was Berchef, and the other was Pragia.
The reason was naturally because of the abundance of monsters worth exterminating for money.
"Anyway, that’s why you seem a bit rough now."
"Is it that noticeable?"
"A guy who used to look gentle has become sharp; it would be stranger if it weren’t noticeable."
The conversation briefly ended with those words.
"But where are we going right now?"
"The southern forest."
"Senior Gerhard is there? Why?"
"You’ll understand when we get there. Ah, now that I think about it, he asked to notify him as soon as you arrived, so it should be fine if you come along."
"Me? Why?"
"I don’t know that much. Stop bothering me."
Silence fell once again.
After walking for a while, they finally stepped into the forest, and a strange feeling touched Aint’s senses.
"...Demonic energy?"
<It’s demonic energy.>
The unpleasantness had become all too familiar to him now.
Aint hesitated. And at that moment.
Rumble rumble-
Not far away, a massive black stem rose vertically, scattering a sound that shattered the air.
"...Kuh!"
"What is this...!"
The shockwave swept the surroundings. Aint and Veriana lowered their posture and swallowed their groans.
—!
The stem that had risen into the sky emitted waves. An opaque, hemispherical demonic energy covered the forest.
<...This is a barrier!>
"...What’s happening!"
"Veriana! What exactly is over there?"
"...Branch."
"Branch?"
"The World Tree branch is there. Half-contaminated."
"...What?"
He knew they had brought the World Tree branch because Gerhard had mentioned it.
But what was that?
<I thought the location was top secret, so they didn’t even tell us, but how does this guy know?>
<Wait, the World Tree branch is contaminated by demonic energy? Then, could this be...?>
These crazy people. How are they managing the World Tree? Gardner spat out curses.
Immediately after.
—!
A bizarre sound, difficult to express in human language, enveloped the inside of the barrier.
——!
It was an extremely unpleasant and chilling scream.
"...Tree?"
The stems wove together, forming a gigantic tree.
And that tree grew as if to pierce the sky, and indeed broke through the sky.
"...Is space breaking apart?"
Veriana’s mouth fell open. Aint’s gaze followed his.
Along the path where the branch extended, cracks formed in the sky, and shattered pieces fell to the ground.
<Could this be...!>
<No, that can’t be! This is absurd!>
’What is it, exactly!’
<If my guess is correct, this is...!>
At that moment, a pure white hand abruptly emerged from the crack.
Crack crack crack, as it forcibly widened the crack, the destruction of space accelerated.
Aint’s complexion turned pale at the terrible demonic energy filling the inside of the barrier.
<...It’s a demon.>
After the hand came an arm, then a head and torso.
<A demon is descending...!>
A monstrous being in human form, yet by no means could it be called human. And a snake coiling around its arm.
"...Andromalius."
The 72nd-ranked demon, Andromalius, had descended.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Fatal Timing [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 116: Fatal Timing [1]
Just a few days before Andromalius descended, when Aint Armian was returning to the Academy by ship.
The Academy was busy preparing for the new semester. Among them, Gerhard was the busiest person at the Academy.
"I hope the prepared items won’t be insufficient?"
"Yes. We’ve filled the warehouse with goods and even secured extras."
"It’s better to have too much than too little. If we can’t sell everything at the Academy, we can sell it elsewhere."
"Yes."
The start of the semester meant students returning, and wherever people gather, money flows.
"The merchants in town..."
"Professor Dominic needs teaching materials..."
Moreover, since a city had formed within the island, they didn’t target only students.
"What about the festival preparations?"
Above all, the second semester featured the Academy’s greatest festival, held in celebration of the Empire’s Founding Anniversary – a week-long spectacle of parades, magical demonstrations, feasting, and ceremonies that attracted visitors from across the continent. What had begun centuries ago as a simple day of patriotic observance had evolved into the island’s most anticipated event.
Supplying the necessary items and preparing facilities for this had long been the exclusive responsibility of the Golden Turtle Company.
"We shouldn’t be careless just because it’s something we always do. With so many distinguished guests coming, there shouldn’t be even the slightest problem."
"Yes."
"This is the best business opportunity of the year. Remember that how much we earn during this time determines our annual profit."
"Yes!"
The students, referred to as the future of the Empire, plus their parents and everyone else who came to see the festival.
The Academy’s festival was the second most magnificent among all the founding anniversary celebrations held throughout the Empire.
The first, of course, was the one held in the capital.
"That concludes today’s meeting."
"Thank you for your hard work!"
The two-hour meeting came to an end.
"What’s next on the schedule?"
"There’s a meeting with the Merchants’ Association."
"What about Aint Armian?"
"He hasn’t returned to the Academy yet."
"Then you go to the meeting with the Merchants’ Association instead."
Gerhard reviewed the meeting contents once more and stood up.
"...What are you planning to do now?"
"Field work."
"There’s no scheduled field work that requires you to leave tasks to me, is there?"
"I’ll tell you when I get back."
"I’m not a merchant."
"But you are a member of the company."
"I’ve never done any merchant work."
"Don’t worry. The employees will handle everything, so you just need to go and pretend to look important."
"...Wait, what kind of..."
Hyde laughed dryly, but Gerhard had already left.
"...He keeps forgetting that I’m not a merchant but a servant and bodyguard."
Haah, Hyde sighed.
***
After stopping by the warehouse, Gerhard grabbed various items.
"Um... Branch Manager?"
"I’ll record exactly what I’ve taken out, so don’t worry."
"Yes, understood...!"
Gerhard reassured the warehouse keeper and left.
In truth, as the vacation was ending, he was becoming increasingly anxious.
’Andromalius.’
The cause was, of course, the demon scheduled to be summoned.
Even though he knew through the prophecy book that a demon would descend and that Aint would defeat it, that knowledge couldn’t completely eliminate the fear that demons inspire.
’It’s a demon, after all. The first demon to appear on the continent in a thousand years.’
He couldn’t even begin to guess how powerful this demon would be.
’Can Aint really stop it? The future has already changed. Who knows what will happen next?’
Originally, he wouldn’t have been this anxious, but Barosu’s incident had a major impact.
The demonic species that Aint should have somehow defeated alone had not only severely injured Barosu but also killed several members of the Black Spear Mercenary Band.
Although it eventually fell to Aint’s hands, would the same result have occurred if Gerhard hadn’t assigned Barosu to him?
Today’s field work was a manifestation of that anxiety.
"You’re setting traps?"
"Yes."
The goal was to install as many traps and snares as possible around the World Tree branch to at least inflict some damage when Andromalius was summoned.
"But why are we going with Senior Luina?"
"Luina also knows about the demonic species."
He was bringing her as an escort, just in case.
Since Aint was the demonic species’ top priority, he thought the possibility of a demon being summoned while Aint was absent was significantly low.
Nevertheless, because of that slight possibility, he was bringing Luina along.
"Don’t worry. I won’t tell anyone about the World Tree branch."
"Can we trust her, Senior?"
"Luina is trustworthy."
"If you say so, I have no choice. But while I might be fine with it, I’m not sure if Senior Luina will be."
"The other person I was going to introduce to you is actually Luina."
At those words, both women’s faces changed simultaneously.
"...You were going to introduce me to Ariadne?"
"I made a promise."
"Don’t you know that it was Fridien who took the gold seal rights that our family possessed?"
"Goldenheim mediated. It was purchased with a fair price under mutual agreement, but are you really going to make an issue of that?"
"Of course not, but..."
Luina was by no means a saint who forgave everything and embraced all with love.
No matter how fair the compensation was, the value of what was lost was actually priceless.
It was inevitable to feel regret for what was lost and resentment toward those who took it.
Especially since she was aware of how the nobles’ attitudes toward Berchef had changed after losing the Grand Duke position.
"...I don’t particularly dislike Fridien. But I don’t have any desire to become friends either."
"Like our relationship before?"
"..."
"There’s no problem between you two. On the contrary, there’s the shared cause of fighting against the demonic species. Is there any reason not to work together?"
Luina couldn’t readily answer.
"Wow, I see you in a new light, Senior. You’re incredibly selfish."
"So?"
"I don’t mind bad men. After all, you’re from the Grand Duke family."
From Ariadne’s perspective, there was nothing bad about this.
It was an opportunity to build a good relationship with Berchef, who resented them despite them having done nothing wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 117: Fatal Timing [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 117: Fatal Timing [2]
"But didn’t you say she was likely to become the successor to the direct line of the Grand Duke family?"
"That was a mistake. I just omitted one word at the beginning."
The word ’former’.
"Ha."
Ariadne gave a dry laugh. Luina tried to compose herself.
"...Yes, that’s precisely it. I don’t think we need to fight each other when facing a demon."
"Senior Luina is more generous than I thought. I look forward to working with you."
Luina extended her hand first. Ariadne accepted the handshake with a bright smile.
After settling their relationship, the three headed straight to the forest where the World Tree branch was planted.
"...This is the World Tree branch?"
"More precisely, it’s a contaminated branch."
"It’s truly terrible to see the Mother Tree’s incarnation in such a state. We should let her rest peacefully as soon as possible..."
The condition of the World Tree branch seemed even more serious than before. What had been dingy was now completely black, and now one could feel demonic energy when approaching.
But it didn’t spread beyond a certain range.
"What are we going to do with this?"
"We’re setting traps."
"Traps?"
"Simply contaminating the World Tree branch can’t be the final goal of those demonic creatures."
"That’s obvious, of course."
Anyone could guess that they planned to use the contaminated World Tree branch for something.
Though no one would guess it was demon summoning.
"So they will definitely return here. I’m setting traps in preparation for that."
"Not a bad idea, but I have one question."
"Speak."
"I understand the World Tree branch is quite valuable, so why wasn’t it managed before it reached this state?"
"...Please don’t bring up my dark history."
"It’s a long story, but there were circumstances."
Luina didn’t ask further.
"But if we’re setting magical traps, is there any need for me to be here?"
"Protection."
"If demonic species tainted the World Tree, we don’t know when they might return."
"It’s not the Mother Tree but a branch of the Mother Tree. It’s like the difference between a King Slime and an ordinary slime that broke off from it."
"That’s quite a big difference. I’ll correct myself."
She drew her sword and began surveying the surroundings.
"What should I do?"
"You help with guard duty too."
"Do you need me as well?"
"Want to dig instead?"
"Elven eyes are as good as slapping an eagle in the face."
Ariadne moved to the opposite side of Luina and stood guard.
’Well then...’
The traps weren’t anything special.
’First, dig the ground...’
Rumble rumble, he dug the ground with magic and drew magic circles inside. The reason for digging was to hide them from the demonic species.
’This is no time to save money.’
He enhanced the performance of the magic circles with reagents and stuffed scrolls between them for linkage. Then he buried bottles of holy water with magic circles engraved on them.
Dozens of them like that. One or two might not be enough, but he thought that dozens of bottles of holy water and linked magic might make even a demon hesitate.
’And additionally...’
Gerhard took out the final scroll.
A luxurious scroll different from the others. It contained high-level magic and was accordingly expensive.
If everything went according to plan, it would be the final blow to Andromalius, who would be weakened by the other traps and holy water.
After completing all the trap installations over a considerable time, Gerhard cleaned up the surroundings once more.
Since secrecy was the essence of traps, there couldn’t be any suspicious signs.
It was at that moment, as he was manifesting magic once more with this in mind.
—!
It began as a faint, very faint vibration.
So subtle that it would be difficult to notice if not for Gerhard, who was digging the ground as an earth mage.
"...What’s this?"
Rumble rumble, the growth of the world’s greatest tree. The blackened World Tree branch was taking deeper root, extending its stems, and growing larger.
"...The World Tree suddenly?"
"Ariadne!"
But no one saw it as a positive sign.
Because instead of the pure mana associated with the World Tree, it was spewing terrible demonic energy.
"The Mother Tree is screaming!"
Ariadne exclaimed. Her pupils shook violently as if an earthquake had occurred.
’...Wait, could it be?’
That can’t be. It can’t be.
Gerhard desperately denied the ominous feeling that suddenly intruded.
"Ariadne, what exactly is happening here!"
"That’s what I want to know!"
"...What exactly did you touch wrongly?"
"No, I didn’t touch anything!"
No one could understand why the half-dead World Tree branch was suddenly growing or why the demonic energy was intensifying.
But everyone knew it wasn’t a good sign.
Luina drew her sword, and Ariadne summoned spirits.
"I should have let her rest in peace sooner!"
Ariadne extended her staff forward. Swirling wind became blades and attacked the World Tree.
Zwooong-
"What is this!"
"A shield?"
But somehow a protective barrier made of demonic energy had formed around the World Tree. Following that, Luina unleashed a sword strike.
—!
This time it had an effect. The trees bent roughly from the shockwave, and fragments of the barrier flew in all directions.
A small crack was visible through the gap.
"That’s it, Luina! Stop it immediately!"
Gerhard cheered and prepared magic, but he couldn’t fulfill his intention.
Crack crack crack-
The branch that had extended high into the sky pierced right through space.
"...What is this."
"What exactly is happening...?"
The split crack gradually widened its area. When it became about the size of a small hole.
Crack-
A pure white hand suddenly protruded and forcibly tore the crack.
The sky splitting.
A hand suddenly protruding.
Space being torn.
None of it seemed real. But it was reality.
The crack widened, and pop, a single being emerged.
"A person?"
"No, something like that couldn’t be human..."
A form resembling a human, but with a completely inhuman, otherworldly feel.
"De-demonic energy...!"
"What on earth is that? What’s happening...!"
Chilling pupils and pressure, explosive demonic energy. And even a huge snake wrapped around the left arm.
The appearance was exactly as described in books.
"Andromalius..."
He could no longer deny reality.
"Ah, no...!"
Why now, why now of all times!
When he had come to set traps just in case!
When Aint wasn’t here!
Gerhard let out a silent scream.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Steel Savior [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 118: Steel Savior [1]
"It’s been a long time since I’ve felt the air of the middle realm."
What is this?
"How refreshing."
Is this a dream?
"But there are worms disturbing my enjoyment."
Why at this very moment?
"Nevertheless, I’m in a good mood today, so I’ll show mercy to these worms. Savor the last 5 minutes of your lives."
Has Andromalius really been summoned?
’What should I do?’
What should I do? What should I do? What should I do? What should I do? What should I do?
His mind went blank.
To think that a demon would be summoned while setting traps. He had never anticipated this possibility.
Can we win?
’But Aint isn’t here?’
The core of all of Gerhard’s plans was Aint Armian.
The natural enemy of demons, the direct descendant of the Armian family.
The hero of the prophecy book who had absorbed all the arrangements left by the first Emperor.
But he wasn’t here.
Moreover, Andromalius’s pressure far exceeded Gerhard’s imagination.
’Was the prophecy book just a fragment...?’
This Andromalius was different from the one he had seen through the prophecy book.
More chilling, more viscous, and more frightening.
His body trembled uncontrollably.
It seemed like no plan, no defense would be of any use.
"...What are you?"
At that moment, the one who broke the silence was neither Andromalius, nor Gerhard, nor Ariadne.
It was Luina Berchef.
She, who dreamed of becoming the most noble and strongest knight, stepped forward even when facing a demon.
"Are you addressing me?"
"Who else would I be talking to?"
It wasn’t that she had no fear. Her pupils and sword were trembling.
Nevertheless, their focus was clearly directed at Andromalius.
"...Yes, I suppose so."
Pfft. Andromalius snickered.
Pffft ha ha ha. The snicker soon turned into raucous laughter. Though it was merely laughter, the air resonated loudly.
"Kugh...!"
"Kyaaa...!"
Gerhard and Ariadne clutched their ears. Luina frowned but didn’t break her stance.
"Ah, forgive me. It’s been so long since I received a question from an insignificant creature that it feels fresh."
But you know.
"I have never permitted a creature to question me."
The smile on Andromalius’s face disappeared.
"You insignificant creature don’t know your place."
—!
"Kugh...!"
It was just a lightly flicked finger. It was just a single strand of demonic energy.
Nevertheless, Luina, who had blocked it, stepped back a couple of paces. Her aura cracked, and her sword trembled violently.
"Luina!"
"Senior!"
Seeing her struggle, Gerhard became aware of his own wretchedness.
’Damn it...!’
To think he was trembling and not doing anything. It was the height of shame and disgrace.
’I’m more afraid of losing money than facing a demon. I’m more afraid of dying without spending the money I’ve earned. I’m more terrified of my assets disappearing!’
What was a mere demon anyway?
Hadn’t he gone to such lengths to stop it?
He should be cautious, but there was no need to be excessively afraid.
"Ariadne, prepare for battle."
"...Yes. I can’t just sit here and wait to die. I showed you a pathetic sight."
Gerhard and Ariadne struggled to overcome their fear and raised their staffs.
As if they were of no concern to him, Andromalius muttered while clenching and opening his hands.
"Hmm, is this all? Tsk, indeed, even if I had pushed myself a bit due to being ahead of schedule. Well, still, it’s more than enough to kill these bugs."
Let’s see.
"Did they say I could run wild as I please after killing all the humans within the barrier?"
Andromalius’s gaze swept over everyone.
Two humans and one elf.
And.
"It’s you."
Not far away. One human who had been approaching, irritating his senses, and another trivial one.
"Armian."
Andromalius stretched out his blackened hand. A beam of light far thicker than what Luina had blocked was discharged in a straight line.
————!
Pure white light and black darkness collided. The shockwave spread in all directions.
The earth shook, trees broke, and dust that had been something scattered.
"...It’s Aint."
And at that sight, Gerhard’s eyes came alive.
His assumption that the demon summoning wouldn’t occur until Aint arrived hadn’t been wrong.
Then there was hope.
Then they could defeat the demon.
Because that was the original history.
Even if something had changed, they had prepared more thoroughly than in the original history.
"Luina!"
"Yes!"
"Go, go and help Aint. Andromalius’s top priority is Aint. If Aint dies, we all die!"
"But then you..."
"Quickly!"
"Understood!"
Luina sprinted.
"Ariadne, you too."
"What about you, Senior?"
"I have something to do."
"Something to do?"
"Yes. I didn’t expect to use it so soon, but..."
If you’ve set traps, you have to activate them.
***
<This is absurd...!>
Summoning demons from hell to the middle realm was by no means an easy task.
To pierce the dimensional barrier required a corresponding price. Massive mana, or life force.
And gathering those would naturally leave traces. But there were no signs anywhere that might indicate a demon summoning.
Or maybe they just didn’t know.
<How was something so important managed in a way that it became a medium for demon summoning!>
<There must have been signs!>
Regardless of Gardner’s outrage, the situation was unfolding.
"Wait, wait... Aint...!"
The moment he saw the demon, Aint advanced, suppressing his fear and terror.
It was instinct. The demon aversion possessed by the natural enemy of demons.
The light energy possessed by Armian extremely cursed and raged against the demonic energy.
Led by that, Aint swung his sword.
————!
A collision with the flashing demonic energy.
Aint rolled on the ground once from the massive rebound. The shock penetrating beyond the sword made his entire body creak.
It was stronger than any enemy he had met and fought so far.
The demonic species he had fought just a short while ago was incomparable.
"Cursed bloodline."
Despite the considerable distance, his eyes met the demon’s. He got chills from those abyssal pupils. His skin trembled.
"How insignificant."
The low voice distinctly struck his eardrums.
’Can I win? Really? This is incomparable to that demonic creature?’
The difference in power, realized from just one collision, made him face reality.
His entire body trembled like an aspen tree.
<Stay calm, Aint!>
At that moment, Aint’s sword began to emit light.
<Though this is completely unexpected, that doesn’t mean you must lose!>
The light pushed back the darkness, slowly erasing the pressure exerted on Aint.
<You are an Armian. A being feared by demons.>
<It is not you who should be trembling in fear, but that creature!>
A warm energy enveloped Aint. His ragged breathing stabilized.
"...Can I win this?"
<It’s not a question of whether you can win or not.>
<You must win.>

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Steel Savior [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 119: Steel Savior [2]
If he didn’t win, there would be no future. For the peace of the continent, and even to survive, Aint had to behead the demon and emerge alive.
<Have you forgotten your resolve from last time?>
<You’ve always fought against enemies stronger than you. Yet, you’re the one who’s still alive!>
<I’ll help you. Behead that disgusting demon and show the world that Armian is still strong!>
Grip! Aint’s hand holding the sword tightened.
Gardner was right. This wasn’t a question of whether he could win or not. It was a battle he had to win.
There was no hope in running away.
"Unpleasant, utterly unpleasant."
The demonic energy intensified. In response, Aint also activated his aura. Brilliant light opposed the darkness.
"Indeed, the Armian folk have no reason to exist in this world."
It was at that moment.
—!
——!
—!
As magic circles activated, a massive whirlpool of mana surged. Bright light beams flashed like fireworks.
They were over dozens of magic spells.
Lightning struck, flames flickered, and spears of ice and earth were shot.
They all pounced on Andromalius at once.
"Pathetic."
None of them seemed to reach Andromalius.
Or so they thought.
"...Kugh?"
Andromalius let out a short scream. Hissss, acrid smoke was rising from his entire body.
<What is that? Is it decomposing the demonic energy?>
Something hidden within the magic was decomposing the demonic energy, breaking through and effectively striking Andromalius.
"...Who on earth?"
"Aint!"
At that moment, a call for him was heard.
"Senior Luina? Ariadne?"
"Aint."
"Hello, Aint! Veriana is here too?"
"Why are you here? What’s happening...!"
"It’s a long story. We don’t have the luxury of time now."
Luina stood beside Aint. Ariadne held her staff behind them.
"For now, that demon, Andromalius, is the priority."
"...That’s true."
<Not bad. With these people, especially Luina Berchef, they will be considerable help!>
Aint felt his heart ease. It was the difference between shouldering everything alone and having companions.
"Let’s attack first before he regains his senses."
"But what was that? Did you do it, Senior?"
"It was Gerhard."
"...Is Senior Gerhard here too?"
Now that he thought about it. Aint belatedly realized that Veriana had come to see Gerhard.
"This damned creature...!"
But the conversation couldn’t continue any longer. The enraged Andromalius began to move.
Boom! The wall of rock that had risen collapsed in an instant. No one was unaware of what this phenomenon meant.
"Senior Gerhard is in danger!"
<Go save your patron immediately!>
The aura activates. It boasts an even more brilliant presence along the first Emperor’s sword.
Aint became a flash of light and charged. Like a galloping horse, he compressed the distance in an instant.
There was no room to gauge this or that.
Full power from the start.
However they did it, the vulnerabilities exposed thanks to Gerhard were a good opportunity.
——!
Sword and hand collide.
The shockwave spread. Shattered demonic energy and light aura scatter in all directions.
It was much more manageable than the initial collision. Whether the reason was Gardner’s help or Gerhard’s help didn’t matter.
Aint’s sword strike falls upon Andromalius.
—!
Andromalius’s body is slammed into the ground. The earth shakes, and fragments of rock bounce up.
Aint, who has twisted his body in mid-air, draws his sword in the air.
The concentrated beam of light becomes a flash and falls vertically.
—!
A massive explosion occurs. Aint, who has closely followed, swings his sword repeatedly.
"No matter when I feel it, it’s always unpleasantly repulsive...!"
But Andromalius remained intact. With an angry roar, his entire body is stained black.
—!
Aint’s body is thrown back even faster than when he was descending.
Andromalius follows closely.
Even as he couldn’t properly control his body due to the shock, Aint raised his sword. Fists pour down like a waterfall.
"That sword. That damned sword! It’s that chilling and disgusting sword from back then! Garbage that should disappear from this world!"
The sacred nature of the sword was eating away at the demonic energy, and it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that Aint was enduring thanks to it.
But even that had its limits.
A streak of blood flowed from the corner of his mouth due to his battered internal organs.
At that moment.
—!
Another sword intervened. It ambushes the demon, who was focusing all his attention on Aint.
Andromalius screams. Black blood stained the tip of the sword that pierced his weakened back.
"You worm of a woman...!"
"Foul-mouthed, as a demon should be."
The owner of the sword, Luina, catches her breath.
Swish, as the wind of the hiding elf pounces on the demon, it hits the ground.
Clang, sword and hand collide.
Slash, the sword flows along the arm and cuts the demon’s chest.
Or rather, it seemed to cut.
—!
A small shadow that popped out blocked Luina’s sword.
It was a snake.
The black snake that Andromalius had wrapped around his right hand.
"Fine. I acknowledge that I’ve underestimated you too much."
A chilling bloodlust weighs down heavily.
"To think I have to give my best against worms. Such humiliation wouldn’t have occurred in hell...!"
Crunch, Andromalius’s face distorted fiercely.
"Rejoice. I’ll make sure you’re not really dead even after you die..."
The storm poured down like blades. Another knight, who had been terrified, pushed away his fear and delivered a sword strike.
"You worms dare to interrupt my words...!"
Veriana screamed and was thrown back.
"Well done! Ariadne, Veriana!"
Following that, the two knights struck successively.
Sword and hand collide, sword and snake collide.
Darkness and light, demonic energy and aura express their presence while eating away at each other.
The coordination between Aint and Luina was like comrades who had entrusted their backs to each other for a long time.
They filled each other’s gaps and struck at the demon’s vulnerabilities.
The winds that flew appropriately added vigor to them.
Nevertheless, Andromalius was not easy to deal with.
"How dare...!"
He opens his mouth and spews demonic energy.
Extremely compressed demonic energy directly hits Aint. Though he blocked it, he couldn’t withstand the shock and stepped back.
The snake follows, blocking Aint’s movement.
Luina, who was targeting the demon’s back, is astonished by the grotesquely twisted body that avoids her sword.
Crunch, enduring the rupturing of muscles, she forcibly changes course and penetrates the side.
"You damned woman!"
Clang-
But immediately after, a heavy fist breaks through the aura and dents the armor. Luina’s body flies far away.
"Pathetic."
The wind tries to restrain the demon, but dozens of demonic energies pour down like fireballs with a lightly flicked finger.
Along with an explosion, Ariadne’s scream was heard.
"Cursed bloodline of Armian. Now there’s no one to help you."
The snake returns to Andromalius’s right arm. Instead, a spear of demonic energy pounces on Aint.
Amidst this, once again, a fist falls.
"I’ve been waiting for this moment for a long time."
In the face of overwhelming power and demonic energy, the aura was gradually losing its light.
"The moment of wiping out the seed of that cursed one."
The aura is crushed, and the armor is smashed.
"He will spit blood in the afterlife. After a thousand years, we will ultimately be the victors."
"...I won’t let that happen!"
"You won’t let that happen?"
Bang!
Aint’s body staggered.
"Do you think you can defeat me relying on that meager sword?"
Bang!
A thick foot trampled on the fallen Aint.
"Yes, perhaps, as he said, if I had delayed more, I might not have been able to defeat you in this state."
But everything is retrospective.
"From now on, I’ll wipe out everything bearing the name Armian..."
——!
Andromalius was thrown back.
"...Quite persistent."
After rolling on the ground once, he straightened his posture.
"I highly commend your spirit. That you can still have such a look in your eyes when facing me."
He expressed admiration for the eyes that didn’t die even though they were wearing broken armor and bleeding all over.
"Aint Armian."
It was Luina.
With a pale complexion, she blocked Aint’s view.
"I’ll somehow draw his attention. You watch for an opportunity and stab his heart."
The demon is strong. But if asked whether it’s absolutely unbeatable, the answer was no.
"My sword was effective."
Her sword had wounded Andromalius. Twice, in fact.
"Then your sword would be even more fatal."
Since the Armian sword is the natural enemy of demons.
"So I’ll pull him in. Aim for the vulnerable spot, aim for the vital point."
It was the only way to victory, and Aint was more suitable for that role than Luina.
"I should..."
Aint’s eyes wavered.
Luina’s condition was abnormal to anyone’s eyes. Drawing attention in this situation was no different from sacrificing one’s life.
"Set aside personal feelings. As things stand, we’ll all die."
Either they defeat the demon, or they fall. It was one or the other.
"And I am a knight. Though I don’t have a lord to serve at the moment."
This empire, this world could be considered her lord.
A knight.
"Does not flee, leaving the lord behind."
Does not overlook the empire being destroyed by a demon.
A knight.
"Does not die after the lord."
There’s no meaning in living if the empire collapses. So they do their utmost to prevent it.
That is.
"My chivalry."
And this method is the only way to protect the empire.
Luina’s hand holding the sword tightened.
"Remember, Aint."
There’s only one chance.
Luina was about to charge towards the demon, Andromalius...
"No."
Someone abruptly blocked Luina’s view.
"I can’t allow you to go, Luina."
By whose decision.
"...Gerhard?"
Gerhard’s eyes were wild.
"After all I’ve done to get here."
After all the effort I’ve made to stop that damned creature. After all the money I’ve spent.
Do you think I’d let the future unfold exactly as the prophecy book showed?
"Watch, Luina."
Crack crack crack-
Space split open.
"This is."
A giant hand popped out.
"Something that has never existed before and will never exist again."
Following that, shoulders, torso, and legs revealed themselves to the world.
"An ego golem."
A giant steel giant carrying its master on its shoulder entered the battlefield.
Gwoooooo-
The golem roared.

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Victory’s Price [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 120: Victory’s Price [1]
It was.
Something enormous.
It was.
A knight of solid steel.
A black knight, painted black, evoking even more intimidation.
Woooong-
A red light flickered through the giant helmet.
<What is that? A golem?>
"...What is this."
"A golem...?"
"...What is that thing."
Aint and Luina, along with Veriana who was sprawled in a corner of the blood-soaked battlefield, gaped in stunned silence at the magnificent appearance of the golem. Their eyes widened with a mixture of awe and disbelief as they beheld the colossal figure dominating the landscape before them.
It wasn’t their first time seeing a golem—those magical constructs of metal and enchantment were familiar enough—but it was their first time witnessing a giant golem of such impossible scale, nearly 10 meters tall, its polished steel surface gleaming ominously under the waning light. The sheer size of the creation defied conventional understanding of what mortal hands could craft.
"This is what it’s like to see from above."
Gerhard took a deep breath.
Everything below looked as small as toys.
Aint, Luina.
"Insignificant toys."
And even Andromalius.
"Do you think you can defeat me by creating such a thing?"
"Nothing is impossible."
Of course, it wouldn’t be easy—he harbored no delusions about the challenge ahead. The demon was ancient and powerful, steeped in malevolence older than human civilization. But if there was absolutely no possibility of victory, Gerhard wouldn’t have invested so much effort, time, and precious resources in creating this masterpiece of magical engineering. Every enchanted joint, every spelled plate of armor had been meticulously crafted for this moment.
"Now, Wooden."
Gerhard stroked the golem.
"Show your power to that garbage demon."
That was the signal.
The golem’s red eyes grew even more intense. The massive body began to move.
Slowly, very slowly, befitting its enormous size.
That’s what he thought at first.
But the golem’s great sword was already in front of Andromalius’s nose.
"...!"
Claaaang!
But the great sword failed to achieve its purpose. Somehow, something enormous had positioned itself between the golem and Andromalius.
Hisssss-
A snake flickering its tongue. The snake that had been wrapped around Andromalius’s right arm had stretched to nearly 30 meters, transforming into a gigantic monster.
"I leave this to you. Crush it."
Hissssss!
At Andromalius’s command, the snake sprang like a coil.
"It’s coming, Wooden!"
The golem took its stance. It slightly bent its knees and extended its sword.
Swooosh-
The snake’s head changed direction in mid-air. The sword strike barely missed in the air.
No, it seemed to miss, but the sword changed its trajectory and chased after the snake.
Booom, there was an explosion despite the sword and scales colliding. The snake’s massive body was thrown far away.
"...Was it possible for a golem to move like that?"
"It’s incredibly fast...!"
The two knights were astonished. Though they didn’t know much about golems, they knew that none of the golems they had seen so far could do such a thing.
"...Not completely worthless after all."
Even Andromalius seemed surprised as his eyes widened slightly.
"Of course, do you know how much I’ve poured into this?"
Money equals combat power.
At least in the golem academic world, this was an absolutely valid statement.
The golem that had thrown away the snake didn’t stop. It narrowed the distance in an instant and swung down its sword as if to split the world.
Just before the sword touched Andromalius, the ground sank deeply.
They fell vertically to tens of meters below ground.
———!
Immediately after, like a meteorite falling, a massive impact struck the earth.
The golem’s sword couldn’t cut Andromalius in one go. He blocked it by crossing his blackened arms.
But the scattered fragments of demonic energy, the flowing blood, and the shaking pupils proved that it was quite an effective hit.
It’s working. Indeed, money doesn’t lie.
Gerhard’s face was filled with ecstasy.
"...How dare you! A lowly human mocking me!"
And seeing this, Andromalius raged.
Demonic energy extending from his entire body wriggled like snakes and pounced on the golem.
Though the golem swung its sword to cut off some, it couldn’t block all of them, nearly hundreds.
But there was no need to do so from the beginning.
——!
The golem’s body emitted a soft light, forming a translucent barrier.
"Pathetic tricks!"
But the real attack was the fist that followed.
A gigantic force with densely packed demonic energy.
Claaaang!
The barrier shattered into pieces, belying its impressive appearance.
Nevertheless, the force wasn’t completely dissipated and struck the golem’s chest.
The golem’s breastplate dented. The massive body, pushed by the force, was thrown out of the pit.
Tap, Andromalius exhaled roughly and came up.
"...To dare to wound me."
Crunch, Andromalius roughly swept back his hair with one hand.
The reason for using only one hand was that the other was half-broken and dangling.
"None of you will die peacefully."
"There’s a famous saying in the upper world. Those who only talk big are usually one of two things."
The golem took its stance again. The dented breastplate had somehow been restored to its original state.
"Either an idiot or a fraud. Which one are you?"
"Malius!"
Andromalius shouted.
"How long must I listen to the nonsense of these bugs?"
At that moment, a massive body pounced on the golem.
It was so fast and large that it couldn’t be avoided.
Therefore, the golem didn’t avoid it.
Gerhard raised the earth to create a barrier, and in the momentary gap created by that barrier sacrificing itself.
The golem, activating its heart’s power even more and draining its master’s mana, overlaid aura on its sword.
The golem’s two legs dug into the earth.
And.
————!
An emerald-colored slash cut the snake in half.
***
"...Good heavens."
"...What am I seeing right now?"
<Is that a golem?>
Aint stared blankly at the golem.
It was his first time seeing a 10-meter golem, and despite witnessing it with his own eyes, he couldn’t believe the golem’s performance.
To consistently push back a demon that had seemed impossible to defeat.
To cut that giant snake in half.
<How much has golem technology developed during the thousand years I was asleep?>
<At this level, they might easily handle demons just by making golems, without needing the arrangements of the first Emperor.>
"...No, not all golems are like that..."

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Victory’s Price [2]
chapters.content:
Chapter 121: Victory’s Price [2]
If they were, this world would have become a battleground of golems against golems, not humans against humans or humans against monsters.
"...As expected of Gerhard."
Luina was no different from Aint.
No, the shock was even greater for her, who had been prepared to sacrifice her life.
"...We can win."
Not a slim gamble that risked life, but hope for a certain victory.
"Gerhard!"
She called his name without realizing it. And Gerhard responded.
"You don’t have to shout so loudly, I can hear everything."
Gerhard’s appearance wasn’t in the best condition, but his eyes were still alive. He threw potions to Luina and Aint.
"Luina, Aint. I’ll leave the rest to you."
"What do you mean?"
"Huh? Why suddenly?"
"Wooden can no longer fight."
Flash-
A blue light enveloped the golem. When they opened their eyes after closing them due to the brightness, the golem had disappeared without a trace.
"It used up all the core’s magic power for that last attack."
It would be impossible to operate for a while.
"The same goes for me."
And the same applied to Gerhard. After all, he had put even his own mana into the core to deliver the maximum blow.
His completely drained mana heart was throbbing painfully.
"But..."
<No, you can do it. Your patron has done more than enough.>
Look at his condition. Gardner whispered.
<His arm is broken.>
Though it was slowly regenerating, it was still a serious injury for now.
<Above all, that cursed reptile is gone!>
The joint attacks of Aint and Luina were certainly organic and could sufficiently wound Andromalius.
Yet, they couldn’t seize a decisive opportunity because there were two opponents.
The black snake whose scales couldn’t even be damaged by ordinary aura.
They couldn’t find a way by just attacking recklessly, and Luina had wanted to gamble with her own life.
Though it had been disrupted when Gerhard suddenly intervened.
Anyway, the situation had improved.
"Yes, understood."
Luina downed the potion in one go.
"You wouldn’t ask for the impossible. I’ll trust you."
Over the past semester, an indescribable trust had built up between Luina and Gerhard.
Some might say it was Luina’s one-sided trust... but at least she believed that if Gerhard said something was possible, then it was.
"Aint."
With her firm gaze, Aint’s expression also changed.
"Yes, Senior."
"Can you stand?"
"Of course."
Aint swallowed the potion and gripped his sword. There wasn’t a place that didn’t ache. There were more than a few places where his bones had cracked.
Nevertheless, he had to fight. Because lives, the continent depended on it.
And because this was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for victory.
The two knights began to move again.
***
"...Malius?"
Among those on the battlefield, the one most shocked by the snake’s death was neither Aint nor Luina.
It was Andromalius. The master of the now-dead snake.
"...This is absurd! To a mere toy like that...!"
The black snake, Malius, was not just a snake. It was both his avatar and a part of him.
Malius’s death wasn’t simply the death of something separate, but the disappearance of a part of Andromalius.
"...!"
But there was no time to mourn, as the situation wasn’t over yet.
The demon could neither endure nor acknowledge the current humiliation.
"...Fine, I’ll kill you all. Every last one of you!"
He faced the two knights who were bringing forth their blades with an even more ferocious momentum.
The demon clenched his fist. Aint and Luina lowered their stance.
Immediately after, the knights kicked off the ground.
A pure white light and a blue radiance drew long trajectories, targeting one goal from different directions.
Black demonic energy greeted them.
Booooom!
Dust rose as various scars were carved.
Shattered fragments scattered in all directions, and the shockwave swept around.
The demon’s demonic energy surged. Wriggling like a living snake, it stabbed at the knights’ gaps.
However, the knights were not alone. They covered each other’s gaps as their swords intersected.
It was the most beautiful dance.
A sacred dance that trapped and slaughtered the demon.
—!
Gradually, the wounds on the demon’s body increased. The tough outer shell was not as it used to be, and the broken hand created an unavoidable weakness.
—!
The power of the natural enemy raged like a fish in water, eating away at the demon’s energy.
"You Armian seed, not even worth eating...!"
The more brilliant the light, the more the darkness lost its intensity.
The more the sword light scattered, the more the form of the demonic energy disappeared.
Nevertheless, the demon didn’t fall.
"Do you think I’ll lose?!"
The spilled blood became poison, and the fragmented demonic energy obeyed its master’s command even in that state.
"I am Andromalius! Count of Hell and Commander of 11 Legions of Hell!"
He roared, standing on two feet and facing the humans.
"I am the vanguard of Hell, come to conquer the middle realm!"
The demonic energy boiled. More violently, more ferociously, more savagely.
"So what?"
But what stood before him weren’t insignificant humans.
"Then I am the Armian that you all hate so much."
The natural enemy of demons.
"I am the successor of the first Emperor, whose name alone makes your kind tremble!"
The adversary of Hell.
<Go, Aint! That’s nothing but a last desperate struggle!>
The cause that thwarted the wishes of all demons.
The first Emperor’s sword shone brilliantly.
The white light, which had destroyed and consumed demonic energy to grow, expanded incomparably.
————!
Light and darkness intersected.
"Ah."
Andromalius touched his chest.
Blood gushed from his chest, which had split open a moment later.
Crack, and then another sword pierced his heart.
"I-I...!"
The demon’s eyes rapidly lost their vitality.
"Don’t think... I’m the last...! This is just the beginning...! Eventually, the middle realm will be ours...!"
<Typical third-rate villain dialogue.>
That was the end.
Andromalius, having lost his vitality, collapsed.
Immediately after, the corpse turned to dust and scattered.
"...This."
<Demons are not beings of the middle realm. Therefore, they aren’t even allowed to leave behind corpses.>
Thus, the demon died.
It was a miraculous achievement from a desperate situation.
But it wasn’t a satisfactory ending for everyone.
"...This is ridiculous. The body just disappears? I broke my back stopping it, and I get nothing?"
A certain merchant who had hoped to use the snake’s corpse to create various things was in despair.

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Spirit Contract [1]
chapters.content:
Chapter 122: Spirit Contract [1]
Gerhard knew that demons were beings not even allowed to leave their corpses in the middle realm.
Through a method he never wanted to know.
"..."
How much could he get from dismantling that giant snake’s corpse?
Though the black scales were somewhat ominous, they were so solid that they couldn’t even be scratched without the aura that Aint and Luina had carefully forged.
The golden eyes that had gleamed and the blood would probably sell at a high price as magical materials that wizards would go crazy over.
The sharpness of the teeth was at a level where even decent swords couldn’t compare, and the hardness of the bones would certainly be material for excellent armor.
Not only that, but the flesh permeated with demonic energy could somehow be purified and sold as medicine.
If marketed as a snake soup made from a demon’s familiar, anyone would go wild for it.
But the crown jewel would have been the heart.
Since all the enormous strength and vast demonic energy possessed by that snake originated from the heart, the heart could have been the ultimate elixir comparable to a dragon’s heart, or a power source.
’If I had somehow purified that and enhanced Wooden’s core?’
It wouldn’t have been easy, but Wooden might have advanced to another level.
A corpse from which one could suck the marrow.
But those dreams, that money, had vanished in an instant.
After all that hard work, he gained nothing.
"Aah..."
Gerhard, whose legs had given out, unconsciously sat down.
"We won! We really won! We actually won!"
Aint’s cheer came from far away.
"We defeated a demon!"
Luina’s excited voice was heard right in front of him.
"It’s thanks to you, Gerhard! Without that golem of yours, it would have been impossible...?"
Achievement, relief, excitement, jubilation, emotion, joy, happiness.
Various emotions were complexly expressed on her flushed face.
"Are you crying?"
"I’m not crying."
"Are you badly injured somewhere? I don’t see any wounds on the outside..."
"...You know nothing, Luina."
"What does that suddenly mean?"
Gerhard didn’t bother to explain. Even if he did, there was no way Luina would understand.
"Senior!"
A swift shadow tightly grabbed his hand. It was Aint.
"We won! It’s all thanks to you, Senior!"
"It’s not because of me, but because of you. You’re the one who beheaded the demon."
"No! Without your golem, we could never have pushed the demon to the end!"
"Yes, I get it, now let go of my hand."
And don’t press your face so close to mine.
"What exactly happened to the demon?"
"It died. Since demons are not beings of the middle realm, their corpses turned to dust and disappeared."
However, not everything was gone.
Others didn’t see it, but part of the demon was absorbed into Aint’s sword.
<It’s one of the abilities residing in the sword. It absorbs some of the demon’s power and strengthens its owner.>
A warrior who becomes stronger with each demon he slays. That was the first Emperor.
<Don’t tell anyone. Since you never know when it might leak out, it’s good to keep some part of your power hidden from anyone.>
Gardner explained that it’s a knight’s virtue to hide 10% of their power, even from close companions.
"And the barrier is gradually being lifted."
"Barrier?"
"Yes. The moment the demon was summoned, a barrier isolated the surroundings from the outside."
That explains it. He thought it was strange that no one came despite the commotion.
’Was it like this in the original future too?’
Perhaps Andromalius had set up the barrier after Aint and Luina arrived.
"Then the real thing starts now."
With such a commotion, the Academy would now learn about demons.
There would be a major disturbance, and a lot of investigations would be poured on the five people at the scene, including Gerhard, Luina, and Aint.
"Then just talk about this incident. Don’t mention that you knew about the demonic species from before."
"Yes."
"I know."
Knowing about the demonic species beforehand wouldn’t work in their favor, no matter what excuse they gave.
They coordinated on a few other points as well. Fortunately, both of them readily followed Gerhard’s opinion.
What was somewhat unexpected was that while some trust had built up with Luina, he hadn’t expected Aint to agree so readily.
’It seems our relationship has deepened a bit more after catching this demon.’
Not bad.
"By the way, I’ve been wanting to ask, what is that?"
As the conversation was wrapping up, Luina’s finger was pointing at Gerhard’s shoulder.
On his shoulder, something small, about 10cm, was wriggling.
"It’s Wooden."
A black knight the size of a small doll.
"Wooden?"
"That... this form? Really?"
"Yes, this is the giant golem you were so grateful for."
<Gring?>
Wooden tilted his tiny head and waved his hand.
"...Is it possible for a giant golem to shrink like that?"
"...It’s not linked right now, is it, Senior?"
"I told you. It’s an ego golem."
"Ego? It really has its own consciousness?"
"Of course. Wooden, hand."
<Gring!>
Wooden extended his small hand forward. At this sight, Luina and Aint were astonished once again.
"...I’ve never seen a golem like this."
"Because it’s a masterpiece that didn’t exist before and won’t exist in the future."
"No, really? Aren’t you secretly linking it and doing this on your own, Senior?"
"That’s not the case, Aint."
The answer came from somewhere completely different.
"Please give me a potion too, Senior. I feel like I’m dying."
It was Ariadne, with a small hole in her side.
"Where were you resting that you show up when it’s all over?"
"I was fighting hard and fainted, how can you say I was resting!"
Gerhard threw her a potion.
"Ariadne, you say that’s not the case? Do you know about this golem?"
"Of course. I put the ego in it."
"You put it in?"
"Yes."
Ariadne nodded.
"It’s a spirit."
==
The time rewinds to a while ago.
